line: I doubt that.

line: My point is, it's a matter of interpretation. It may not be what you believe, but that doesn't make it wrong. If you start to think that way, you'll be acting just like Vedek Winn, Only from the other side. We can't afford to think that way, Jake. We'd lose everything we've worked for here

line: I began my service at the monastery as the gardener. I had no other ambition but to grow the most lovely Feloran bromeliads on the planet. Unfortunately, the Prophets did not allow me that peaceful life. I understand my friend Vedek Winn has brought her blessings to your station.

line: I'm Benjamin Sisko, commander of Deep Space Nine. My chief of operations, Miles O'Brien. Do any of you need medical assistance?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I think we're all fine, considering. I'm Professor Natima Lang. These are two of my students, Rekelen and Hogue.

line: What happened to your ship?

line: We were caught in a meteor swarm. I'm a decent teacher, but I'm afraid I'm not much of a shuttle pilot. Do you think you'll be able to repair our ship?

line: I'll have to take a look. Excuse me.

line: We'd like to be on our way as soon as possible. We know having Cardassians on a Bajoran station may cause trouble. That's the last thing we want.

title: Profit and Loss
line: If anyone can fix your ship, it is Mister O'Brien. In the meantime, you're welcome to stay here. If you stick to the Promenade, I'm sure there won't be any trouble.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Wait, wait, wait a second. Are you telling me you agreed with General Yiri's decision to execute his brother?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Of course I agreed. Yiri's brother was a traitor to the Trelonian government.

title: Profit and Loss
line: The evidence is all circumstantial.

title: Profit and Loss
line: It all comes down to a question of loyalty. My dear Doctor, Yiri had to choose between protecting his brother and protecting the state. He chose the state, as would I, every time.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I suppose that's one way of looking at it. But then again, before you can be loyal to another, you must be loyal to yourself.

title: Profit and Loss
line: And who can we thank for those misguided words of wisdom? Sarek of Vulcan?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Actually, it was Bashir of Earth.

title: Profit and Loss
line: With sentiments like those, you wouldn't last for five seconds on Cardassia.

line: Would you?

line: Well, assuming you're not a spy

line: Assuming.

line: I heard an interesting rumor today.

line: I didn't expect you to admit it. I'm simply serving notice. You try to sell it and I'll see to it that you spend the next fifty years digging trenches in a penal colony.

line: All right? This is the happiest day of my life.

line: Natima, wait. At least let me buy you and your friends a drink. I can make you a Samarian Sunset.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I don't drink Samarian Sunsets anymore.

line: Why not?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Because they remind me of you.

line: Is this Ferengi bothering you?

line: This Ferengi happens to be Natima's old and cherished friend. Who are you?

title: Profit and Loss
line: These are my students.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Students. You don't say. I'd love to sit in on one of your classes. What do you teach?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Her teachings will change the future of Cardassia.

line: That's enough, Rekelen.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Not at all. I want to hear more. I always knew Natima was destined for greatness.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Quark.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Just one drink. It'll be like old times.

title: Profit and Loss
line: It'll never be like old times.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You're right. It'll be better. I'll be right back with refreshments.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Your hands are shaking. So, how well does this woman know you? Just enough to dislike you, or well enough to really hate you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: She used to work here on the station. She was a correspondent for the Cardassian information service. It was before your time.

title: Profit and Loss
line: So which is it, dislike or hate?

title: Profit and Loss
line: It's none of your business, but if you have to know, I was the love of her life.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Must have been some life.

title: Profit and Loss
line: What about our drinks?

title: Profit and Loss
line: If you want a drink, the bar's right over there.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Go ahead.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Your Samarian Sunset.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I said I didn't drink these anymore.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Because they remind you of me. But since I'm here anyway, you may as well enjoy yourself. Besides, it's on the house. You know, you're as beautiful as ever.

title: Profit and Loss
line: And you're as big a liar as ever.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You see, just like old times. I've missed you, Natima. That's no lie.

line: You seem to have kept busy.

title: Profit and Loss

line: Please. I haven't heard a Rule of Acquisition in seven years and I don't want to hear one now.

title: Profit and Loss
line: So, how long are you going to be on the station?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Thank you for another enjoyable lunch. Doctor.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I didn't think there'd be any Cardassians left on the station.

title: Profit and Loss

title: Profit and Loss
line: What do we do now?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Is something wrong?

title: Profit and Loss
line: We have to leave as soon as possible. Goodbye, Quark. Thanks for the drink.

title: Profit and Loss
line: But you didn't touch it.

title: Profit and Loss
line: How are your repairs coming?

title: Profit and Loss
line: The damage is more extensive than I thought. They were lucky to escape the attack.

title: Profit and Loss
line: The attack?

title: Profit and Loss
line: They weren't in any meteor swarm. They were hit by Cardassian disrupters.

title: Profit and Loss
line: That doesn't make sense. Why would Cardassians fire on other Cardassians?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Maybe you should ask her.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Commander, I hate to be an imposition, but I need my ship.

title: Profit and Loss
line: That's not possible. Mister O'Brien is still working on it. Your ship sustained more damage than we originally thought. In fact

title: Profit and Loss
line: You suspect that our ship was damaged by Cardassian weapons. You're right, of course.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Professor.

title: Profit and Loss
line: It's all right, Hogue. I should've told them the truth in the first place.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Then why didn't you?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Because Cardassians don't involve outsiders in their internal politics. Especially Bajorans.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Being shot at by your own people goes a little beyond politics.

title: Profit and Loss
line: We take our politics very seriously. Commander, if I don't get my students to safety they're going to be killed. And if they die, the future of Cardassia may die with them.

title: Profit and Loss
line: There are some who believe the future of Cardassia should not remain in the hands of the military.

title: Profit and Loss
line: And you're among them?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Yes, we are.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Rekelen and Hogue are two of the most important leaders of our movement.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Which makes you fugitives.

title: Profit and Loss
line: The military's afraid to let us speak our minds.

title: Profit and Loss
line: They've already tried to kill us once. They're sure to try again.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Which is why I have to get them off this station as soon as possible.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'll dispatch additional work crews to help repair your ship.

title: Profit and Loss
line: We saw another Cardassian aboard the station in the bar.

line: Garak. He saw you?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'm certain of it.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Well then, we may have a problem. Mister Garak is a bit of a mystery to us. I'll assign you some guest quarters. You'll be safe there until your ship is ready.

title: Profit and Loss
line: We appreciate your assistance, Commander.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Ah, Mister Quark, this is a surprise. I don't believe you've ever been in my establishment before.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You usually don't frequent mine, either. Though I did see you in there today.

title: Profit and Loss
line: The Replimat was a little crowded. So what brings you here now?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Oh, I just wanted to see what you're offering. What do you get for that?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Seventeen strips of latinum.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I tell you what, I'll give you twenty.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Twenty? How uncharacteristically generous for a Ferengi.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Just one businessman trying to help out another. I figure we have to stick together.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Well, this is the latest style on my homeworld. Do you like it?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'm no expert on Cardassian fashions. What do you think?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I don't know. It's been so long since I've had a Cardassian customer.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Then you're in luck. There're some board on the station right now.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Now that you mention it, I think your lady friend may find this style very appealing. You're old friends, aren't you?

title: Profit and Loss
line: You're very perceptive, for a Cardassian.

title: Profit and Loss
line: It would have been hard to miss the way you were looking at her.

title: Profit and Loss
line: It would've been hard to miss the way you were looking at her.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Personally, I find this style a bit too radical, but your friend seems the sort who appreciates that kind of thing.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Different tastes for different people. Nothing wrong with that, is there?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Oh, you'd be surprised how detrimental a poor choice of fashion can be. Take this dress. It may be all the rage now but in a very short time it can become tiresome, an affront to the eyes. Certain people might even think it's objectionable. And then Nothing but rags.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I see.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Mister Quark, might I offer you some free advice?

title: Profit and Loss
line: As long as I'm under no obligation to follow it.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I've been in this business a long time and I know there's nothing worse than following the wrong trend. Now you're a smart fellow, with your own inimitable sense of style. Perhaps you should mention this to your lady friend. I'd hate to see her fall victim to fashion.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Would you like to explain that?

title: Profit and Loss
line: She's chosen to associate herself with some rather flamboyant companions. It would be a tragedy if she got in the way when her friends go out of fashion.

title: Profit and Loss
line: If anyone tries to harm her, they're going to have to deal with me.

title: Profit and Loss
line: What're you going to do, short change them at the dabo table?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I think I'll buy this dress after all. See that it's mended.

title: Profit and Loss
line: What is it you want from me?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I know you're in trouble. I want to help you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I don't want your help.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I owe you. You saved my life. If you'd turned me over to the authorities, I would have been executed.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I admired your courage. It was a brave thing you were doing selling food to the Bajorans. I thought you were a man of honor.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'm a Ferengi. You should've known better.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You're right. I should have. Instead

title: Profit and Loss
line: Can't you even say it?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I can't even think it.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Okay, I'll say it for you. We fell in love. And that month we spent together was the best time of our lives and you know it.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I think you're confusing lust with love.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I admit I'm capable of that, but not this time. I loved you, Natima.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Then how could you have betrayed me?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I didn't betray you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Don't lie to me, Quark. I know better. You used my personal access codes to authorize payments for goods you never provided.

title: Profit and Loss
line: So I took a little money from the Cardassian Communication Service. They could afford it.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You stole that money.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I saw a chance for profit and I took it. Maybe that was wrong. I don't know. But what I really regret is betraying your trust. That was the worst mistake of my life.

title: Profit and Loss
line: And you'd do it again in a second. I believed in you, Quark. But you were using me like you use everyone. For profit.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Then let me make it up to you. Let me help you. I ask for nothing in return.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Nothing?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Except that you stay with me forever.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I can't stay here. My students need me.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Listen to me, Natima. You can't leave me. Not now. If you don't stay with me, I'll have to follow you. And I will, wherever you go, until you agree to take me back.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You don't even know me anymore. I'm part of the Cardassian underground. Following me will only get you killed.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'll take that chance.

title: Profit and Loss
line: What about the bar?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I don't care about the bar. I'll turn it over to Rom. He'll run it into the ground in a month, but it doesn't matter. I have to be with you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: It won't work, Quark. You say you'd do anything for me. Maybe right now, you even believe it. But I know better. In the end, you'd only care about yourself.

title: Profit and Loss
line: But I love you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I don't love you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Now which one of us is lying?

title: Profit and Loss
line: You'd better go.

title: Profit and Loss
line: All right. But if there's anything you need, anything at all, I'll be waiting.

title: Profit and Loss
line: It'll be a long wait.

line: Professor Lang's ship should be ready to go in about an hour, Commander.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Good, I'll let her know.

line: We have a Cardassian warship approaching fast.

line: They're taking up an attack posture.

title: Profit and Loss
line: They're ignoring us.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Shields!

line: Shields up.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Commander. We think we should talk.

title: Profit and Loss
line: All right, Garak, do you mind telling me why a Cardassian warship is threatening my station?

title: Profit and Loss
line: No one is threatening you. The Central Command merely wants to make sure they have your undivided attention.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Well, they have it. I assume this has something to do with Professor Lang and her students?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Students is a rather benign term for them. Terrorists would be more accurate. The Cardassian government would very much like Hogue and Rekelen returned home immediately.

title: Profit and Loss
line: They haven't committed any crimes here. As long as they're on my station, they're free to do whatever they want.

title: Profit and Loss
line: This is all very embarrassing, Commander. The Central Command would hate to see the Federation pulled into such an insignificant and purely internal affair.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I would hardly call it insignificant. Judging by the behavior of the ship out there, it appears the Central Command considers Hogue and Rekelen to be extremely dangerous.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Not at all. Annoying, perhaps, inconvenient, maybe, but dangerous? Hardly. And if they were dangerous, would the Central Command entrust the situation to me, a simple tailor?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Which only confirms what I have suspected all along. You, Mister Garak, are no simple tailor.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Really, Commander, that's another discussion entirely. All you really need to know right now is that the return of Hogue and Rekelen is in the best interests of the Cardassian Empire.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Or at least in the best interest of the Cardassian military.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Is there a difference?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Do you really expect a Bajoran station under Federation command to turn over Cardassian political refugees on your say-so?

title: Profit and Loss
line: The ultimate decision is of course yours. I am simply relaying a message.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Then relay this. Tell the Central Command if anyone attempts to take Hogue and Rekelen by force, I will respond in kind. Am I clear, Mister Garak?

title: Profit and Loss
line: Absolutely. Thank you for your time. Oh, and if you'd like, stop by the shop one day. I have a number of suits that would look quite flattering on you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Here, you go. Two mugs of Kanar on the house.

title: Profit and Loss
line: We didn't order these.

title: Profit and Loss
line: They're the drinks I promised you the first time you came in here. Sorry they took so long but things have been a little hectic. Do you mind?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'm afraid that we do.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Professor Lang told us you couldn't be trusted.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You Cardassians do hold grudges. Seven years ago Natima and I had some little silly lovers' quarrel and well, all I can say is I'm willing to let bygones be bygones.

title: Profit and Loss
line: But Professor Lang isn't.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I have to say I find your loyalty to her extremely touching.

title: Profit and Loss
line: There is nothing that we wouldn't do for her, and if she says we're not to talk to you, we don't talk to you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I understand. She's your teacher, you're her students. You have to listen to her. So, if you don't want to talk to the only person who can get you off this station in one piece, that's fine with me.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Wait.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You say you can help us get away?

title: Profit and Loss
line: It's possible.

title: Profit and Loss
line: How?

title: Profit and Loss
line: One second.

title: Profit and Loss
line: The station's security chief's a shape-shifter. You can never be too careful. I take it you know what a cloaking device is? Well, I have one. It's not in the best of condition but it'll work for about fifteen minutes. Long enough to get you away from here.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Sounds expensive.

title: Profit and Loss
line: We don't have much latinum. What we do have is yours.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Exactly how much latinum are we talking about? No, forget I said that. I don't want your money. Consider the cloaking device a gift.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'm surprised. Ferengis aren't known for their generosity.

title: Profit and Loss
line: We are a deeply misunderstood race.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You may've saved our lives. Our movement owes you a debt of gratitude.

title: Profit and Loss
line: And I know exactly how you can repay me. You have to convince Natima to stay here.

title: Profit and Loss
line: The Professor will never agree to stay behind.

title: Profit and Loss
line: No Natima, no cloaking device, and no way off this station.

title: Profit and Loss
line: She won't do it.

title: Profit and Loss
line: You have to talk her into it. After all, you're the ones the Cardassians are after.

title: Profit and Loss
line: He's right. She shouldn't have to risk her life for our crimes.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I suppose we could ask her.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Don't ask her. Tell her.

title: Profit and Loss
line: We will. We'll do our best.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'm sure you will. I shudder to think what would happen if the military got its hands on you.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Meet us at our quarters in an hour.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'll be there.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Come in.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Where are Rekelen and Hogue?

title: Profit and Loss
line: They're waiting at the ship.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Perfect. I know my quarters might seem a little crowded at first, but tomorrow morning, I'll put in a request for something bigger.

title: Profit and Loss
line: That won't be necessary.

title: Profit and Loss
line: All right. If you want your own quarters to start out with, I can arrange that, too.

title: Profit and Loss
line: I mean I'm not staying.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Now hold on. Your students and I have an agreement. They get the cloaking device and you stay with me. That way everyone's happy.

title: Profit and Loss
line: Quark, you say you love me? Then give me that cloaking device and let me be on my way.

title: Profit and Loss
line: And let you disappear out of my life again?

title: Profit and Loss
line: I'm not part of your life.

title: Profit and Loss
line: But you are. You always have been. Don't you understand, since you left me, not a day goes by that I don't regret what I did. And now you're asking me to lose you again.

title: Profit and Loss

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Sir, I know this is none of my business

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: But you're going to give me your opinion anyway.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I don't know what the Cardassians told you

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: They played a confession from the man who planted the bomb. A man they most likely tortured to death.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: And you don't think you might be playing into their hands?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I've got people out there killing people, Major. You suggest I turn a blind eye to that?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Well, they don't have a right to defend themselves?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: They've crossed the line.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: If Starfleet is unwilling to defend their people in

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: They chose to live with the Cardassians.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Well, I didn't. But I lived with them for twenty six years before the liberation came. Every Bajoran lived with them in constant fear. I know what those colonists are going through. Most of all, I know that the Cardassians can't be trusted to keep their side of the bargain in this treaty.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: So, you'd suggest the Federation not keep our side of the bargain either, perhaps by arming these colonists?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I can tell you one thing for certain. The Cardassians are the enemy, not your own colonists, and if Starfleet can't understand that, then the Federation is even more naive than I already think it is.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I've been sent to relieve you

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: There must be some mistake. I just reported for duty an hour

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Yes?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Sorry to disturb you, sir, but there's a message here from Commander Sisko.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: We have been asked to escort you to airlock eleven, sir.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: A Cardassian freighter's just arrived.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Is there a problem?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Apparently another bomb has been found and disarmed.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Where's Commander Sisko?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Comfortably asleep in his quarters, I hope. Remember me?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I take it we're not about to board a Cardassian freighter.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I'm hoping I don't have to remind the admiral how many people pass through here during a week's time. It's not possible to keep tabs on every single person while they're on the station

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: If I didn't know you better, commander, I'd think you were just making excuses

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I'm not making excuses! Would it be in keeping with Federation policy to frisk everyone who steps through our airlocks? To search every room of every visitor during their stay?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Of course not but with two kidnappings and a ship being destroyed all in less than a week's time obviously your security measures leave something to be desired

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Security on this station is by the book. Our security program and the officers who work in it are first-rate.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Then what were they doing when all this was happening? We here at Starfleet are watching how you resolve this situation very closely, commander. We think it might be prudent to replace this chief of security you have

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Odo is both highly intelligent and extremely thorough. He's the most qualified person I have for the job.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Still, it would be a concrete example that you are taking active measures to resolve this situation and to make sure it doesn't happen again.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I stand behind my chief of security one hundred percent.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: That may be a mistake, Commander

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Then it's my mistake.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Then let me make my point again. Starfleet is very unhappy this has happened. We want this matter taken care of immediately. I don't have to remind you how this reflects on your position

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: We're doing everything we can to apprehend the kidnappers

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Don't bother me with details. Just clean up the mess, Commander. And quickly. Before this becomes a permanent stain on your record. Do I make myself clear?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Yes, sir.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: What do you think they're telling him?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: With two kidnappings and a ship exploding in the course of a week, I'm sure they've got a few things to say.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: It's their own fault. I've been warning them from the beginning.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: What are you talking about, their fault? You're in charge of Security.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: If you will let me be in charge of Security I will give you a safe station. You people tell me to do my job then give me a Federation rulebook listing all the things I can't do. Untie my hands before you start to blame me, Mister O'Brien.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I'm sure no one meant to blame you, Odo.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Give me the right to set a curfew, let me do more searches of arriving passengers, give me fifty more deputies.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: And this station will be just the way it was during the occupation.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Say what you like, it was safer then.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Unless you happened to be a Bajoran.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I want a complete review of all security measures on board this station.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I'd be delighted to accommodate you.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: What do we have from the guard?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: He's given us a description of the two who assaulted him. A Vulcan female and a human male in a Starfleet officer's uniform.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: We're trying to locate anyone they might have contacted here.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: How many ships left the station during the night?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Only two, sir. A Bardeezan merchant ship and a Galador freighter.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: What were their destinations?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: The Bardeezans went through the wormhole. The freighter is operating on a trade route between Galador Two and Farius Prime.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I'm guessing these people wouldn't take Dukat through the wormhole. They'd head back to the Demilitarized Zone with him. Dax, check the Galador ship's registry and make sure it's in order. Chief, see if you can identify its warp signature from our sensor records.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: No problem, Commander. I've got it.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Last known course?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: The computer's showing it was on a bearing two one six, mark one seven seven. As it left our sensor range, it was still heading for Farius Prime.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Major, send a message to Farius Prime. If that ship shows up, and I doubt it will, I want to know about it right away.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I could send the warp signature out over subspace.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: We could make it a general transmission. If it changes course, someone should spot them.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Do it.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: It's a phony. The Galadorans don't have any ships in this sector. The registry is forged.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Doctor, Major, you're with me. Odo, send a message to Commander Hudson at the Volan colony that I'm moving in his direction on the assumption that Dukat will be taken to the Demilitarized zone. Give him the warp signature of the ship.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Aye, sir.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Commander, we just received a general subspace transmission from somewhere in the Demilitarized zone. A group there is taking credit for the kidnapping of Dukat. They're calling themselves the Maquis.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Commander, a Klingon freighter two light years from the Demilitarized zone has ID'ed the warp signature. The ship did change course just as you predicted.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Transmit their last known coordinates and heading to us, Chief.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Acknowledged.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Let us know if anyone else picks up their signature.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Aye, sir. O'Brien out.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Set a new course, Major.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Yes, sir. Their heading takes them into the Badlands.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Badlands?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: It's a stretch of the Cardassian border ships try to avoid. A lot of plasma storms in the area.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: A few ships have been lost there over the past year or two.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Sounds like the perfect place for a hideout. Excuse me, sir. What do you plan to do if we catch up with them? After all, these Maquis are Federation colonists.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: We're going to get Gul Dukat back by any means necessary.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Even if we have to fire on our own people?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Long range sensors are picking up the warp signature. It leads to an M-class asteroid.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Take us there.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Scanning the surface. I've located the ship.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Those are human life signs.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Is there a Cardassian among them?

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: No, sir.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: Prepare to beam down.

title: The Maquis, Part One
line: I'm glad to see you had no trouble finding us, Ben. It seems that one disaster after another keeps bringing us back together again. To Be Continued

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'm glad to see you had no trouble finding us, Ben. It seems that one disaster after another keeps bringing us back together again. And now for the conclusion.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: You should have seen the look on your face when you saw me standing there, Ben.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I hardly recognized you without your uniform.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Well, it's been feeling a little tight lately.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Just like that.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: It's just a uniform, Ben.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Is that all it is? I remember when you first put it on.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Yes, graduation day at the Academy. We both swore we'd be starship captains by the time we were thirty.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: And admirals by forty.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Yes.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I think we've both done pretty well for ourselves.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Yes, we have, haven't we? But now I've got something better. These settlers, Ben, if you saw all they have accomplished without any help from the Federation, then you'd fight along with them.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I don't think so.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: They've traveled out here to the back of the beyond and built homes out of the wilderness. Now maybe the Federation can turn their back on them, but I can't.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'm not asking you to, but your joining the Maquis isn't helping anyone. Your actions have only endangered the treaty and put millions of lives at risk.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: The Federation believes that it can solve every problem with a treaty, but out here, on the frontier, without the power of the Federation to back them up, a treaty is only a piece of paper.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Do you have evidence that the Central Command has violated the treaty?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Not yet, but we will.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: If you're depending on Gul Dukat for proof, you're going to be disappointed.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: We'll find out, won't we.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I want him back, Cal.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: He's not here.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Then where is he?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I never thought I'd see the day when you'd side with a Cardassian against me.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Damn it, Cal. I'm on your side.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: You've got a funny way of showing it, Ben.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'm trying to stop you from making one of the biggest mistakes of your life. The Federation believes in the treaty. If you destroy it, Starfleet will come after you and they won't be satisfied until you're behind bars. If we work together to end the violence

title: The Maquis part 2
line: The violence will never end as long as the Central Command continues to smuggle weapons to their colonies. I wish there were a better way to handle this thing. I really do. Nobody wants peace any more than the Maquis.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: And you're willing to blow up Cardassian ships to get it.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: The Bok'Nor will never smuggle weapons again.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: And its crewmembers won't be returning home to their families either. Look, you say that the Central Command is behind the smuggling. Fine. Let's prove it.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: How?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: We'll go to Cardassia, find the evidence you need to back up your claim, and when we do, we'll take it to the Federation

title: The Maquis part 2
line: No. The Federation abandoned us. Told us to take care of ourselves. Well, that's what we intend to do, Ben. But you, you could be invaluable to us. Let us use your station.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: For what?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: A maintenance facility for our ships.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I can't allow that.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Every week innocent people are being murdered by the Cardassians. I will not allow those deaths to go unpunished.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: You don't want peace, Cal. You want revenge.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I prefer to call it retaliation. I'm sorry we won't be working together, Benjamin. It would've been nice. Like old times.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Commander!

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Sorry, Ben.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Okay, let's go. Knowing Ben's temper when he wakes up, we won't want to be here. Come on. Let's move out.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Lieutenant, I want to speak with the Cardassian Central Command.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Then you're in luck. Legate Parn will be arriving within the hour.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: A Legate? I feel honored. While I'm waiting, I'll talk with Starfleet.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Admiral Necheyev's already here.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Chief, The Maquis must have transferred Dukat off their ship before they reached that asteroid. I want to know where they've hid him.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I can retrace their warp trail, see if they met up with any other ships.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Do it.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Admiral.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Commander, the Cardassian Central Command has gone on military alert in response to the kidnapping of Gul Dukat.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'm not surprised.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: This Security Chief of yours, the shape-shifter.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Odo.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Odo. Are you sure you wouldn't be better off with a Starfleet officer heading your security team.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Admiral, I have complete faith in Odo's ability to do his job.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: If you say so, Commander.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I do. And as for Gul Dukat, I assure you we're taking all possible steps to locate him.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Good. Keep me informed of your progress.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I will. But Admiral, there's a bigger issue here than rescuing Dukat.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: And what is that?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: The Maquis.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: The Maquis are a bunch of irresponsible hotheads.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: These hotheads are responsible for the bombing of the Bok'Nor.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'm aware of that, Commander. We never should've allowed those colonists to remain on the Cardassian side of the Demilitarized zone.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Well they're there, Admiral, and they're not leaving.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: What about Commander Hudson? He's lived with these people. What's his analysis of the situation?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'll have to ask him.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: You do that. And Commander, I want you to find the Maquis. Talk to them. Remind them that they're citizens of the Federation. That it is imperative that we preserve the treaty with the Cardassians.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: A treaty the Cardassians may not be honoring.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Are you questioning Federation policy, Commander?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: All I know is that the situation in the Demilitarized zone is deteriorating rapidly.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Personally, I think you're overstating the problem. Establish a dialogue with the Maquis. They're still Federation citizens. I'm sure they'll listen to reason. Good luck, Commander.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Establish a dialogue? What the hell does she think I've been trying to do?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Commander?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Just because a group of people belongs to the Federation it does not mean that they are saints.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Excuse me?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Do you know what the trouble is?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: No.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: The trouble is Earth.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Really?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: On Earth there is no poverty, no crime, no war. You look out the window of Starfleet headquarters and you see paradise. Well, it's easy to be a saint in paradise, but the Maquis do not live in paradise. Out there in the Demilitarized zone, all the problems haven't been solved yet. Out there, there are no saints, just people. Angry, scared, determined people who are going to do whatever it takes to survive whether it meets with Federation approval or not.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Makes sense to me.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'm glad someone understands.

line: Legate Parn's ship just put in at docking bay five. Maybe you'd like to give the same speech to him.

line: I think you'd better get down to Security. I've caught one of the Vulcan's accomplices.

line: Really? Then perhaps you could explain why the two of you were spending so much time together.

line: Surely it's no crime keeping company with a beautiful female. You ought to try it, Odo. It might improve your disposition.

line: Do you expect us to believe that a Vulcan would be interested in you for your lobes?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Vulcans are a species that appreciate good ears. Commander, this is very embarrassing, having to discuss my personal life in such surroundings.

title: The Maquis part 2

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Save the excuses, Quark. Just tell us what you were up to.

line: Sakonna was in the market for certain items which I was able to obtain. At a considerable discount, I might add.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: What items?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: We're waiting.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Let's see. Where to begin? She wanted some deflector shields, navigational arrays, maybe a couple of hundred photon torpedoes.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Photon torpedoes!

title: The Maquis part 2
line: And pulse cannons and some high energy disrupters.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Weapons. You sold weapons to a terrorist group.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I did not. The Pygorians sold them the weapons. I merely made some introductions. Besides, I hadn't even heard of the Maquis until after Dukat was kidnapped.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I want a complete list of every weapon she purchased.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Of course. And if you need some one to testify against Sakonna in court, I'd be more than willing.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Would you?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: In a second. And let me know if there's anyone else who needs testifying against. I'll tell you one thing, Commander, Sakonna was on a tight clock. Whatever she needed those weapons for, it's going to happen within the next few days.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Just get me the list.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Sir? I assume you'll be going out to search for Dukat again?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: As soon as O'Brien tells us where to look.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: As Chief of Security, I'd like to go along.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I'll be happy to have you along.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: One other thing. How long do I keep him in here?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Forever.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Odo.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: This isn't funny. Odo!

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Commander, this is Legate Parn. He insisted on seeing you immediately.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Because my business here is crucial. It demands immediate attention. And as a member of the Cardassian Central Command I must assure you, Commander, that what we have to discuss is most crucial indeed.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I understand. I assure you we are doing everything we can to find Gul Dukat.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Please, Commander, your efforts are appreciated but unnecessary. You see, Central Command has learned that Gul Dukat was the leader of a small group of misguided officers who were funneling weapons to our colonies in the Demilitarized zone.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: The Maquis are right. The Cardassian settlers are being supplied by the Central Command.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Dukat and the others were operating entirely without our knowledge. Central Command would never sanction anything that would violate our treaty with the Federation. We've arrested Dukat's co-conspirators and they shall be dealt with accordingly.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Where does that leave Dukat?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: With the Maquis, where he belongs.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Are you saying you don't want him back?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I assume the Maquis will execute him for his crimes.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I wouldn't be surprised.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Well then, I don't see what difference it makes whether we do it or they do it.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: How do we know they won't use Dukat's death as an excuse to send troops into the Demilitarized zone?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I can assure you, Commander, that there shall be no retaliation. The Cardassians have no desire to go to war again with the Federation. You have my word.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Your word?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Major. I've found our little talk very enlightening.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I hoped you would.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Unfortunately, I have some business to attend to, but I do hope you'll take the time to enjoy the station.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Thank you, Commander, but I too must attend to my business. Besides, I am afraid this place has lost its charm since the last time I was here.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: I don't believe a word he said.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Neither do I. But he did tell me something that I needed to know. Cal was right. The Central Command is smuggling weapons into the Demilitarized zone.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: We just received a report that three Federation settlers were killed on Hakton Seven. The Cardassians claim it was in response to the destruction of the Bok'Nor.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Which gives the Maquis a new excuse to strike back. Chief, what have you found?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Based on the residual subspace distortion of their warp drive, I was able to plot the course of the Maquis ship that took Dukat. As you can see, long range sensors show no signs of any other vessels traveling along that route.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: All right. They didn't transfer him to another ship. What about a planet?

title: The Maquis part 2
line: It's possible. Their course took them past five M Class planets. I've downloaded their coordinates into the Rio Grande's computer.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Good work. Sisko to Odo.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Yes, Commander.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Find Doctor Bashir and meet me immediately at landing pad C.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: On our way.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Commander, you know there's no reason to go after Dukat. I mean, you heard Legate Parn. They don't want him back.

title: The Maquis part 2
line: Are you suggesting we leave him to the Maquis?

title: The Maquis part 2

title: The Wire

title: The Wire

title: The Wire
line: I just thought the story got a little redundant after a while. I mean the author's supposed to be chronicling seven generations of a single family, but he tells the same story over and over again. All of his characters lead selfless lives of duty to the state, grow old and die. Then the next generation comes along and does it all over again.

title: The Wire
line: But that's exactly the point, Doctor. The repetitive epic is the most elegant form of Cardassian literature, and The Never-Ending Sacrifice is it's greatest achievement.

title: The Wire
line: None of his characters ever really come alive, and there's more to life than duty to the state.

title: The Wire
line: A Federation viewpoint if ever I heard one. This is ridiculous. Can't you just move to the front of the line? Tell them it's a medical emergency or something.

title: The Wire
line: We'll be there in a minute. Look, maybe if you lent me another book by a different writer.

title: The Wire
line: It would only be a waste of time. When it comes to art, you're obviously a prisoner of Federation dogma and human prejudice.

title: The Wire
line: I'm fine.

title: The Wire

title: The Wire
line: I assure you, I'm in perfect health. Now, you were asking about other Cardassian books. Something maybe a little more accessible

title: The Wire
line: Perfect health. Then Cardassian standards must be a little lower than mine. Come on.

title: The Wire
line: Doctor, what do you think you're doing?

title: The Wire
line: I'm taking you to the Infirmary.

title: The Wire
line: That won't be necessary.

title: The Wire
line: Frankly, Doctor, I'm a little tired of humoring you. There's nothing wrong with me that a little peace and privacy wouldn't cure. Now if you'll excuse me, I seem to have lost my appetite.

title: The Wire
line: What was that all about?

title: The Wire
line: I have no idea.

title: The Wire
line: Can you tell what's wrong with it?

title: The Wire
line: In my expert medical opinion, I'd say It's sick.

line: I know that, but why is it sick?

title: The Wire
line: I'm a doctor, not a botanist. Did you ask Professor O'Brien?

line: Keiko's at a hydroponics conference on Rigel Four. She won't be back for a week.

line: And none of your past hosts have had any experience with plants?

title: The Wire
line: Daxs have never been much on gardening. Tobin was the only one who ever tried his hand at it, but he had even less luck with plants than he did with women.

title: The Wire
line: Do you even know where it's from?

title: The Wire
line: I picked it up on Ledonia Three.

title: The Wire
line: May I?

title: The Wire
line: Be my guest.

title: The Wire
line: That explains it. Ledonian soil contains a benevolent mycorrhizal fungus that helps the native plants retain water. But the fungus in this potting soil's almost completely died out. If we can salvage what's left and cultivate a new batch in the lab, that should do the trick.

title: The Wire
line: Keiko would be proud of you.

title: The Wire
line: It's all there on the screen. I only wish my humanoid patients were as easy to treat.

title: The Wire
line: Did Chief O'Brien dislocate his shoulder again?

title: The Wire
line: It's Garak. At lunch today, he seemed as though he was going to have some kind of seizure. He was having trouble breathing and he appeared to be in a great deal of pain. When I tried to get him to come to the Infirmary, he outright refused.

title: The Wire
line: Maybe he just doesn't like going to see the doctor.

title: The Wire
line: That's not it. It's that damn Cardassian evasiveness of his. I mean, making me guess about his past is one thing, but when it comes to his health? I don't know. Why can't he just tell me what's going on?

title: The Wire
line: It sounds like you're taking this personally.

title: The Wire
line: I suppose I am. It's just that Garak and I have been having lunch together once a week for more than a year now. You'd think he'd come to trust me a little.

title: The Wire
line: Why should he? It's not like you two are really friends.

title: The Wire
line: No, of course not. I suppose when it comes right down to it, I don't trust him either. I mean, for all I know, the man is a Cardassian spy.

title: The Wire
line: Exactly.

title: The Wire
line: Exactly. If he doesn't want my help, that's his prerogative.

title: The Wire
line: So I take it we understand each other?

title: The Wire
line: Garak, how long have you been living on this station?

title: The Wire
line: Too long.

title: The Wire
line: And in all that time, have I ever let you down?

title: The Wire
line: I have never done business with you until now.

title: The Wire
line: Which is why this deal is so important to me. I want our business relationship to get off on the right foot. Now relax. You'll get your merchandise.

title: The Wire
line: Soon, Quark I. can't wait much longer.

title: The Wire
line: You and Garak going into business? I couldn't help overhearing your conversation.

title: The Wire
line: Oh, that. I'm helping Garak get a new sizing scanner for his shop.

title: The Wire
line: A sizing scanner?

title: The Wire
line: Not just any sizing scanner. The best. Straight from Merak Two. Calibrated to be accurate down to the micrometer. And, I might add, at a very reasonable price.

title: The Wire
line: Really? I thought Garak sounded a bit upset.

title: The Wire
line: Upset? Garak? I hadn't noticed. Now, is there anything I can do for you? A little Saurian brandy to go, or maybe a late night session in a holosuite?

title: The Wire
line: No. Thank you. I think I'll call it a night.

title: The Wire
line: Suit yourself.

title: The Wire
line: There. How does that feel?

line: Much better.

title: The Wire
line: Try not to yell at any more admirals for a while.

line: Chief.

line: You wanted to see me?

title: The Wire
line: Yes. I was hoping you could give me a hand. I've been trying to access the old Cardassian medical files but I haven't been having much luck.

title: The Wire
line: I'm not surprised. The Cardassians did a general systems sweep before they pulled out. The medical files would have been deleted along with everything else.

title: The Wire
line: Is there any way to recover them?

title: The Wire
line: Maybe. These subroutines don't look anywhere near as bad as the engineering files did. I might be able to reconstruct the data by microscanning the purge trace.

title: The Wire
line: How long will that take?

title: The Wire
line: Two, maybe three weeks.

title: The Wire
line: Well, that settles that. Thank you anyway, Chief.

title: The Wire
line: Sorry I couldn't be any more help.

line: This is Bashir.

line: Doctor, I need you in my bar right away.

title: The Wire
line: Come on, Garak. Don't you think you've had enough?

title: The Wire
line: On the contrary. Anyone who talks about the numbing effects of your liquor is severely overstating the case.

title: The Wire
line: What's all this?

title: The Wire
line: He came in complaining about a headache. The next thing I knew he drank up half my stock of kanar.

title: The Wire
line: Doctor, what a pleasant surprise. I apologize for my outburst at lunch, but I promise I'll make it up to you. Please, join me.

title: The Wire
line: I think I will. May I?

title: The Wire
line: By all means.

title: The Wire
line: What are you doing?

line: I think it's a little noisy in here. I prefer to drink somewhere quiet.

title: The Wire
line: The Infirmary? My dear Doctor, what kind of fool do you take me for? Now give me back my bottle. Give me my bottle!

title: The Wire
line: I will. In the Infirmary.

title: The Wire
line: I'm not going to the Infirmary and I refuse to play this ridiculous game. Now give me, give me

title: The Wire
line: Make it stop. Make it stop.

line: Bashir to Ops. Medical emergency. Two to beam to the Infirmary. Energize.

title: The Wire
line: Some kind of implant?

title: The Wire
line: Apparently.

title: The Wire
line: What's it for?

title: The Wire
line: Well, I was hoping you could tell me. After working for the Cardassians for five years, I'd guess you know them as well as anyone.

title: The Wire
line: Maybe so, but I never bothered to look inside their skulls.

title: The Wire
line: No, I don't suppose you did.

title: The Wire
line: Do you think this is the cause of Garak's condition?

title: The Wire
line: It's possible. Whatever this thing is, it's situated in his postcentral gyrus and has filaments that connect it to his entire central nervous system.

title: The Wire
line: Maybe it's some kind of punishment device. A parting gift from the Cardassian government.

title: The Wire
line: I thought of that, but based on the amount of scarring in the surrounding tissue, this implant's been in there for years. And as far as I can tell, Garak's only been in pain for the past few days.

title: The Wire
line: Interesting. I wish I had an answer for you, Doctor.

title: The Wire
line: Well, I was hoping you could help me get one. I think Quark knows what this thing is.

title: The Wire
line: Now what makes you say that?

title: The Wire
line: I overheard them talking the other night. Garak was negotiating to buy some merchandise from Quark. He seemed pretty desperate. I tried to ask Quark what it was about, but

title: The Wire
line: No need to explain, Doctor. The direct approach seldom works with people like him. This could answer some of my own questions. Quark has sent several coded messages to Cardassia Prime in the past few days.

title: The Wire
line: Really?

title: The Wire
line: I routinely monitor all of Quark's subspace communications.

title: The Wire
line: Is that legal?

title: The Wire
line: It's in the best interests of station security. Doctor, do you want to know what Quark knows or not?

title: The Wire
line: I see your point.

title: The Wire
line: Then meet me in Security at oh two hundred hours. Quark always makes his clandestine calls after the bar closes.

title: The Wire
line: I wouldn't miss it.

title: The Wire
line: Quark, you parasite. It's been too long. Is Hartla still working for you?

title: The Wire
line: The dabo tables wouldn't be the same without her.

title: The Wire
line: Oh, what I wouldn't give to see her again.

title: The Wire
line: I'm sure she misses you too.

title: The Wire
line: I'll bet she does. She would've bankrupted me if the occupation would've lasted much longer. But I'm sure you didn't contact me just to reminisce. What can I do for you?

title: The Wire
line: How'd you like to earn a little extra latinum? Maybe enough to buy yourself a promotion?

title: The Wire
line: You have my undivided attention.

title: The Wire
line: I need a piece of Cardassian bio-technology and the schematics relating to its installation.

title: The Wire
line: Bio-technology. That shouldn't be too difficult. What is it?

title: The Wire
line: You know, I never ask those kinds of questions, but I've got the requisition code number.

title: The Wire
line: Give it to me. I'll look for it.

title: The Wire
line: I knew I could count on you. Here it is.

title: The Wire
line: I hope you don't have one of those little bugs hidden in my quarters.

title: The Wire
line: Should I?

line: Hold on.

title: The Wire
line: This won't take long.

title: The Wire
line: Take your time.

line: Quark, you idiot!

title: The Wire
line: Is something wrong?

title: The Wire
line: Is something wrong? I'm ruined. My career is over.

title: The Wire
line: What did I do?

title: The Wire
line: You and your damn requisition code. It's for classified bio-technology, Quark. Even the cursed number is classified. Where did you get it? No. Don't tell me. I don't want to know. If I'm lucky, I can still get through this with my skin intact. Maybe they won't trace the request back to me.

title: The Wire
line: Who won't?

title: The Wire
line: The Obsidian Order.

title: The Wire
line: Nice talking to you, Boheeka. We'll have to

title: The Wire
line: Do it again sometime.

title: The Wire
line: The Obsidian Order. That certainly complicates things.

title: The Wire
line: Who are they?

title: The Wire
line: They're the ever-vigilant eyes and ears of the Cardassian Empire. It is said that a Cardassian citizen cannot sit down to a meal without each dish being duly noted and recorded by the Order.

title: The Wire
line: What happens if you eat something that doesn't meet with their approval?

title: The Wire
line: People have been known to disappear for less. Whether you agree with their goals or not, you can't help but admire their efficiency. Even the Romulan Tal Shiar can't compete with them when it comes to intelligence gathering and covert operations.

title: The Wire
line: What has all this to do with Garak?

title: The Wire
line: I wish I knew.

title: The Wire
line: Do you think the Order put that implant in Garak's head?

title: The Wire
line: I have a better question. If the implant is a punishment device, then why is Garak trying to get his hands on another one?

title: The Wire
line: He did ask for the specifications. Maybe he's trying to find some way of removing it.

title: The Wire
line: Either way, I'd like to have a talk with him when he wakes up.

title: The Wire
line: You'll have to get in line. Thank you, Constable.

title: The Wire
line: Computer, report on the status of patient Garak.

title: The Wire
line: Patient Garak is no longer in the infirmary.

title: The Wire
line: What? When did he leave?

title: The Wire
line: Patient checked out at zero three twenty hours.

title: The Wire
line: Garak? Are you in there? Computer, open the door to chamber nine oh one, habitat level H three. Emergency medical override Bashir one alpha.

title: The Wire
line: Ah, Doctor, what a pleasant surprise. I'm sorry, I must've missed the door chime.

title: The Wire
line: What the hell do you think you're doing? Triptacederine. How much of this did you take?

title: The Wire
line: A mere thirty cc's. Not nearly enough, I'm afraid.

title: The Wire
line: Thirty cc's would anesthetize an Algorian mammoth.

title: The Wire
line: We Cardassians must be made of sterner stuff. I barely feel it.

title: The Wire
line: Listen to me, Garak. I've had just about enough of your nonsense. Now you're coming back to the Infirmary with me.

title: The Wire
line: I don't think so. Believe me when I tell you there's nothing you can do for me.

title: The Wire
line: Oh, and Quark can, is that it?

title: The Wire
line: I thought I was supposed to be the spy.

title: The Wire
line: Quark's not coming, Garak.

title: The Wire
line: How do you know?

title: The Wire
line: I heard him talking to his Cardassian contact. He couldn't get the item you requested.

title: The Wire
line: Really? That's most distressing, but I suppose, not all that surprising. Ah, well. Maybe it's for the best. My hypospray, if you please.

title: The Wire
line: Another dose of triptacederine might kill you.

title: The Wire
line: Thank you for your concern, Doctor, but I'd rather have the hypospray.

title: The Wire
line: I'm not going to let you commit suicide. I'm here to help you.

title: The Wire
line: I doubt you can. I think you'll find that I'm experiencing some slight deterioration of my cranial nerve cluster.

title: The Wire
line: It's not so slight, I'm afraid. We've got to get you to the infirmary.

title: The Wire
line: My dear Doctor, I have no intention of putting myself on display for the amusement of the Bajoran inhabitants of this station.

title: The Wire
line: It's not your pride I'm worried about. It's that implant you're carrying around inside your head.

title: The Wire
line: You know about that, do you?

title: The Wire
line: It's some kind of punishment device, isn't it?

title: The Wire
line: Punishment device? I suppose in a way that's what it's become.

title: The Wire
line: If it wasn't put there to punish you, then what's it for? Garak, I need to know what we're up against. If you tell me what it was meant for, maybe I could find some way to remove it.

title: The Wire
line: It's hopeless, Doctor. Believe me, it can't be removed.

title: The Wire
line: How do you know?

title: The Wire
line: That's the whole point. If it could be easily removed, it would be useless. You see, on Cardassia I was entrusted with certain information. Information that needed to be kept safe regardless of the situation. My implant was given to me by Enabran Tain himself, the head of the Obsidian Order. If I was ever tortured, it was designed to stimulate the pleasure centers of my brain to trigger the production of vast amounts of natural endorphins. I do hope you appreciate the irony, Doctor. The sole purpose of the implant was to make me immune to pain.

title: The Wire
line: What caused it to malfunction?

title: The Wire
line: It was never meant for continuous use.

title: The Wire
line: Continuous use? What do you mean?

title: The Wire
line: Living on this station is torture for me, Doctor. The temperature is always too cold, the lights always too bright. Every Bajoran on the station looks at me with loathing and contempt. So one day I decided I couldn't live with it anymore, and I took the pain away.

title: The Wire
line: You activated the implant.

title: The Wire
line: I created a device which allowed me to trigger the implant whenever I wanted. At first, I only used it a few minutes a day, but I began relying on it more and more until finally I just turned it on and never shut it off.

title: The Wire
line: How long has it been on?

title: The Wire
line: Two years.

title: The Wire
line: And now the implant is breaking down.

title: The Wire
line: That's correct.

title: The Wire
line: Then why not just shut the damn thing off?

title: The Wire
line: It's too late, now. My body has become completely dependent on the higher endorphin levels generated by the implant.

title: The Wire
line: So, that's it then. You're going to just give up and let them win.

title: The Wire
line: Them, Doctor?

title: The Wire
line: The Central Command, the Obsidian Order, whoever it is who exiled you here. You're just going to roll over and die, let them destroy you, give up any hope of ever seeing Cardassia again.

title: The Wire
line: Doctor, did anyone ever tell you that you are an infuriating pest?

title: The Wire
line: Chief O'Brien all the time, and I don't pay any attention to him either.

title: The Wire
line: Has it ever occurred to you that I might be getting exactly what I deserve?

title: The Wire
line: No one deserves this.

title: The Wire
line: Oh, please, Doctor. I'm suffering enough without having to listen to your smug Federation sympathy. Do you think because we have lunch together once a week, you know me? You couldn't even begin to fathom what I'm capable of.

title: The Wire
line: I'm a doctor. You're my patient. That's all I need to know.

title: The Wire
line: Wrong again. You need to know who you're trying to save. During the occupation, I was a Gul in the Cardassian Mechanized Infantry. We were stationed just outside the Bajoran Capital. Shortly before the withdrawal, a handful of Bajoran prisoners escaped from my custody. My aide, a man named Elim, tracked them to a Cardassian shuttle about to depart for Terok Nor. Elim got aboard, but the captain refused to let him search the ship, because he claimed he was under strict orders from Gul Dukat to depart immediately. So I had the shuttle destroyed, killing the escapees, Elim, and ninety seven Cardassian civilians.

title: The Wire
line: You can't be serious.

title: The Wire
line: I followed my orders. None of those prisoners escaped off of Bajor alive. Unfortunately as it turned out, one of the passengers on the shuttle was the daughter of a prominent military official. I was stripped of my rank and commission, and exiled from Cardassia. So now you know, Doctor. I hope I haven't shattered too many of your illusions.

title: The Wire
line: Listen to me, Garak. Right now I'm not concerned with what you did in the past. I'm simply not going to walk out of here and let you die. We need to turn that implant off and whatever withdrawal symptoms or side effects you may experience, I promise I'll help you through them. I need to know where that triggering device is. Where is it?

title: The Wire
line: The desk, second drawer.

title: The Wire
line: That'll be all for now. If you need to reach me, I'll be here for at least the next twenty six hours.

title: The Wire
line: Computer I'm reading an ongoing erosion of tissue in the patient's lymphatic system. Explain.

title: The Wire
line: Unable to determine a cause due to insufficient data on Cardassian physiology.

title: The Wire
line: All right. Continue to monitor the status of the patient's cranial implant. Inform me if it shows any sign of reactivation.

title: The Wire
line: Yes?

title: The Wire
line: Doctor, I was hoping I could ask Garak some questions.

title: The Wire
line: He's asleep. He has been ever since I turned off his implant. Come on, we can talk outside.

title: The Wire
line: Doctor, I need to talk to him as soon as possible. I have four cases left in my homicide files which I'm almost certain were committed by the Obsidian Order. If Garak was a member he may be able to shed some light on them.

title: The Wire
line: I'm afraid your questions will have to wait.

title: The Wire
line: How long?

title: The Wire
line: I don't know yet. Constable, Garak's body has undergone a severe shock. I don't know when he'll recover. I'm not even sure if he'll recover.

title: The Wire
line: In that case I want to talk to him now. Wake him up.

title: The Wire
line: I'll do no such thing.

title: The Wire
line: Doctor, these are murder cases and Garak may be a suspect.

title: The Wire
line: That may be so, but he's still my patient and I won't have him disturbed. So until further notice, his quarters are off limits to everyone except emergency medical personnel. So, if you'll excuse me, I have a patient to attend to.

title: The Wire
line: Garak?

title: The Wire
line: Leave me alone.

title: The Wire
line: I don't think that would be a good idea right now. Your blood chemistry is severely imbalanced. You need to rest.

title: The Wire
line: Don't touch me.

title: The Wire
line: Just calm down.

title: The Wire
line: I don't want to be calm, Doctor. I've been calm long enough. Look at this place. It's pathetic. To think that this is what my life has been reduced to. This sterile shell, this prison.

title: The Wire
line: Take it easy, Garak. Look, you're obviously experiencing some side effects from the deactivation of the implant.

title: The Wire
line: Ridiculous. I feel more clear-headed than I have in the past two years. Two years. What a waste these past two years have been.

title: The Wire
line: There was a time, Doctor, oh there was a time when I was a power. The protégé of Enabran Tain himself. Do you have any idea what that means?

title: The Wire
line: I'm afraid I don't.

title: The Wire
line: No, you don't, do you. You don't know much of anything. Tain was the Obsidian Order. Not even the Central Command dared challenge him. And I was his right hand. My future was limitless until I threw it away.

title: The Wire
line: You mean when you had that shuttle shot down to stop those prisoners from escaping?

title: The Wire
line: Stop them? I only wish that I had stopped them.

title: The Wire
line: You didn't?

title: The Wire
line: No, Doctor, my disgrace was worse than that. Unimaginably worse.

title: The Wire
line: What could you have possibly done worse than that?

title: The Wire
line: I let them go. It was the eve of the Cardassian withdrawal. Elim and I were interrogating five Bajorans. They were children, Doctor. None of them were older than fourteen years old. They knew nothing. They lived in bombed-out rooms, scrounged for food on the streets. They were filthy and they stank. The room was freezing cold, the air was like ice, and suddenly the whole exercise seemed utterly meaningless. All I wanted was a hot bath and a good meal. So I let them go. I gave them whatever latinum I had in my pockets, and opened the door, and flung them back into the street. Elim couldn't believe his eyes. He looked at me as if I were insane.

title: The Wire
line: You took pity on those children. There's nothing wrong with that.

title: The Wire
line: No! I was a fool! I should've finished the interrogation and turned them over to the troops for execution. But because I was chilly and my stomach was growling, I failed in my duty and destroyed everything I had worked for.

title: The Wire
line: And so they exiled you.

title: The Wire
line: That's right. And left me to live out my days with nothing to look forward to but having lunch with you.

title: The Wire
line: I'm sorry you feel that way. I thought you enjoyed my company.

title: The Wire
line: I did. And that's the worst part. I can't believe that I actually enjoyed eating mediocre food and staring into at your smug, sanctimonious face. I hate this place and I hate you.

title: The Wire
line: Okay, Garak, that's your prerogative. Now I really think you should lie down.

title: The Wire
line: Get away from me.

title: The Wire
line: Garak.

title: The Wire
line: Garak, stop this. I don't want to hurt you.

title: The Wire
line: Bashir to Infirmary. I need an emergency medical team in Garak's quarters now.

title: The Wire
line: Administer another twenty cc's of hyperzine.

title: The Wire
line: He's not responding.

title: The Wire
line: Give it a second. Begin cardiostimulation.

title: The Wire
line: His heartbeat is stabilizing.

title: The Wire
line: But his lymphatic system is critical. I don't understand it. I shut down the implant. It can't be affecting his blood chemistry anymore, yet toxins are still accumulating in his lymphatic tissues. Computer, display analyzes of all biochemical samples taken from the patient in the past thirty-nine hours. Display them by chemical composition. Isolate and display sample number seventeen. Bring up sample twenty three. Sample twenty seven. Sample thirty two. Sample thirty five. Sample forty. Stop. Bring back sample thirty five. Superimpose the molecular structure of this leukocyte with an analogous sample from yesterday. That's it. The molecular structure of Garak's leukocytes has been altered. That must be what's causing the accumulation of toxins in his system.

title: The Wire
line: Can we synthesize Cardassian leukocytes?

title: The Wire
line: Probably, but that could take weeks and we don't have that much time. We have three or fours days at most.

title: The Wire
line: If we turn the implant back on, we might be able to keep him alive for another week or two.

title: The Wire
line: No.

title: The Wire
line: What?

title: The Wire
line: I won't allow it. I never want that thing turned on again.

title: The Wire
