line: We asked Mrs O'Brien and she said it would be okay, so I invited Nog to come with us to the Gamma Quadrant.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Now hold on a second, Jake-o.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Dad, if Nog doesn't get a good grade on this science project, he's going to drop out of school. And I can't let that happen.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Maybe he can help you analyze the survey information when we get back?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That's not enough. Mrs O'Brien said he'd have to be an equal partner. Come on, Dad. He's my friend. I have to help him.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Morn, you've been sitting here all day staring at the same drink. Talk to me. I want to help. I'm not just your bartender, I'm your friend. Whatever's wrong, I'm here for you.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Hold that thought.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Well? What did he say?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: What did who say?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Commander Sisko. About my idea.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You mean using the monitors throughout the station to sell merchandise?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Stop torturing me, Odo. Tell me what he said.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Guess.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: He said yes.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Guess again.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: It would triple my profits. But how could he refuse?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Maybe it's because he doesn't like you.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Don't be ridiculous. Major Kira's the one that doesn't like me. Sisko

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Doesn't like you either.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: What did I ever do to him?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Oh, I could think of one or two things.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: One or two things. That's nothing. So do you think there's any way I can change his mind?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Ha!

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Uncle Quark?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Not now.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I just wanted to tell you I'm not going to be able to work my shift for the next couple of days.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Why not?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm going to the Gamma Quadrant with Jake and his father.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You're going to the Gamma Quadrant with Commander Sisko. How Lucky for you.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I always wanted to see what the cockpit of a runabout looked like. Hey, how do you fire the phasers?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Nog, you promised.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I wasn't going to touch anything.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Why don't the two of you stow our gear in the back while I go through pre-launch?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'll do it.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'll be right there.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Fire the phasers?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: He was kidding. Look, Dad. I know this isn't exactly the trip you planned on, but you'll see Nog's a great guy.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm sure he is. I was just hoping that you and I could spend this time together.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We will. Don't worry. You won't even know Nog's along. This'll be a great trip, you'll see.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Ah, there you are. Where do I put my bags?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Uncle Quark, what are you doing here?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: What does it look like? I'm going with you.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Since when?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Really, Commander. You don't expect my nephew to go all the way to the Gamma Quadrant without proper supervision? No offense. Some of my best friends are humans. But my brother Rom isn't as liberal as I am. Let's face it, he's never been comfortable about Nog's friendship with your son.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You can tell Rom not to worry. I'll take good care of the boy. And I promise I won't try to corrupt him with my human values.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I know that, but Rom is convinced all humans look down on Ferengi, and by allowing me to come on this trip you can help prove him wrong. He is wrong, isn't he?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Dad, please.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: All right. But let's get going before anyone else shows up.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Thanks, Dad. Thanks.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: This place is great.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Our preliminary surveys suggest it's a lot like Earth during the early Devonian period. A lot of plant life, fish, some insects, but no predators or large animals. Pretty, isn't it?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I don't see what's so pretty about it.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I think they mean the trees and stuff.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark, this is as close to paradise as you're going to get. All you need to do is allow yourself to see it.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I can tell you what I see in two words. Exploitable resources.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I suppose you want to cut down all these trees and start strip mining the entire planet.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: As a wise man once wrote, 'Nature decays, but latinum lasts forever.'

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Rule of Acquisition number one oh two.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Good lad. Nog, I have some ointment in one of my bags. Get it.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: What's the problem?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Oh, I get a mild reaction now and then.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: To what?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Nature.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Perhaps you'd be more comfortable sleeping on the runabout.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: And miss all the fun? Never. Besides, I'm really looking forward to our getting to know each other better.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Ahh, that's much better. Now, if it only wasn't so hot.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I hadn't noticed.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: It isn't the heat so much as the humidity and the insects, the stench of these flowers. I'm glad we could talk like this. There's nothing like facing the wilderness to bring people closer.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The answer is still no, Quark.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: No? No to what?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm not going to allow you to sell merchandise over the station's monitors.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Why not? It's a brilliant idea. With my connections, I could offer a whole range of merchandise which normally couldn't be acquired in this sector.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Such as?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Collectibles. Andorian jewellry, Vulcan IDIC pins, Bolian crystalsteel. And with my low overhead, I could offer these items at a significant discount.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark, you're wasting your time, and mine.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Did I mention I was going to donate two percent of my net profits to the Bajoran Fund for Orphans? Three percent?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: So how's it going?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The atmosphere's seventy seven percent nitrogen, twenty one percent oxygen, and two percent carbon dioxide. The water contains traces of copper, nickel and a little birythium.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You're showing a little lead there too.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: It's from the surrounding soil, but we think it's localized.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We're going to check other water sources just to be sure.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Why not wait until tomorrow. I was just about to start dinner.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Jumbalaya?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: How'd you know?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Great.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Jumbowhat?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You're going to love it.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The two of you did good work today.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Yes!

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Anyone want some more?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Not me.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Me neither, Commander, but it was very good. You know, I think I'm developing a taste for human food.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I still say there's some dirt in the sauce. And these bugs. Look at this. They get into everything. It's disgusting.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I thought the Ferengis liked eating bugs.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Only certain bugs. Ferengi bugs. Nog, get some more ointment for the back of my neck.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Yes, Uncle.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Better get a good night's sleep. We have another big day tomorrow.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Yeah, I want to start cataloging the plant life first thing in the morning. You know what this reminds me of?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: A camping trip we took on Itamish Three.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I don't think I remember you, me, and Mom ever having more fun together.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Isn't that where I taught you how to water ski?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Mom taught me how to water ski.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Yes. She was always the graceful one. You know, Jake, we really need to get away more often.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm ready whenever you are. I'm sure Nog is too. I'm joking.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm on fire! I'm on fire!

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark, cover it up! Are you all right?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: No, I'm not all right! My ears itch, my nose is running, I'm eating foreign bugs. Now look at me. One minute I'm trying to pick out a couple of bugs out of that jumbawhatsit pot, next thing I know, whoosh!

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark, calm down. Look, do us all a favor. Sit down and try to stay out of trouble.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: What did I do?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'd better go see if he's okay.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Now see what you've done.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: What I've done?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The boy couldn't stand seeing his favorite Uncle insulted. I guess Rom was right after all. You don't like Ferengis, do you?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That is not true.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: All right, name me one Ferengi you do like. Ah ha. You see? I was right. You Federation types are all alike. You talk about tolerance and understanding but you only practice it toward people who remind you of yourselves. Because you disapprove of Ferengi values, you scorn us, distrust us, insult us every chance you get.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark, I don't have to stand here and defend myself.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Tell me, Commander, would you allow your son to marry a Ferengi female?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I never thought about it.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Exactly my point.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Don't hurt me.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: How many of them are there?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: There's just the two of us.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Not you, the Jem'Hadar.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We don't know who you're talking about. We are not your enemies.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Then you'd better run.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: It's too late. You're done running.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: This has not been a good day.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Dad, this is Jake. Where are you? Dad, answer me.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm telling you, Jake, something's happened to them. Maybe they were attacked by a wild animal.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You heard my Dad. There aren't any wild animals, just insects and plants.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Maybe they were attacked by a vicious tree?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Take a look at this.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I don't know any trees that wear boots.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We'd better beam up to the runabout.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Listen, we can't run away just 'cos we're scared.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Hey, who said anything about being scared? I just thought the runabout would be a good place to er, to plan our next move.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: There's nothing to plan. My Dad never would've left here without telling me first, not unless he was in some sort of trouble. We can track them with the tricorder.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Hey! Wait for me.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Hey! Is anybody there? Hello! We're humanoids! We require food and water. Hello?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark, shut up.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: This is your fault. They were after you, not us. Why don't you say something to them? Tell them you've never seen us before. We have nothing to do with her! This is a misunderstanding!

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Quark.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I have the right to express my opinion.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm about to put my fist in your opinion.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You don't scare me. And you want to know why you don't scare me? Because I'm already more scared than I've ever been in my life.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You're not helping anything.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm not helping anything? I don't see you coming up with any ideas. Or her.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: If she wants to help us, she will. Right now, I'd say she's even more scared than you are.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Believe me, she's not.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: She's obviously been running from these people for a while. She's probably been through a lot. She doesn't know who we are, what we're about. I just hope that Jake and Nog are smart enough to stay out of sight until help gets here.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Trust me, I didn't raise my nephew to be a fool. He'll find the nearest dark hole and climb into it.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm not so sure about Jake. If I know him, he'll be looking for us.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Don't they teach you how to neutralize security fields in Starfleet?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I've never seen anything like this before. It seems like it's generated by

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Don't. The security barrier will kill you.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Thanks for the warning.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I have no wish to see you hurt.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: A lovely sentiment.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: How did you know that the security barrier's lethal?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Because everything about the Jem'Hadar is lethal.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Anything you can tell me about them might be helpful.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Are you saying you've never heard of the Jem'Hadar?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We're not from around here. My name is Benjamin Sisko. I'm from the United Federation of Planets. We came through a wormhole to get here. Our home is thousands of light years away.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: My name is Eris.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm glad to meet you, Eris.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That's Quark. Tell me about the Jem'Hadar.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: They're the most feared soldiers in the Dominion.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The Dominion? The Ferengi have been trying to open up trade negotiations with the Dominion for almost a year now. We've never heard of the Jem'Hadar.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Then you've been fortunate. Negotiations with the Dominion can be a dangerous thing.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: If it's so dangerous, why would anyone do business with them?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The Dominion decides that you have something that they want and then they come and take it by negotiation or by force. Believe me, I know. I've seen it happen on my own world. Kurill Prime was offered entry into the Dominion. They thought our telekinetic powers would be useful to them.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Back there in the camp, that's what you used to knock me down.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: When Kurill refused the Dominion's offer, they sent in the Jem'Hadar. They destroyed our communications center, they executed our leaders, and before we realized it, they had seized control of the entire planet.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: How did you manage to escape?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I was on a freighter returning home when the attack occurred. We fled, but they came after us.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Why?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: My mother was an outspoken opponent of the Dominion. I guess they wanted to make an example of my family.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That thing they put around your neck

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: It suppresses my telekinetic abilities. Without it, I might be able to break through the security barrier.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Then we'll just have to find a way to get this collar off.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Even if we do get past the barrier, no one ever escapes from the Jem'Hadar.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Luckily for us, they seem as sure about that as you do. Look around you. They've placed the three of us in the same containment field. I've never seen more than four guards on duty at any one time. As far as I can tell, there's only this single containment field between us and freedom. They're overconfident, and that's what's going to help us get out of here. Maybe if I can pry off that casing, I can get at the locking mechanism. May I?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Of course.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Are you sure you know how to read that thing?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Pretty sure.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Pretty sure? We've been walking for hours and you're only pretty sure?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Would you be quiet? I'm picking up some kind of humanoid lifeforms.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I don't know who they are, but they don't look friendly.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I wish we could get closer.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I don't think they'll look any friendlier close up.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Hello! I know someone must be listening to me out there.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: If we escape, do we have to take him with us?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: He's not so bad.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Whoever's in charge, you're missing a very lucrative opportunity.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Doesn't he realize he's not accomplishing anything?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Don't be so sure. We need to know what the Jem'Hadar plan to do with us. Which means we need to get their attention.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Did I mention I happen to be a close personal friend of the Grand Nagus. He's a very powerful person.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: And if there's one thing I know

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That's enough.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: It's that Quark is hard to ignore.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm Commander Benjamin Sisko of the United Federation of Planets. I want to know why we are being held here.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That's not my concern.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Then why won't you let us go?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Because the Founders don't want you released.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: And who are the Founders?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That's not your concern.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: This isn't getting us anywhere. Commander, allow me. How would you like a thousand cases of tulaberry wine.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Don't bother, Commander. I'm not going to do any permanent damage.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: If the Founders are the ones who give the orders, I want to meet them.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Those aren't my orders.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: He can't take you to the Founders because they don't exist. They're a myth.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The Founders exist. They created the Dominion.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: And the Jem'Hadar are their servants?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: A Ferengi and a human. I was hoping the first race I'd meet from the other side of the anomaly would be the Klingons.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm sorry to disappoint you.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: It's too late for apologies. The Dominion will no longer stand by and allow ships from your side to violate our territory. I hear that Klingons are effective warriors. What's that weapon they're so fond of? The bat'leth?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I am not interested in discussing the Klingons.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: All right. Then what about the Cardassians? Are you satisfied with the treaty your Federation made with them? It seems a tactical error.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: How do you know so much about our side of the galaxy?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We gain more knowledge every day, and now we have you to help us learn more.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I don't plan on telling you anything.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I won't be the one asking the questions.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Who will?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I was really hoping to meet a Klingon.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Well, now that we're all friends, I feel much better.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I hope this works.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You wanted a plan, I came up with a plan. Now let me concentrate. Computer, scan the region around our base camp for human and Ferengi lifesigns.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: One human and one Ferengi located.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: That's them.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I told you this would work. Computer, lock onto the two lifeforms and beam them up.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Unable to comply. Subjects are located inside a spatial distortion field.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I knew it couldn't be that easy.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Maybe we'd better go back to the station for help.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Good idea. Computer, fly us back to the station.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Please restate command.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Computer, disengage autopilot and lay in a course back to the wormhole.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Enter authorisation code.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Go ahead. What are you waiting for?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I don't know the authorisation code.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Vessel approaching from the planet's surface, bearing one seven three mark two eight one.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Computer, evasive manoeuver! Fire phasers! Launch torpedoes and escape pods!

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Computer, display the approaching ship on the monitor.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Computer, where'd the ship go?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: The vessel has entered warp, bearing one seven one mark two five nine.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Maybe they didn't see us.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Maybe we're not what they're after.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: So what do we do now?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We'll have to shut down the autopilot.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: How do we do that?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I guess we'll find out how much I learned working for Chief O'Brien.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Lieutenant, what's the eta of the Odyssey?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: They're due in eight hours. I'm reading elevated neutrino levels from the wormhole.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: On screen.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Hail them, Lieutenant.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: They're not answering.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Shields up. Go to yellow alert.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Computer, intruder in Ops. Activate a level three containment field.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm Major Kira Nerys, First Officer of this station. You'll have to excuse the containment field, but around here it's customary to identify yourself before transporting into someone else's command center.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: I'm Third Talak'Talan of the Jem'Hadar. I'm here to inform you that your commander has been detained for questioning by the Dominion.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Detained? For how long?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Indefinitely. Commander Sisko will serve as an example of what happens to anyone who interferes with the Dominion.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: What kind of interference are you talking about?

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Coming through the anomaly is interference enough. Unless you wish to continue to offend the Dominion, I suggest you stay on your side of the galaxy.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: You're making a mistake if you think that detaining Commander Sisko will stop us from exploring the Gamma Quadrant.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: We anticipated that response.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Security team to Ops.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Here's a list of vessels we've destroyed for violating our territory.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Where did you get this datapadd.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: From the Bajoran colony on our side of the anomaly. You should be proud. I hear they fought well for a spiritual people. I hope we won't have to repeat this lesson.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Chief, lock a tractor beam onto his ship.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Acknowledged. I can't establish a lock, Major. They must have some kind of deflectors we haven't seen before.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: They've entered the wormhole. We've lost them.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Got it. It looks like some kind of multiple locking system.

title: The Jem'Hadar
line: Even if I can break through the security barrier, how do you plan to get off the planet?

title: The Jem'Hadar

line: Yes.

title: The Search, Part One
line: Welcome home. To be continued...

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Our mission is to take the Defiant into the Gamma Quadrant and try to find the leaders of the Dominion, the Founders.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What the hell is wrong with Starfleet? How could they do this to him?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: This has been a long time coming, Major. Starfleet has never been happy with the Constable. I want him to stay as much as you do but he has to want to stay.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Ever since we've come into the Gamma Quadrant, I've had this feeling of being drawn somewhere, to a specific place. The Omarion Nebula.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The last time I saw the Defiant, she was dead in space and surrounded by Jem'Hadar ships.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Sisko? Bashir?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I don't know.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Welcome home. And now the conclusion.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You really are just like me, aren't you?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And you're saying this is where I'm from?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: This is your home.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I wish I could remember it.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's understandable that you cannot. You were still newly formed when you left us.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Newly formed? You mean I was an infant?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: An infant, yes.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I suspected as much. Tell me, do I have any family at all?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Of course.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'd like to meet them, if that's possible.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You already have. We are all part of the Great Link.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Is that all of us, or are there others?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Odo, this isn't a police investigation.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm aware of that, Major.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Then stop interrogating these people. This is the moment you've been waiting for all your life. Enjoy it. He really is happy to be here. Aren't you?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes, of course. It's just this is all very sudden.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And you have many questions.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes. Please, what exactly is this Great Link?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The Link is the very foundation of our society. It provides a meaning to our existence. It is the merging of thought and form, the sharing of idea and sensation. Is something wrong?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I've lived a very solitary life.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: That's unfortunate but necessary, as you'll learn in time. But now, that part of your life is over. You're home.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What are you doing?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Take it.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's not time. He isn't ready.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: He's been gone too long. He needs to remember, if only for a moment. Don't be afraid.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Odo. What have you done to him?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I allowed him to experience the Link.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Odo.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes, Major.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Are you all right? What happened?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm not sure. But I know one thing. She's right, I am home.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Commander's log, supplemental. It's been six days since we had to abandon the Defiant after the Jem'Hadar attack. We still don't know what happened to the rest of the crew. Doctor Bashir and I have plotted a course back to the wormhole. Whether the shuttle can get us back there or not is questionable at best. Our engines are failing, our external sensors are barely functioning and life support systems are at twenty percent and dropping.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: But other than that we couldn't be in better shape.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I thought you were sleeping.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: From the sound of things I wish I were.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Things could be worse.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I believe you. You think it's some kind of tractor beam?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Could be. I wish these sensors were working.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Now what?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Whoa. Hey, don't shoot. We surrender.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Chief. Dax.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I don't believe it. We thought you'd been captured by the Jem'Hadar.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Well, we had our doubts about ever seeing you again either, Julian.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: We've been searching for you for days.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What about the others?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: No sign of them yet, but we still have ships out looking for them.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Meanwhile, our orders are to get you back to DS Nine as soon as possible.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: There are big things happening there, Benjamin. I think you're in for a surprise.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: This is beautiful.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: How long do they plan on making us wait here?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's only been a few hours.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I finally return home and they still treat me like an outsider.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Believe me, you're not the outsider here. I am.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You? KIRA I'm the one they don't trust, not you.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: How perceptive, Major. If our history has taught us anything, it's to avoid contact with Solids whenever possible.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Solids?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Our name for mono-forms like yourself, who'll never know the joys of the Great Link.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I don't intend to stay long. There's a chance Sisko and the others survived the attack. I'm going to go back to the shuttle and try contacting them.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm sorry. I cannot allow you to send any communications from the planet's surface. They could be traced back here. We value our isolation.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes, of course.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Tell me, Odo, have you made good use of the arboretum?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: In what way?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: By assuming the various shapes surrounding you.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Why would I do that?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: To become a thing is to know a thing. To assume its form is to begin to understand its existence.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Understand it? How?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Living among the Solids has damaged you far worse than I realized. It has left you ignorant of the gifts you possess.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Then teach me what I need to know.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'll do what I can. But in the end, this is another journey you'll have to make on your own.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And when it is over you'll be ready to take your place in the Great Link.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Odo.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'd like to be alone if you don't mind.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: All right. But if you need me, I'll be in the shuttle trying to contact Sisko. Don't worry. When I was in the resistance I learned to camouflage subspace messages with quantum interference. I taught the method to Commander Sisko. If anyone intercepts the signal all they'll read is elevated levels of background radiation.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Good luck.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You too.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Well, Commander, it appears your mission was an even greater success than we hoped.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: So I'm told. Has the delegation from the Founders arrived on the station yet?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: They're already meeting with representatives from the Federation Council and a dozen other Alpha Quadrant alliances. We're hoping to have a treaty signed within a matter of days, and we have you to thank for it.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Actually it's Lieutenant Dax and Chief O'Brien who deserve most of the credit.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: We were lucky the Jem'Hadar handed us over to the Founders.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: We just had to convince them that we were serious about peace.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Actually, it didn't take that much convincing.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I suppose the only question is, can we trust them?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's a risk, I know, but both the Federation Council and Starfleet Command believe it's one worth taking. By the way, Commander, one of the Founders asked to see you the moment you arrived on the station.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Asked to see me?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: If you're not too busy.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Well, I suppose I could spare a few minutes.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Commander Sisko, come in. I've looked forward to meeting you. I am Borath.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And you're one of the Founders?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: That's correct. You seem surprised.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Not really. Only I hadn't realized till now I've already met one of your people.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You're referring to Eris, of course. Yes, she is one of us. Though she couldn't very well admit it while you were pointing a phaser at her. I'm glad to see you're not holding one now.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Do I need one?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Not at all. You seem skeptical.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Can you blame me?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: No. I realize you have no reason to trust the Dominion, but you must understand that we were only trying to defend ourselves.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: From what?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: We felt threatened by your incursions into the Gamma Quadrant.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And now?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Commander, you risked your life to bring us a message of peace and friendship. We chose to accept your offer. Would you rather we refused?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: No.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Good. Because believe me, Commander, an alliance between the Dominion and the Federation will be beneficial to both our people.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Doctor, welcome back.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Why thank you, Garak. It's good to be back.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Business keeping you busy?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The tailoring business, or the spy business? I'm joking, of course.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Of course.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I've missed you. I've been genuinely concerned for your safety. Lunch hasn't been the same without you.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: That's very kind of you to say so, Garak. Hopefully things'll start getting back to normal around here.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Oh, I doubt that's going to happen, Doctor. I doubt that very much.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And why is that?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: There's an old saying on Cardassia. Enemies make dangerous friends. And I fear the Dominion will make a very dangerous friend indeed.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I take it you're referring to the peace talks.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Exactly. I'm afraid these treaty negotiations are a mistake we're going to live to regret.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Is that your opinion or the opinion of the Cardassian Central Command?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The former, I assure you. The Central Command is very much in favor of this treaty. Which, as far as I'm concerned, only justifies my fears.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Well, I for one, hope you're worrying about nothing.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Sub-Commander T'Rul, are you all right?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm fine. I had a minor disagreement with some Starfleet security officers. They refused to allow me to speak with the Federation's negotiating team.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What did you want to talk to them about?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I wanted to protest the exclusion of the Romulan Empire from the treaty negotiations.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I wasn't aware the Romulans had been excluded.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Every great power in the Alpha Quadrant has been invited to participate except for us.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: There must be some mistake.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The mistake is thinking the Romulan empire will stand by and allow such a betrayal to go unchallenged. Believe me, Doctor, if a treaty is signed without our approval, it will mean war.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Still feel that I'm worrying about nothing, Doctor?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Computer, transmit a subspace signal using a narrow theta band frequency shifted into a background radiation domain.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Working.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I hope you're out there, Commander.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Unable to transmit signal due to external interference at all frequencies.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Identify source of interference.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Interference generated by thermal radiation from a subterranean power source.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Locate power source.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Power source is located four kilometers beneath the planet's surface, coordinates one two seven mark three.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Can you identify?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Unable to identify due to an unknown polymetallic substance within the surrounding rock.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Any luck, Major?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: No. Some kind of power source interfering with my signal. Do you have any idea what it could be?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I haven't a clue.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Are you all right?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I have spent the last two hours shape-shifting. Rocks, flowers, trees. I have been everything in that garden.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And nothing. Oh, I can become a rock, all right, but I have no more of an idea what it is to be a rock than I did before.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm not really sure what that means.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm not sure either, and that's unfortunate. Now if you'll excuse me, I have to return to my bucket.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Commander. Admiral Nechayev is here to see you.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Send her in.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You asked to see me, Commander?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I understand that the Romulans haven't been invited to the peace talks.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: That's correct.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I was wondering what prompted that decision.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The Founders requested that they be excluded.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Did they say why?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: They felt the Romulans would be a disruptive influence.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: More disruptive than the Cardassians?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: They seemed to think so. Do you have a problem with this, Commander?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Whether I have a problem with it isn't the point. It's the Romulans we have to worry about.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Commander, if this treaty is signed, and I'm confident it will be, we'll never have to worry about the Romulans again.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Are you sure of that?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Quite sure. After all, what chance would they have against the combined power of our new alliance?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: They wouldn't have much of a chance at all.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm glad we agree. Believe me, Commander, the Federation carefully weighed all the options before entering into these peace talks.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I realize that.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Then we have nothing further to discuss, do we?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Why do you dislike humanoids so much? I know they have their flaws, but I've found many of them to be kind, decent people.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Like Major Kira?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes, like Major Kira.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Then you've been more fortunate than most Changelings.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Changelings?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You recognize the term.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I've been called a Changeling on occasion.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's a name given to us by the Solids. They meant it as an insult, but in defiance we took it and made it our own.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Go on, please.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The Great Link tells us that many years ago our people roamed the stars, searching out other races so we could add to our knowledge of the galaxy. We went in peace, but too often we were met with suspicion, hatred and violence.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Why?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The Solids feared our metamorphic abilities, so we were beaten, hunted and killed. Finally we arrived here. And here, safe in our isolation, we made our home.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Tell me, why was I sent away?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Because even in our solitude we desired to learn more about the galaxy. You were one of a hundred infants we sent off to gain that knowledge for us.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: But how could you be sure that we'd find our way back here?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You had no choice. The urge to return home was implanted in your genetic makeup. And now, thanks to the passageway, you're the first to return to us. We weren't expecting you so soon.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: When were you expecting me?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Not for another three hundred years.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: How long was I away?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: A long time. But now all that matters now is that you're here.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's different than I imagined it would be.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Whatever you imagined, I promise it will be better.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Odo, are you here, Odo? I'm going to try to track down the source of the interference. If I can't find it and neutralize it, I'm going to have to leave here and try to find Sisko and the others. I'm really glad you made it home, Odo. I know everything is going to work out just fine. I don't believe it. I'm talking to a tree. You're probably not even here, are you?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Why would shape-shifters need a door? Kira to computer. Scan the area dead ahead of me for one hundred meters.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Unable to penetrate due to interference.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Excuse me. Pardon me. After you. Look out. Coming through. Sorry to keep you waiting, gentleman. That's two synthales. On the house.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What's put you in such a good humor?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I have inside information that the peace agreement is about to be finalized.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And where did you get this information, from one of your friends on the Federation Council?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: If you must know, I overheard two Jem'Hadar officers.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And you believed them?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I don't see why not. Oh, I know we got off to a rocky start but, they're not so bad really. I think they have the gene.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What gene?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The gambling gene. They've barely been on the station a week and already they can hardly drag themselves away from the dabo table.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: How fortunate for you.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: How fortunate for all of us. You see, I have a dream. A dream that one day all people, human, Jem'Hadar, Ferengi, Cardassians, will stand together in peace around my dabo tables.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You're a regular visionary, Quark.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I am, aren't I?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You're in my way.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Sorry.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Now look

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Gentlemen, please, remember my vision.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: That's enough.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: All right, what's going on here?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: He addressed me in a disrespectful tone.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: That's a lie.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Easy, Doctor. We're all friends here.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Tell him that.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'll see this doesn't happen again.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I expect you will.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Is that's it? You're just going to let him walk away?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Our orders are to give the Jem'Hadar a wide berth.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Look, I know what the orders say, but he attacked Chief O'Brien and we have rules here against that sort of thing.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm aware of station regulations, Doctor. However, the Jem'Hadar are not. We have to allow them some time to get used to our customs.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: So in the meantime, they're free to do whatever they want?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Remember that before you get into another brawl with them.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Dad, pass me the potatoes. Dad?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Yes, Jake.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The potatoes?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Oh.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Dad, is something wrong?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Not really. I'm just a little preoccupied, that's all. It's these Dominion negotiations.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What about them?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Well, it's all happening behind closed doors. I guess I just feel out of the loop.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: There's something going on, isn't there?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Like what?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: You tell me.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Come in.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Benjamin, did you know about this?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Know about what?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm being transferred to the Lexington. I'm their new Science Officer.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: There must be some mistake.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The orders are right here.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Let me see this. I don't believe it.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Bashir to Sisko.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Go ahead, Doctor.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Commander, I need to talk to you about the Jem'Hadar.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I want to know what the hell is going on.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Commander, I don't appreciate your barging in here.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I want to know why my Science Officer's been transferred without my consent. I want to know why my Chief of Operations is lying in the Infirmary while the Jem'Hadar who beat him is free to walk the station, and I want to know why the Federation is willing to risk a war with the Romulans to form an alliance with a group of people that we hardly know and barely trust.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Are you finished?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I haven't even begun.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Admiral, I think you should tell Commander Sisko what he wants to know.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: All right. I suppose he deserves to be the first to hear the news.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What news?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The Federation is pulling out of this sector. All Starfleet personnel currently stationed on DS Nine will be reassigned to other posts. Yourself included.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What about Bajor?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Our plans for Bajor are on hold for the time being. From now on Bajor will be the Dominion's responsibility. They'll be running this station.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And you're telling me the Bajorans have agreed to this?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: We're confident they'll have no objections.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And if they do object, what then? You send in the Jem'Hadar?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The Jem'Hadar are used only against our enemies. Bajor will be protected, Commander. We'll see to it.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What about the wormhole? Will they get to protect that too?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's the price of peace, Benjamin.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Well, if you ask me, the price is too damned high. What is the Federation supposed to get out of all this?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Our friendship. Isn't that enough?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And you, Benjamin, get a promotion. Captain Sisko. It's an important step toward that Admiralcy you've always wanted.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I want a chance to speak to the Federation negotiating team before this treaty is signed.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's too late for that, Ben. The treaty was signed late this afternoon.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's the beginning of a new era, Commander, and you helped make it possible. Congratulations.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Odo, I've been waiting for you.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Major, I have just had the most remarkable experience. For a few moments I actually felt what it was like to be an Arbazon Vulture. The air currents beneath my wings, the exhilaration of soaring above the treetops. Oh, it was all very stimulating.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I'm so happy for you.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I know you are.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: So, I guess this means you'll be staying here a while.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I've enjoyed working with you, Major.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I've enjoyed working with you too, Odo. But before we say goodbye, I need your help one last time.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Certainly.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Remember that power source I was telling you about?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: The one preventing you from trying to contact Commander Sisko.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: Well, I've found it.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: And what did it turn out to be?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I couldn't tell. There was a door blocking my path. I need you to help me open it.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: What kind of door?

title: The Search, Part Two
line: It's composed of some kind of metal the tricorder couldn't identify. Other than that, it's an ordinary door.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: That's odd. My people have no need for doors. They dislike taking humanoid form.

title: The Search, Part Two
line: I know.
