title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: How can we explain what happened to them?

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Give me your ID cards.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: It's in my pocket.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: We'll switch these with two of the casualties. As far as anybody knows, you both died here. Is that okay with you, Bell?

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Thanks.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: My pleasure.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Come on, let's get you out of here.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Anything else we can do for you?

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: There is one more thing.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Name it.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Tell people the truth about what happened here.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: I would've done that anyway. First officer's log, supplemental. Upon returning to the present with our missing crewmembers, we were relieved to discover that the timeline had been restored.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Come in.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: How do you feel?

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Better.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: I thought you might like to see this. I found it in the historical database.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: I'm not looking forward to explaining this to Starfleet Command.

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: Well, at least it's a good picture. You know, Commander, having seen a little of the twenty first century there is one thing I don't understand. How could they have let things get so bad?

title: Past Tense, Part Two
line: That's a good question. I wish I had an answer.

title: Life Support
line: Jake! Hi!

title: Life Support
line: Leanne. I thought you were on Bajor.

title: Life Support
line: I came back early. You know, I was just thinking about you.

title: Life Support
line: Really?

title: Life Support
line: Yeah. I passed by the Klingon restaurant and I was thinking about the time you and I and Orak were eating dinner

title: Life Support
line: And you ordered the gagh. How is Orak? I haven't talked to him in a while.

title: Life Support
line: We stopped seeing each other a few weeks ago.

title: Life Support
line: Oh.

title: Life Support
line: Yeah. So, are you doing anything tomorrow night?

title: Life Support
line: I'm supposed to play dom-jot with Nog.

title: Life Support
line: Oh.

title: Life Support
line: But they're not really firm plans. In fact, I was thinking of canceling them.

title: Life Support
line: Really? If you do cancel, would you be interested in dinner?

title: Life Support
line: Sure.

title: Life Support
line: Great. How about eighteen hundred at the Klingon restaurant?

title: Life Support
line: I'll be there. But this time we'll skip the gagh.

title: Life Support
line: Definitely. I'll see you then.

title: Life Support
line: Okay.

title: Life Support
line: Move aside! Look out! Move! Move!

title: Life Support
line: What have we got?

title: Life Support
line: Bajoran transport coming in. They had some kind of accident on board. They've got casualties.

title: Life Support
line: They're docking.

title: Life Support
line: We should have beamed the wounded directly to the Infirmary.

title: Life Support
line: They have a loose plasma coil. We couldn't beam through the radiation.

title: Life Support
line: Docking clamps secure. I'm opening the airlock. Stand back.

title: Life Support
line: Come on.

title: Life Support
line: This way, this way. It's all right.

title: Life Support
line: Here, I've got you.

title: Life Support
line: It's all right. Come along now.

title: Life Support
line: This way, Eminence.

title: Life Support
line: Kai Winn?

title: Life Support
line: The Vedek. Take care of the Vedek.

title: Life Support
line: Odo to Kira.

title: Life Support
line: Kira here.

title: Life Support
line: I think you should meet us in the Infirmary, Major.

title: Life Support
line: Vedek Bareil was on the transport. He's been injured.

title: Life Support
line: The report from the transport, sir.

title: Life Support
line: Give me the short version.

title: Life Support
line: There was a molecular fracture in one of the warp plasma conduits. It was only a matter of time before it gave way. Once it collapsed the entire relay system exploded.

title: Life Support
line: Was it sabotage?

title: Life Support
line: I don't think so.

title: Life Support
line: Why would you suspect sabotage?

title: Life Support
line: I would prefer to discuss that with the Emissary in private.

title: Life Support
line: Put a pressor field on that artery.

title: Life Support
line: The arterial disruption is too severe the pressor can't stop the hemorrhaging.

title: Life Support
line: All right. Clamp off the artery and then increase the plasma level to maximum.

title: Life Support
line: Cardiac arrest.

title: Life Support
line: Clear.

title: Life Support
line: He can't take much more of that.

title: Life Support
line: The arterial pressure is falling.

title: Life Support
line: I see it.

title: Life Support
line: The neurotransmitter levels are falling too.

title: Life Support
line: Two cc's cordrazine.

title: Life Support
line: Doctor?

title: Life Support
line: Do it.

title: Life Support
line: Synaptic failure. Apply direct neuro-stimulation to the brainstem.

title: Life Support
line: Thank you. Vedek Bareil and I were on our way to a secret meeting with a member of the Cardassian Central Command. It was my intention to open talks between Bajor and Cardassia that would lead to a treaty and to a final peace settlement.

title: Life Support
line: You have been negotiating peace with Cardassia?

title: Life Support
line: The Prophets teach us that while violence may keep an enemy at bay, only peace can make him a friend.

title: Life Support
line: How long has this been going on?

title: Life Support
line: Vedek Bareil has been working to set up this meeting with Legate Turrel for the past five months. They've discussed issues ranging from war reparations to the exchange of ambassadors. There's even the possibility that the Cardassians will issue a formal apology for the pain and suffering inflicted on the Bajoran people during the occupation. I was on my way to our first face-to-face meeting when we had the accident.

title: Life Support
line: Please, don't take this the wrong way, but I never would've guessed that you would be the one to bring such a bold vision of peace to Bajor.

title: Life Support
line: A large share of the credit goes to Vedek Bareil. Without him, the talks could have never come this far.

title: Life Support
line: It sounds like you've developed a deeper appreciation for Vedek Bareil.

title: Life Support
line: I must admit he has been a loyal and trustworthy aide since the election. I'm not sure I could have been as forgiving if I'd been in his place. These talks were Bareil's idea. He's guided me through them, and without him in the future, these talks may never resume.

title: Life Support
line: I'm sorry. The radiation severely damaged his neural pathways. I did everything I could.

title: Life Support
line: I know you did. Did he ever regain consciousness?

title: Life Support
line: No. I don't think he suffered.

title: Life Support
line: Thank you, Doctor. I'm on duty in Ops. Excuse me.

title: Life Support
line: Kira. I think they can get along without you in Ops today.

title: Life Support
line: Maybe, but I need to be there. I appreciate your concern but I'll grieve in my own way in my own time.

title: Life Support
line: We're ready to begin the autopsy, Doctor.

title: Life Support
line: Release the stasis field. Let's begin with a neural scan. I want to map his central axonal pathways, find out where the breakdown began.

title: Life Support
line: Shall I begin taking neural tissue samples?

title: Life Support
line: Looks like the damage began in the parietal lobe, spread through the rest of the brain in a retrograde manner.

title: Life Support
line: Wait a minute. A neuron just fired in his cerebral cortex. There it is again. His nerves. His nerves are still transmitting electrical impulses to his brain

title: Life Support
line: How can that be? His brain activity level is zero. His nervous system should be completely inactive.

title: Life Support
line: I don't know but it means his body's still capable of sending messages to the brain, even though the brain can't process them. The radiation he was exposed to might have fortified his peripheral cell membranes. If we can regenerate his pathways with his own neuron cells, we might be able to revive him.

title: Life Support
line: What about brain damage? There's been no oxygen to his brain for almost forty minutes.

title: Life Support
line: But he's been in stasis for most of that time. That, combined with the strengthening of his cell membranes might buy us the time we need.

title: Life Support
line: We'll have to direct a burst of electrical energy into his cerebral cortex. If the burst is the proper intensity, it should create a cascade effect within the brain and the neurons might resume their normal firing pattern. Okay. Let's close up the cranial cavity.

title: Life Support
line: The neurogenic stimulator is in place. Let's try a fifty millivolt burst.

title: Life Support
line: Increase it to sixty.

title: Life Support
line: Seventy.

title: Life Support
line: That's five millivolts above what normal tissue can withstand. It'll burn out his cerebral cortex.

title: Life Support
line: If I'm right, the inaprovaline drug I gave him should provide additional resistance against the excess electro-stimulation. Seventy.

title: Life Support
line: Doctor!

title: Life Support
line: Well, it's a little early to tell, but I'm hoping he'll make a full recovery. He should be back on his feet again in a few weeks.

title: Life Support
line: You say that so calmly, but it's not every doctor that can lose a patient and then has him back on his feet in a few weeks.

title: Life Support
line: Indeed, you are too modest. You've performed nothing less than a miracle here. The Prophets must walk with you, Doctor.

title: Life Support
line: Well, I and the Prophets, were lucky that the ionizing radiation left a residual signature on Bareil's axonal pathways. That's what really made this possible.

title: Life Support
line: Whoever deserves the credit, Doctor, I am grateful.

title: Life Support
line: And I am grateful you were not taken from us, Vedek Bareil.

title: Life Support
line: My work here is not yet finished.

title: Life Support
line: No, it is not. We must resume the negotiations immediately. We can't risk losing the momentum we've established. I would like to send a coded message to Legate Turrel and invite him to come to DS Nine to continue the talks.

title: Life Support
line: Wait a minute. Bareil's in no condition to conduct negotiations.

title: Life Support
line: Bareil will simply be advising me. I will conduct the actual talks.

title: Life Support
line: I'll allow it as long as your visits don't tire him.

title: Life Support
line: Agreed. Vedek, we will talk again soon.

title: Life Support
line: Eminence.

title: Life Support
line: So, are we going to be playing springball next month?

title: Life Support
line: You bet, although I'm afraid I'll have an unfair advantage.

title: Life Support
line: You mean playing against a dead man?

title: Life Support
line: No. I've been practicing.

title: Life Support
line: My Dad said that you were looking for me.

title: Life Support
line: Yeah. It's about tomorrow night

title: Life Support
line: Don't worry, I've already taken care of that. I met these three Terrellians who were bragging about how great they are at dom-jot. So I arranged a game, us against them.

title: Life Support
line: Nog, we have a little problem.

title: Life Support
line: No, we don't. I guarantee we'll beat them.

title: Life Support
line: It's not that. I just can't make it tomorrow night.

title: Life Support
line: But it has to be tomorrow night. They're leaving the next day.

title: Life Support
line: I, I made other plans.

title: Life Support
line: What could be more important than dom-jot?

title: Life Support
line: I have a date.

title: Life Support
line: Oh. Well, that's different.

title: Life Support
line: It is?

title: Life Support
line: Yeah. Money is money, but women are better.

title: Life Support
line: Is that a Rule of Acquisition?

title: Life Support
line: It's a personal rule. So, who is she?

title: Life Support
line: Leanne.

title: Life Support
line: Leanne! Way to go, Jake. So, what is the name of my date? I hope she's as cute as Leanne.

title: Life Support
line: Your date?

title: Life Support
line: She has a friend, right?

title: Life Support
line: I'm sure she does.

title: Life Support
line: Then tell her to bring her along.

title: Life Support
line: Nog, that's not what I had in mind.

title: Life Support
line: That's because you were confused. Would you rather the three of us go out?

title: Life Support
line: When you put it that way.

title: Life Support
line: Exactly. Just one thing, Jake. You're still pretty new at this dating business. Just promise me you won't do anything to embarrass me.

title: Life Support
line: I'll do my best.

title: Life Support
line: Ah, this'll be great. Maybe I'll even wash my lobes.

title: Life Support
line: I suggest that we put off discussion of the Cardassians returning the Orbs until diplomatic relations have been established.

title: Life Support
line: That would only delay an inevitable argument.

title: Life Support
line: But it will give the peace process a chance to grow. Once the Cardassians are invested in the process, it may be easier to discuss these matters.

title: Life Support
line: Very well.

title: Life Support
line: A wise decision, Eminence.

title: Life Support
line: I hope so, Vedek Bareil. The first meeting with Turrel is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon. I will see you again before then.

title: Life Support
line: I take it you're not here to deliver a good report, Doctor?

title: Life Support
line: In order to revive you, I had to flood your nervous system with neurogenic radiation. Unfortunately, this has caused some kind of selective vaso-constriction of your arteries. The result is an inadequate blood flow to your internal organs.

title: Life Support
line: So what do we do?

title: Life Support
line: We'd like to place you back into stasis, do some research on your condition.

title: Life Support
line: For how long?

title: Life Support
line: I don't know yet. Days, weeks even months.

title: Life Support
line: Maybe even years?

title: Life Support
line: Maybe.

title: Life Support
line: I'm sorry, Doctor, that's not acceptable. I can't allow myself to be put in storage when my people need me. I don't want to wake to a Bajor still haunted by the memory of the occupation.

title: Life Support
line: I realize how important these talks are to Bajor, but as your physician my duty is to you first.

title: Life Support
line: And I have a duty to Bajor. Please, help me heal my people. It's the only thing that matters to me.

title: Life Support
line: There is an experimental drug called Vasokin which would increase the blood flow to your organs and might enable you to function normally for a while. But there is a great deal of risk attached.

title: Life Support
line: What sort of risk?

title: Life Support
line: In twenty two percent of cases, Vasokin has severely damaged the patient's lungs, kidneys, even heart. Sometimes the brain. In your condition, it could even be fatal.

title: Life Support
line: But it would allow me to function normally for the next few days?

title: Life Support
line: Yes. But why risk your life for a few days?

title: Life Support
line: I have no great desire to die, Doctor, but I am determined to carry out the will of the Prophets as long as I am able, and I cannot carry out their will if I am unconscious in some stasis tube. Please, begin the Vasokin treatment.

title: Life Support
line: All right. We'll start this afternoon. I only hope we don't regret this.

title: Life Support
line: So do I.

title: Life Support
line: Captain's log, stardate 48498.4. Legate Turrel has arrived aboard the station to resume the negotiations. Vedek Bareil suggested that I sit in on the talks as an impartial observer, and Kai Winn has agreed.

title: Life Support
line: Perhaps you didn't hear me. There are no Bajoran prisoners left in Cardassian hands.

title: Life Support
line: Maybe we should redefine our terms. Perhaps there are no official prisoners but are there be a number of, shall we say, detainees?

title: Life Support
line: There are, of course, people being detained at the Justice Ministry for crimes against the state, but that is a discussion for another time. Now, I would like to discuss what you've called war reparations. We would be willing to pay for the destruction of all Bajoran property incurred during the occupation as long as you would be willing to return to us all Cardassian property and equipment left behind on Bajor.

title: Life Support
line: What sort of property?

title: Life Support
line: I can provide you with lists of material, equipment, as long as we have an agreement in principle that anything of Cardassian origin does still belong to the Cardassian people.

title: Life Support
line: I will consider your offer.

title: Life Support
line: Good. Shall we take a recess?

title: Life Support
line: He's up to something.

title: Life Support
line: That much seems clear.

title: Life Support
line: But what? Why is he insisting on this principle of his? I need Bareil. He's the only one who knows the entire negotiating record. Bareil has been talking with Turrel for months. He understands him, respects him. I think he even likes him.

title: Life Support
line: I'm afraid you may have to face the possibility that Bareil may not be able to help you much longer.

title: Life Support
line: I was chosen by the Prophets to lead our people into a new era. I know that. But I was not meant to be in a room with a Cardassian debating legalisms and diplomatic nuances. I can't do this without Bareil. If he dies, then peace with Cardassia dies with him.

title: Life Support
line: My father used to take me to the wilderness preserves on Vulcan, so for years I thought their planet was like, animals and plants everywhere. I had no idea there were people on Vulcan.

title: Life Support
line: Boy, Jake, she talks a lot for a female.

title: Life Support
line: Excuse me?

title: Life Support
line: Riska ,weren't you telling me your uncle runs a bar on Osinar Six? You know, Nog's uncle runs this bar.

title: Life Support
line: Is that right?

title: Life Support
line: Let's not make foolish conversation. Just sit there and look beautiful.

title: Life Support
line: Nog, what do you think you're doing?

title: Life Support
line: I think I know how to handle females. Jake, you know, I've been thinking. After we're done eating, we could take the females to the holosuites. I borrowed one of my uncle's private programs, The Massacre on Ferris Six. We could spend an hour pillaging and looting the frightened townspeople.

title: Life Support
line: I don't think so.

title: Life Support
line: No one's asking you to think, my dear. Here, make yourself useful. Cut up my food for me.

title: Life Support
line: You must be joking.

title: Life Support
line: She's so dumb. She's perfect.

title: Life Support
line: That's it.

title: Life Support
line: Wait, you're not leaving?

title: Life Support
line: I suppose you want me to sit here and cut your food for you, too?

title: Life Support
line: I never said anything about cutting

title: Life Support
line: I hope you and your friend enjoy your holosuite. Come on.

title: Life Support
line: Nog!

title: Life Support
line: Don't say another word, Jake. I think you've done enough damage for one night.

title: Life Support
line: Me?

title: Life Support
line: Yeah, you. You were treating my female as if she was an equal.

title: Life Support
line: And you were behaving like an idiot. This is the last time I'll ever do a favor for you. From now on you get your own dates.

title: Life Support
line: And you can find someone else to play dom-jot with.

title: Life Support
line: Fine!

title: Life Support
line: Good!

title: Life Support
line: Turrel is trying to get a concession from you that I already rejected. Tell him that the question of Cardassian property on Bajor was already dealt with in the Armistice talks four years ago. Don't worry, he'll still pay the reparations.

title: Life Support
line: What about this question of mining rights? His attention has been wandering. He's in pain. Give him more of the drug.

title: Life Support
line: He's had enough.

title: Life Support
line: Then you'll need to give him something else. The negotiations resume in less than six hours and we still have forty pages.

title: Life Support
line: Listen to me. I don't care about your negotiations, and I don't care about your treaty. All I care about is my patient, and at the moment he needs more medical care and less politics. Now, you can either leave here willingly or I'll call security and have you thrown out.

title: Life Support
line: You won't need to call them. I'll do it myself.

title: Life Support
line: Put yourself in the hands of the Prophets, Bareil. They will not forsake you.

title: Life Support
line: Yes, Eminence.

title: Life Support
line: Is there anything I can do?

title: Life Support
line: Just be here. I'm beginning to dislike seeing that look on your face, Doctor.

title: Life Support
line: As I feared, the Vasokin has already damaged your internal organs.

title: Life Support
line: What happens now?

title: Life Support
line: I can replace the damaged organs with artificial implants, but as long as you're taking the drug I can't guarantee that the damage won't spread. I think you should reconsider letting me put you in stasis.

title: Life Support
line: I'm afraid my mind's made up. Just get me through the negotiations. I must carry out the will of the Prophets. Please. Whatever it takes, just do it.

title: Life Support
line: Are you going to call security and have me removed from this room now, Doctor?

title: Life Support
line: It hadn't occurred to me. Yet.

title: Life Support
line: How is Bareil?

title: Life Support
line: The organ replacement surgery went well. He's still unconscious, but he should be awake within the hour.

title: Life Support
line: Oh, good. There are still several points I have to discuss with him before the next negotiating session.

title: Life Support
line: That's why I'm here. When you see Bareil, I want you to tell him that you don't need him, that you can complete these negotiations without him.

title: Life Support
line: But I do need him, Doctor.

title: Life Support
line: I realize that. But I want you to tell him that you don't.

title: Life Support
line: You seem to be asking me to lie.

title: Life Support
line: I'm asking you to free Bareil of his obligations to you. The only way he'll accept that is if you tell him he's no longer needed, that you can go on without him. Now, if that's a lie, then so be it.

title: Life Support
line: That doesn't sound like a Starfleet officer.

title: Life Support
line: I'm a doctor first. And right now, I'm trying to give my patient his best chance to live. The only way to do that is to put him in stasis. Bareil knows that, but his desire to complete these negotiations is so strong that he's forcing me to keep him conscious and mentally alert, even though it may kill him.

title: Life Support
line: None of us wants that to happen, Doctor. But if I'm not mistaken, the decision regarding Bareil's treatment is up to him.

title: Life Support
line: Yes. As the patient, it is his right to make that choice. But I'm asking you to help me change his mind. Eminence, you're the Kai. These are your negotiations. Let this be your moment in history. Finish the talks on your own and you won't have to share the credit with anyone.

title: Life Support
line: You say that as though success is guaranteed, Doctor.

title: Life Support
line: Of course. If the talks fail, you'll need someone to accept the blame. A scapegoat. You're a coward. You're afraid to stand alone.

title: Life Support
line: Bareil's already made his decision, Doctor. I won't interfere. And Doctor? I won't forget what you've said here.

title: Life Support
line: Neither will I.

title: Life Support
line: So, you never told me about your double-date.

title: Life Support
line: Not much to tell

title: Life Support
line: That's not what I hear. Quark tells me that you and Nog aren't speaking to each other.

title: Life Support
line: You should've seen the way he acted, Dad. He was acting like a spoiled brat. I've never been so embarrassed. I don't think Leanne will ever speak to me again.

title: Life Support
line: So what did he do?

title: Life Support
line: All kinds of stupid things. Riska couldn't even say two words without him telling her to be quiet. And he insisted that she cut up his food for him. He was treating her like she was some kind of slave.

title: Life Support
line: Sounds like he's acting like a Ferengi to me. You can't blame him for that.

title: Life Support
line: Well, in that case, maybe you were right all along.

title: Life Support
line: About what?

title: Life Support
line: You once said that Humans and Ferengis are too different to ever really be friends.

title: Life Support
line: I remember saying that. And you know what? I was wrong. You and Nog proved that. Sure, you have your cultural differences, but there's a real bond between you.

title: Life Support
line: Well, I know one thing. I'm never going to set him up on a date again.

title: Life Support
line: I think you two should talk this over before it becomes too big a problem.

title: Life Support
line: I'm not sure Nog is going to be willing to talk to me so soon.

title: Life Support
line: Well, I guess you'll have to do something to get his attention.

title: Life Support
line: What happened?

title: Life Support
line: I don't know.

title: Life Support
line: Two cc's morphenolog. It's all right, it's all right. You're getting help. You're getting help. I thought I made it clear there were to be no visitors for the next three hours.

title: Life Support
line: It's not her fault, Doctor. Bareil called me himself. He said he had some ideas on the treaty.

title: Life Support
line: And you just couldn't wait to hear them, could you. His left temporal lobe is showing signs of massive synaptic failure. Well, I hope you got all the advice you needed, Eminence, because the Vasokin has damaged his brain and that damage is irreversible.

title: Life Support
line: Will he regain consciousness?

title: Life Support
line: Not in his present condition.

title: Life Support
line: You were able to replace some of his internal organs with artificial implants. Could you do something similar with the damaged parts of his brain?

title: Life Support
line: It's hard to say with any certainty. There's still a great deal about the way the brain operates we don't understand. One of my professors at medical school used to say that the brain had a spark of life that can't be replicated. If we begin to replace parts of Bareil's brain with artificial implants, that spark may be lost.

title: Life Support
line: But you're saying if we don't do it, Bareil will never regain consciousness and he'll die.

title: Life Support
line: I think we need to consider what Bareil would want us to do.

title: Life Support
line: Vedek Bareil wanted these negotiations to be completed, no matter what the cost.

title: Life Support
line: With all due respect, your Eminence, you're hardly an impartial observer here. You have a personal interest in these talks.

title: Life Support
line: There is more at stake than one man's life.

title: Life Support
line: One man's life is all I'm concerned with at the moment.

title: Life Support
line: I think she's right, Julian. I think Bareil would want the positronic implants.

title: Life Support
line: Kira, if I go through with this, the man who wakes up may not be the man you used to know.

title: Life Support
line: I realize that, but I know how important this is to him, and I know he wouldn't want to just be put into stasis indefinitely, waiting for some medical solution that may never come. Do the surgery, Julian. Let him finish what he started.

title: Life Support
line: Mister Sisko.

title: Life Support
line: Odo, I'd like you to do me a favor. I want to be arrested.

title: Life Support
line: Argh! This is outrageous! I didn't steal anything from a Tholian Ambassador!

title: Life Support
line: Just another innocent man arrested for a crime he didn't commit.

title: Life Support
line: What is he doing here?

title: Life Support
line: As if you didn't know. Your accomplice here has also denied involvement, but I have an eyewitness who saw both of you breaking into the Tholian Ambassador's quarters last night.

title: Life Support
line: I don't even know what a Tholian looks like!

title: Life Support
line: Tell it to the Magistrate.

title: Life Support
line: At least put me in my own cell.

title: Life Support

line: Now if you don't mind, Lieutenant, I'd like to get started.

title: Heart of Stone
line: How long do you think it's going to be before the generator finds the right frequency?

title: Heart of Stone
line: It's hard to say. It could take hours.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I don't suppose there's any way to speed things up? I didn't think so.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Don't worry, Major. I have every intention of getting us back to the station by tomorrow night. Chief O'Brien is counting on it.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What does O'Brien have to do with it?

title: Heart of Stone
line: We have an appointment.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What kind of appointment? Talk to me, Odo. It helps pass the time.

title: Heart of Stone
line: The Chief and I are supposed to go kayaking together in a holosuite.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You're kidding. How did he talk you into that one?

title: Heart of Stone
line: He didn't talk me into anything. It's really quite enjoyable.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You mean you've done it before?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Twice. He invited me one evening and, seeing I had no plans, I accepted.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I'm sorry. I'm just having trouble imagining the two of you together in a boat.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Well if it helps any, he's the one who does all the singing.

title: Heart of Stone
line: He sings?

title: Heart of Stone
line: He says it's necessary to establish a smooth paddling rhythm.

title: Heart of Stone
line: This gets better and better. What kind of songs does he sing?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Ancient human sea chanties, mostly. He's particularly fond of one called 'Louie, Louie'.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I never pictured O'Brien as a nautical type.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Next to his work and his family, shooting the rapids is his favorite activity. He's had the holoprogram since he was on the Enterprise.

title: Heart of Stone
line: How long do these boat trips usually take?

title: Heart of Stone
line: That depends.

title: Heart of Stone
line: On what?

title: Heart of Stone
line: On how many times we capsize.

title: Heart of Stone
line: It must be a very difficult program.

title: Heart of Stone
line: It's extremely difficult. According to him, he's dislocated his shoulder a half dozen times trying to make it down those rapids.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Then why does he keep doing it?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Because he loves it. And it's been my observation that you humanoids have a hard time giving up the things you love, no matter how much they might hurt you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I'm glad you're here, Odo.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I'm glad I'm here, too.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo!

title: Heart of Stone
line: Major?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I'm all right. What about the generator?

title: Heart of Stone
line: It's fine. It still hasn't found the right frequency to shatter the crystal.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Tell it to hurry. A couple more tremors like that last one and this whole cave is going to collapse.

title: Heart of Stone
line: We'll just have to make sure that doesn't happen. After all, we've been in worse situations than this one and come out all right.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Name three. I can't think of any either.

title: Heart of Stone
line: No, it's not that. It's just that that wasn't the response I expected.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What do you mean?

title: Heart of Stone
line: In the detective novels Chief O'Brien gives me to read, when the hero says, we've been in tougher situations than this one, his friends always agree.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I never read any of those books.

title: Heart of Stone
line: There must be some humanoid platitude I can use to cheer you up.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I don't have much use for platitudes, Odo. I'd rather face the truth of a situation and go on from there.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I feel the same way.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I know you do. That's why you and I get along so well.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I suppose it is. But in this case, the truth is we're going to get you out of here, Major. And that's no platitude.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I must admit, this is impressive work.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Incredible is more like it. He inventoried the whole cargo bay in under five hours.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You're sure he didn't have any help?

title: Heart of Stone
line: According to the internal sensors, no one else entered that cargo bay the entire time he was there.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I guess he did learn something working in his uncle's storeroom. I assume that all our equipment is where it's supposed to be?

title: Heart of Stone
line: If you're asking if he stole anything, the answer is no. He even found some things we missed on our last inventory.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Okay, so now we know he's a hard worker. The question remains. Why does he want to join Starfleet?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I have no idea.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I don't understand it. I've run through the entire harmonic spectrum and none of the frequencies have had any effect on the crystal. It's almost as if the structure of the crystal is mutating to keep us from finding the right frequency.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Yes, Major. I wish there was something else I could do.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Just keep talking to me.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What do you want me to say?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Anything. Tell me a story.

title: Heart of Stone
line: A story?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I know. Tell me how you got your name.

title: Heart of Stone
line: My name? Now that you mention it, that is an amusing story.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Tell it to me.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Well, as you know, when Doctor Mora first brought me to his laboratory, it was under Cardassian supervision. All specimens had to be clearly labeled in Cardassian, so the overseers would always know what the scientists were working on. Since no one was exactly sure what I was, Mora labeled me Unknown Sample, which the overseer translated into Cardassian as Odo'ital.

title: Heart of Stone
line: So, your name is Unknown Sample?

title: Heart of Stone
line: No, no. Odo'ital literally means the word 'nothing'. Even after it became clear that I was sentient, the Bajoran scientists kept calling me that. As a joke, they split it into two words like a Bajoran name, Odo Ital, which eventually got shortened.

title: Heart of Stone
line: To Odo.

title: Heart of Stone
line: But the thing is, for the longest time, whenever anyone would use my name, the first thing I'd think of was what it meant. Nothing. What better way to describe me? I had no family, no friends, no place where I belonged. I thought it was the most appropriate name anyone could give me. And then I met you. And the others. Sisko, Dax, even Quark. And now, when I hear one of you call me Odo, I no longer think of myself as nothing. I think of myself as me. I'm sorry, Major. I guess that story wasn't as amusing as I'd hoped it would be.

title: Heart of Stone
line: No. I liked it very much. The ultrasonic generator isn't going to work, is it?

title: Heart of Stone
line: No, I'm afraid it's not.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I don't suppose you have any other ideas.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I wish I had.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Neither do I.

title: Heart of Stone
line: It doesn't make sense. The ultrasonic generator should have worked. Something's not right here.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo, you've done your best. It's time for you to go.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Go?

title: Heart of Stone
line: This place is going to collapse at any minute. That Maquis is probably dead from one of the cave-ins. There's nothing more you can do for me.

title: Heart of Stone
line: If you're asking me to leave?

title: Heart of Stone
line: As your superior officer, I'm telling you to take the runabout and get the hell off this moon. That's an order.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo, why are you still standing there? I told you to get out of here.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I'm not leaving.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Constable, I gave you a direct order.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You can order me all you want. As of now, I'm resigning my commission.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo, if you stay here, you'll die.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You don't know that for certain. And even if it were true, I'm not going to abandon you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I want you to get out of here.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Don't you understand? I can't.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You have to. Odo, please.

title: Heart of Stone
line: No. I won't leave you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Why?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Because! Because I'm in love with you. So, now you know.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo, I'm in love with you too.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You wanted to see me, Commander?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Nog, I've given your request a lot of thought.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I appreciate that, Commander.

title: Heart of Stone
line: But I'm afraid I'm going to have to turn you down.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Turn me down? Why? Did I do something wrong?

title: Heart of Stone
line: It's not anything you did, Nog. You're just not Academy material. Here. This belongs to you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Commander, can't we talk about this?

title: Heart of Stone
line: There's nothing to talk about. We both know you'd never make it through the Academy. You couldn't handle the workload or the discipline. You wouldn't last two weeks.

title: Heart of Stone
line: That's not true. I'm a hard worker. I proved that to you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: It doesn't matter. And I'm not going to put my reputation on the line just to satisfy some whim of yours.

title: Heart of Stone
line: It's not just a whim. I'm serious about joining Starfleet.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I don't have time for this, Nog. Now whatever little scheme you had, you can forget it. I'm not giving you that letter.

title: Heart of Stone
line: It's not a joke or a scheme. I want to join Starfleet. I want it more than anything I've ever wanted anything in my life.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You're a Ferengi. Why would you want to be in Starfleet? Where's the profit in it?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I don't care about profit.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Then what do you care about? Come on, Nog, tell me. Why is it so damned important for you to get into Starfleet? Why are you doing this?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Because I don't want to end up like my father.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Your father.

title: Heart of Stone
line: That's right. My father. He's been chasing profit his whole life, and what has it gotten him? Nothing. And you know why? Because he doesn't have the lobes. And neither do I.

title: Heart of Stone
line: And a Ferengi without profit

title: Heart of Stone
line: Is no Ferengi at all.

title: Heart of Stone
line: The eighteenth Rule of Acquisition.

title: Heart of Stone
line: My father is a mechanical genius. He could've been Chief Engineer of a starship if he'd had the opportunity. But he went into business, like a good Ferengi. The only thing is, he's not a good Ferengi, not when it comes to acquiring profit. So now all he has to live for is the slim chance that someday, somehow, he might be able to take over my uncle's bar. Well, I'm not going to make the same mistake. I want to do something with my life. Something worthwhile.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Like joining Starfleet.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I may not have an instinct for business, but I have my father's hands and my uncle's tenacity. I know I've got something to offer, I just need the chance to prove it.

title: Heart of Stone
line: All right. I'll see that you get that chance.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You're going to recommend me to Starfleet Academy?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I'll send the letter the first thing tomorrow morning.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Commander, I don't know how to thank you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa. Don't thank me yet. You still have a lot of work ahead of you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Don't worry. You're never going to regret this.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Yes, Major.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You haven't said a word to me in over an hour.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I've just been going over a few things in my mind.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I'm sorry I waited so long to tell you how I feel about you. If I'd told you earlier, maybe things would've been different.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Ah.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What are you smiling about?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I think I've finally figured out what's going on here. This whole situation hasn't seemed right since the beginning. There've been too many coincidences, too many unanswered questions.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Are you still trying to prove that this is all some kind of conspiracy?

title: Heart of Stone
line: You said the Maquis was standing here when he shot at you?

title: Heart of Stone
line: That's right.

title: Heart of Stone
line: How tall was he? My height?

title: Heart of Stone
line: No. Maybe shorter.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Like this?

title: Heart of Stone
line: More or less. Why does it matter anyway?

title: Heart of Stone
line: It matters because from this position, you're blocking those phaser hits. There's no way someone standing here could hit those rocks without hitting you first.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Maybe he was standing somewhere else.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Maybe. Or maybe you were lying to me. Which makes two times you've lied to me today.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What are you talking about?

title: Heart of Stone
line: You lied when you said you were shot at by the Maquis. And you lied when you said you loved me.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I do love you.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I wish you did, but you don't. Remember Major, I pride myself on my ability to observe human nature, and I've watched you for the past three years. In all that time I never saw any indication that you had those kinds of feelings for me. You like me. You think of me as a close friend. But love? I'm afraid not.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Maybe I told I loved you because I thought it would make you feel better. Because I thought that's what you wanted to hear.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You're lying again. The Kira I know has far too much regard for our friendship to lie to me, even for the best of reasons.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo, I can explain.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Good. And you can start by telling me who you are and what you've done with Kira.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Well done, Odo. You really are quite a skilful investigator.

title: Heart of Stone
line: And you're quite a skilful changeling.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You still have much to learn.

title: Heart of Stone
line: If you want to share your wisdom, tell me where Major Kira is.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Close by.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You were the fugitive we were chasing, weren't you?

title: Heart of Stone
line: That's correct.

title: Heart of Stone
line: How did you get your hands on a Maquis ship?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Now, Odo, you really can't expect me to give you all the answers.

title: Heart of Stone
line: But why did you lead us here? Why replace Kira?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I needed to understand why you chose to live with the Solids rather than your own people. I suspected it had something to do with Major Kira. Now I'm certain of it.

title: Heart of Stone
line: So your plan was to let me think she died. You thought that would take away my link to the Solids.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Then you would return to us.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I assure you, nothing will ever make me do that.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I wouldn't be so sure.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Tell me where she is.

title: Heart of Stone
line: And if I don't, then what? You'll shoot me? No changeling has ever harmed another.

title: Heart of Stone
line: There's always a first time.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Major Kira is down that tunnel, two hundred meters south of here. Save her, if it suits you, but it won't make any difference. She is never going to love you. How could she? You are a changeling.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Major, wake up.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Odo, what happened? What am I doing here?

title: Heart of Stone
line: It's a long story. Right now we have to get you back to the Mekong.

title: Heart of Stone
line: There's one thing I still don't understand. If that Founder was trying to test your allegiance to the Solids, why did she impersonate me?

title: Heart of Stone
line: I suppose it's because you happened to be with me in the runabout. It could have just as easily have been Commander Sisko or Doctor Bashir.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What finally made you realize the truth?

title: Heart of Stone
line: She made eventually a mistake. She said something I know you would never say.

title: Heart of Stone
line: What was that?

title: Heart of Stone
line: Just a slip of the tongue. Nothing important.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I tell you, I won't stand for it. No nephew of mine is going to disgrace our family name by joining Starfleet.

title: Heart of Stone
line: But Uncle Quark

title: Heart of Stone
line: My mind is made up. I forbid it.

title: Heart of Stone
line: No, you don't.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Rom, stay out of this.

title: Heart of Stone
line: I will not. When it comes to the bar you may be in charge, but when it comes to my son, I make the decisions.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Fine. You tell him he can't go.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Nog. Good luck. I would be proud to have a son in Starfleet.

title: Heart of Stone
line: You're both insane.

title: Heart of Stone
line: Like father, like son.

title: Destiny
line: I've assigned these quarters to the senior Cardassian scientist. Her name is Ulani. Her colleague Gilora has the adjacent room.

title: Destiny
line: It's warm in here. I take it you've reset the environmental controls.

title: Destiny
line: I also had Chief O'Brien reprogram the replicators to provide Cardassian food.

title: Destiny
line: Security measures?

title: Destiny
line: I've assigned two of my people to follow the Cardassians at all times.

title: Destiny
line: Fine. Have them keep their distance. I want the Cardassians to feel like guests, not prisoners.

title: Destiny
line: Commander, there are still elements opposed to the peace treaty between Cardassia and Bajor on both sides. We have to be prepared for trouble.

title: Destiny
line: I realize that. But while the Cardassians are here, I want the Bajorans to get used to seeing them walking on the Promenade, buying from their shops, eating from their restaurants, getting to know them as something other than brutal overseers.

title: Destiny
line: I just received the final update from the Cardassians on the transceiver they designed for the communications relay.

title: Destiny
line: How does it look?

title: Destiny
line: I'm still not convinced it's going to work.

title: Destiny
line: The Cardassians seem sure that it will.

title: Destiny
line: I hope they're right.

title: Destiny
line: Whose quarters are these? Gilora's or Ulani's?

title: Destiny
line: Ulani's. And how do you know their names? I was just informed an hour ago.

title: Destiny
line: Odo, please. I have a bottle of Kanar for each of them, along with a personal invitation to Quark's.

title: Destiny
line: Where did you get real Kanar?

title: Destiny
line: I've had three cases in my storeroom since the occupation. There hasn't been much call for it the past few years, but that's about to change.

title: Destiny
line: There are only two Cardassians coming to the station. How much Kanar do you think they can drink?

title: Destiny
line: There may only be two for now, but there'll be more, thanks to the peace treaty.

title: Destiny
line: And as the thirty fourth Rule of Acquisition states, peace is good for business.

title: Destiny
line: That's the thirty fifth Rule.

title: Destiny
line: Oh, you're right. What's the thirty fourth?

title: Destiny
line: War is good for business. It's easy to get them confused. The way I see it, it won't be long before there's a permanent Cardassian presence on the station. Scientists, diplomats, spies.

title: Destiny
line: And they'll all be welcome at Quark's.

title: Destiny
line: As long as they can pay. Rumor has it that the shop next door to mine is going out of business. I'm thinking of renting it and setting up a few Cardassian gaming concessions.

title: Destiny
line: There'll be no live vole fights on the Promenade, Quark.

title: Destiny
line: I would never be party to anything so cruel and inhumane. But, of course, if some Cardassians happened to bring their voles along and they happened to get into a fight, I could hardly be held responsible for

title: Destiny
line: Oh, yes you could.

title: Destiny
line: And you will be.

title: Destiny
line: Fine. Forget the vole fights. But I'll tell you this. Good Kanar is hard to find and I have three cases of it.

title: Destiny
line: But that's just the beginning. Soon, Quark's will become known as the best place for Cardassian food and drink in this sector. I'll probably set up daily shipments from Cardassia. I may even need to buy my own transport ship.

title: Destiny
line: Quark, this Kanar has gone bad.

title: Destiny
line: What?

title: Destiny
line: I suggest you take your bottles and leave, Quark, before I have you arrested for attempting to poison our guests.

title: Destiny
line: Excuse me, Commander. There's a Vedek Yarka here to see you. He says it's urgent.

title: Destiny
line: Thank you for seeing me, Emissary.

title: Destiny
line: What can I do for you?

title: Destiny
line: I am here with a warning from the Prophets. They don't want you to let the Cardassians come aboard the station. If you do, you will bring destruction on us all.

title: Destiny
line: Are you making some sort of threat, Vedek?

title: Destiny
line: Not at all. I'm simply telling you what was foretold in the ancient texts.

title: Destiny
line: Ancient texts? You mean a prophecy?

title: Destiny
line: Trakor's third, when he first encountered the Orb of Change.

title: Destiny
line: I'm afraid I don't know it.

title: Destiny
line: Perhaps you should make more time to study the texts, child.

title: Destiny
line: Are you saying that the arrival of the Cardassian scientists was foretold in a Bajoran prophecy?

title: Destiny
line: Exactly. Trakor's words are clear. When the river wakes, stirred once more to Janir's side, three vipers will return to their nest in the sky. The river has awoken, Emissary.

title: Destiny
line: The Qui'al dam was just put back into operation to divert water to the city.

title: Destiny
line: Just as Trakor prophesied over three thousand years ago. And even now, the vipers are making their way here.

title: Destiny
line: I take it you think the vipers are a reference to the Cardassian scientists.

title: Destiny
line: Yes, and this station is their nest in the sky.

title: Destiny
line: And how exactly is their presence here going to bring destruction on us all?

title: Destiny
line: Trakor said when the vipers try to peer through the temple gates, a sword of stars will appear in the heavens, the temple will burn and the gates will be cast open. You must not let the Cardassians come here. You must not let them violate the Celestial Temple or they will destroy it and Bajor will be cut off from the Prophets forever.

title: Destiny
line: Slow down. Now let me get this straight. You're saying that the vipers, the Cardassians, are going to destroy the wormhole?

title: Destiny
line: Don't you see? This communications relay you hope to create is part of the prophecy. It will allow the vipers to peer through the temple gates. The wormhole, as you call it. And if they do, the temple will be destroyed.

title: Destiny
line: Even if we accept that the Cardassians are the vipers, there are only two of them coming, not three. Isn't it possible that there are other mistakes in your interpretation of the prophecy as well?

title: Destiny
line: There will be three vipers. You will see.

title: Destiny
line: Do you understand what this communications relay could mean for Bajor? If it works, we'll be able to stay in contact with ships in the Gamma Quadrant.

title: Destiny
line: It'll facilitate exploration, help us monitor Dominion activity, give us warning in case of an attack.

title: Destiny
line: None of that matters. You must listen to me. I know it is difficult for you to accept because you are not Bajoran. I have studied the prophecies all my life. We are on the verge of a great disaster.

title: Destiny
line: Is the Bajoran Assembly aware of this prophecy?

title: Destiny
line: Yes. As is the Kai herself.

title: Destiny
line: Yet they still want us to proceed with the establishment of the communications relay.

title: Destiny
line: They have chosen to ignore the signs. That is why I came to you, Emissary. Because I have faith in you. I know that you will do what must be done.

title: Destiny
line: Vedek, I have the utmost respect for your beliefs, but I have no intention of calling this project off.

title: Destiny
line: I hope that you will reconsider, Emissary. My followers and I will remain on the station and pray that you change your mind.

title: Destiny
line: You're free to do that, of course.

title: Destiny
line: Major, have Odo find out everything he can about Vedek Yarka and his followers. I don't want them making any trouble while the Cardassians are here.

title: Destiny
line: I'm Commander Benjamin Sisko and on behalf of the United Federation of Planets and Starfleet Command, I'd like to welcome you to Deep Space Nine.

title: Destiny
line: Thank you, Commander. I'm Doctor Ulani Belor.

title: Destiny
line: Gilora Rejal.

title: Destiny
line: The Cardassian Government wishes to express its gratitude to the Federation for agreeing to work together on this project.

title: Destiny
line: It is our hope that it will be the first of many such projects between our peoples.

title: Destiny
line: That's a hope that I can assure you we share. This is my First Officer, Major Kira.

title: Destiny
line: And on behalf of the Bajoran Provisional Government, I'd like to welcome you. It's our belief that this project will mark the beginning of a new era of peace for Bajor and Cardassia.

title: Destiny
line: Thank you, Major.

title: Destiny
line: Well, now that we've gotten the formalities out of the way, how was your trip?

title: Destiny
line: Exhausting. We spent most of it rehearsing what we were going to say when we got here.

title: Destiny
line: We're scientists, not diplomats.

title: Destiny
line: You did very well.

title: Destiny
line: Please feel free to let the Central Command know that. In the past few days I've been contacted by Guls I haven't even heard of, all of them wanting to emphasize how important this mission is.

title: Destiny
line: I know what you mean. I've gotten three calls from Starfleet Command just this morning.

title: Destiny
line: Major Kira, I want to thank you personally for allowing us to come here.

title: Destiny
line: Me?

title: Destiny
line: You're the ranking Bajoran officer on this station. I'm sure we wouldn't be here if you had been opposed to working with us.

title: Destiny
line: I'll work with anyone who's interested in peace.

title: Destiny
line: I'm glad we already have so much in common.

title: Destiny
line: Well, why don't I show you to your quarters.

line: The signaling platform we've designed is intended to be positioned in the Gamma Quadrant at this point, two kilometers from the far mouth of the wormhole.

title: Destiny
line: Our transceiver has been configured to fit inside it, and use its existing power grid.

title: Destiny
