line: That's what happens when you go tromping around the bayou in the middle of the night. Come, warm yourself up by the fire. Now, I have a first aid kit around here somewhere. Where is it? So, what are you doing out here, anyway?

title: The Visitor
line: I'm a writer. At least, I want to be. And the truth is I was looking for you.

title: The Visitor
line: Oh?

title: The Visitor
line: You are Jake Sisko the writer?

title: The Visitor
line: Yes.

title: The Visitor
line: I can't believe I'm really here talking to you. You are my favorite author of all time.

title: The Visitor
line: You should read more.

title: The Visitor
line: I mean it. Your books, they're so insightful.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm glad you like them.

title: The Visitor
line: There. Good as new.

title: The Visitor
line: Thank you.

title: The Visitor
line: I didn't realize people still read my books.

title: The Visitor
line: Of course they do. A friend recommended Anslem to me and I read it straight through twice in one night.

title: The Visitor
line: Twice in one night?

title: The Visitor
line: It made me want to read everything you'd ever written, but when I looked, all I could find was your Collected Stories. I couldn't believe it. I'd finally found someone whose writing I really admired, and he'd only published two books.

title: The Visitor
line: Not much to show for a life's work, is it? I'm going to go get us some tea.

title: The Visitor
line: I savored those stories. I read them slowly, one each day, and when I was done I wished I hadn't read them at all. So I could read them again like it was the first time.

title: The Visitor
line: There's only one first time for everything, isn't there? And only one last time too. You think about that such things when you get to be my age. That today might be the last time you sit in your favorite chair, or watch the rain fall, or enjoy a cup of tea by a warm fire.

title: The Visitor
line: Can I ask you something?

title: The Visitor
line: Of course.

title: The Visitor
line: Why did you stop writing?

title: The Visitor
line: I lost my favorite pen and I couldn't get any work done without it.

title: The Visitor
line: You're joking. You weren't even forty when you stopped writing. I've never understood why you gave it up.

title: The Visitor
line: It's a long story.

title: The Visitor
line: I have time. Tell me. Please.

title: The Visitor
line: If you had shown up yesterday or the day before, or a week ago, I would have said no and sent you on your way. But here you are, today of all days, and somehow it seems like the right time for me to finally tell this story. It begins many years ago. I was eighteen and the worst thing that could happen to a young man happened to me. My father died. We were very close, my father and I, partly because we'd lost my mother several years earlier.

title: The Visitor
line: I know. I read a biography about you. It said that you stopped writing so you could conduct scientific research?

title: The Visitor
line: It's not quite that simple. You see, just before my father died, I was working on a short story. I don't remember what it was about but I do know that I was taking it very seriously. I worked on it night and day for weeks, and I wasn't making any headway and it was making me miserable. I suppose my father saw that I needed a break.

title: The Visitor
line: Because he insisted I come with him to the Gamma Quadrant to watch the wormhole undergo what they call a subspace inversion.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake-o, let's go.

title: The Visitor
line: Of course what he didn't realize was that I could hide away on the Defiant just as easily as I could on the station.

title: The Visitor
line: Yeah.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, this only happens once every fifty years. You will never forgive yourself if you miss it.

title: The Visitor
line: Yeah, I'll be right there.

title: The Visitor
line: That's what you said ten minutes ago.

title: The Visitor
line: I just want to get this last paragraph right.

title: The Visitor
line: I thought you were going to put that aside for a while.

title: The Visitor
line: I tried, but it's all I can think about.

title: The Visitor
line: Well, I'm no writer, but if I were, it seems to me I'd want to poke my head up once in a while and take a look around, see what's going on. It's life, Jake. You can miss it if you don't open your eyes. Now, what do you say you come up to the bridge with me and we'll watch the wormhole do its thing, and then I'll read what you've got and we'll talk about it. Deal?

title: The Visitor
line: Deal.

title: The Visitor
line: Sisko to Bridge.

title: The Visitor
line: What happened?

title: The Visitor
line: The wormhole's gravimetric field is surging.

title: The Visitor
line: Pull us to a safe distance.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm on it, Benjamin, but we've got another problem. The power output from the warp core just jumped off the scale.

title: The Visitor
line: Sisko to Engineering. Engineering, report. Dax, I'm going to find out what's happening down there. Stay here, Jake.

title: The Visitor
line: Most of the time, I knew enough to do what my father told me. But that day, for some reason, I didn't.

title: The Visitor
line: Sisko to Sickbay, I need a medical team down here right away.

title: The Visitor
line: Dax to Sisko.

title: The Visitor
line: The warp coils are locked into a feedback loop. You've got to realign them or the core's going to blow.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm on it. Jake, I need an interphasic compensator.

title: The Visitor
line: Warning. Warp core breach in forty seconds.

title: The Visitor
line: Dax, better stand by to eject the core.

title: The Visitor
line: We can't.

title: The Visitor
line: The ejection system's offline.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, where's that compensator?

title: The Visitor
line: It's not here.

title: The Visitor
line: Warning. Warp core breach in thirty seconds.

title: The Visitor
line: Got it.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm going to try shunting the excess power out through the deflector array.

title: The Visitor
line: Warning. Warp core breach in twenty seconds.

title: The Visitor
line: Just a little more. There.

title: The Visitor
line: No!

title: The Visitor
line: He was gone.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm not sure I could ever get over losing somebody like that, right in front of my eyes.

title: The Visitor
line: People do. Time passes, they realize that the person they lost is really gone, and they heal.

title: The Visitor
line: Is that what happened to you?

title: The Visitor
line: No. I suppose not. There was a memorial service aboard the station.

title: The Visitor
line: People came forward and talked about my father, what they remembered most about him why and they would miss him.

title: The Visitor
line: Benjamin Sisko was more than my commanding officer. He was the Emissary to my people, sent by the Prophets. But most importantly, he was my friend.

title: The Visitor
line: I didn't step forward. I couldn't. I felt that no matter what I said about him, I'd be leaving so much more out and that didn't seem right.

title: The Visitor
line: I'd never felt more alone in all my life. Everyone went out of their way to look after me, especially Dax. She was my father's closest friend, and I guess she felt responsible for me.

title: The Visitor
line: After a few months things started returning to normal, for everyone else, that is.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, I'm almost done. We have holosuite three for half an hour.

title: The Visitor
line: Great.

title: The Visitor
line: Nog, get down to the storeroom and bring up five kegs of Takarian mead.

title: The Visitor
line: Yes, Uncle. Sorry, looks like we're going to lose our holosuite reservation.

title: The Visitor
line: You know, Nog, things seem to be slowing down a bit. I'll get someone else to bring up those kegs. You and Jake go and have some fun.

title: The Visitor
line: Are you sure?

title: The Visitor
line: Go, now, before I change my mind.

title: The Visitor
line: Next time we go ion surfing, remind me to keep clear of those whip curls.

title: The Visitor
line: I don't know if I really want to try it again.

title: The Visitor
line: You know, Jake I'm going to be gone soon. We probably won't see each other for a while.

title: The Visitor
line: I know.

title: The Visitor
line: So, what are your plans?

title: The Visitor
line: Well, I was thinking about taking that deferred admission and going to Pennington in the fall.

title: The Visitor
line: That'd be great. We'd both be on Earth together.

title: The Visitor
line: But maybe I'll just stick around here. I don't know. I haven't decided yet. It's late. I think I'll turn in.

title: The Visitor
line: Okay.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake?

title: The Visitor
line: Dad?

title: The Visitor
line: What happened?

title: The Visitor
line: I told Dax about what had happened. How it felt so real, not like a dream at all and she very kindly obliged me and did a very thorough scan of my room. I felt vaguely ridiculous, like a child insisting his parents check under his bed for monsters. She tried to tell me it was probably just a nightmare and I did my best to put the entire episode out of my mind. I puttered around the station for the next eight or nine months. Nog was off at Starfleet. My stories stubbornly refused to write themselves. I filled my time playing dom-jot and tried not to think about how alone I felt. Dax and the others were worried about me.

title: The Visitor
line: But before long, they had bigger things to worry about. Tensions with the Klingons were continuing to rise. My father was a kind of religious figure to the Bajoran people, and when he died they took it as a sign from the Prophets that the Federation wouldn't be able to protect them from the Klingons. Eventually Bajor entered into a mutual defense pact with the Cardassians, and the Klingons didn't like that at all. The station's civilian population was leaving en masse. They knew that if war broke out against the Klingons, Deep Space Nine was going to be on the front line.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, where are you going ?

title: The Visitor
line: I thought I'd watch the ships leave from one of the upper pylons.

title: The Visitor
line: You should be on one of those ships.

title: The Visitor
line: I don't have to go, do I?

title: The Visitor
line: No. It's a voluntary resettlement, not an evacuation.

title: The Visitor
line: But it would be prudent that you leave at this time.

title: The Visitor
line: I suppose I wasn't feeling very prudent that day, because I ignored their advice.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake. I wanted to talk to you about something. I spoke with your grandfather and he told me that he asked you to go live with him. Even if this sector weren't on the brink of war, I would like to see you leave the station.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm not going anywhere.

title: The Visitor
line: Oh, Jake. I could order you to go if I wanted to.

title: The Visitor
line: Please don't make me leave. Not yet. This is my home. When my Dad and I came here this place was just an abandoned shell. He turned it into something. Everywhere I look it's like I see a part of him. If I leave I won't have anything left of him.

title: The Visitor
line: All right. You stay a while longer if you want to. But you have to promise me when the time comes and I tell you to go, you'll do it.

title: The Visitor
line: Dad?

title: The Visitor
line: It wasn't until I actually touched him that I knew this wasn't a dream.

title: The Visitor
line: But something was wrong. I didn't understand everything they were saying, but Dax and the others seemed to think that the accident had somehow knocked my father's temporal signature out of phase.

title: The Visitor
line: Benjamin, what's the last thing you remember?

title: The Visitor
line: I was in Engineering on the Defiant. It feels like a few minutes ago.

title: The Visitor
line: Dad, it's been over a year since the accident.

title: The Visitor
line: A year? How could that be?

title: The Visitor
line: We think the warp core discharge pulled you into subspace. If we're right, that would explain why you didn't experience the passage of time.

title: The Visitor
line: According to these readings, unless we can realign your temporal signature, you'll be pulled back into subspace again within the next few minutes.

title: The Visitor
line: Maybe we can set up some sort of containment field.

title: The Visitor
line: We're going to have to reconfigure the field parameters.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, they'll have me fixed up in no time. How are you doing?

title: The Visitor
line: It's all right. Everything's going to be all right.

title: The Visitor
line: I thought it was a dream.

title: The Visitor
line: What was?

title: The Visitor
line: When I saw you in my quarters I should have felt you were alive. I should have known it.

title: The Visitor
line: It's not your fault, Jake. I'm here now. That's what matters.

title: The Visitor
line: We're losing him.

title: The Visitor
line: Look at me. I need to know you're going to be all right.

title: The Visitor
line: His temporal signature is fluctuating.

title: The Visitor
line: I need that containment field now, Chief.

title: The Visitor
line: Right away. Field active.

title: The Visitor
line: It's not working.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake.

title: The Visitor
line: Dad!

title: The Visitor
line: I'm going to try locking onto him with the transporter beam.

title: The Visitor
line: Don't leave me.

title: The Visitor
line: I didn't think anything could be worse than losing him that first time on the Defiant, until I was standing there staring down at his empty bed, knowing he was alive yet trapped somewhere that existed outside of time.

title: The Visitor
line: I can't imagine what that must have been like for you.

title: The Visitor
line: Can I get you something?

title: The Visitor
line: No, nothing.

title: The Visitor
line: Telling me all this is hard for you. Maybe I should come back some other time?

title: The Visitor
line: No. There won't be any another time. You see, I'm dying. You must understand, when person my age says he's dying, he's only admitting to the inevitable. Besides, we old people need to remind everyone to pay special attention to us.

title: The Visitor
line: If that's what you're up to you shouldn't have bothered. You have my attention already.

title: The Visitor
line: You're a good listener. That's important in a writer.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm not a writer yet.

title: The Visitor
line: Sound like you're waiting for something to happen that's going to turn you into one.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm not waiting. I'm doing a lot of reading. You know, to see how it's done. And I'm still trying to figure out what it is I want to write about.

title: The Visitor
line: I see.

title: The Visitor
line: So what happened? With your father, I mean. Did you ever see him again?

title: The Visitor
line: For the next few months Dax and O'Brien tried to find a way to locate him. They even considered recreating the accident, but that was impossible since the wormhole wasn't going to undergo an inversion for decades. Eventually the situation with the Klingons came to a head, and the Federation decided to turn over control of the station to the Klingon Empire.

title: The Visitor
line: There was nothing I could do. I had to leave my home of five years and give up whatever hope there was of seeing my father again.

title: The Visitor
line: Did the Klingons ever contact Starfleet to say that your father had reappeared?

title: The Visitor
line: No. I was left with no choice but to try to get on with my life. I went to Earth, drifted around and eventually ended up studying writing at the Pennington school. After graduation, I settled here in Louisiana so I could be near my grandfather. He had a restaurant in the French Quarter, you know.

title: The Visitor
line: I've been there. It's still called Sisko's. And on the wall there's a copy of the letter your publisher sent you when he accepted your first novel.

title: The Visitor
line: Grandpa was always showing off his famous grandson. He was just as proud of me as my father would've been.

title: The Visitor
line: You wrote Anslem in this house, didn't you?

title: The Visitor
line: At that desk, right over there. It came out to generally favorable reviews, and little by little I began to think less and less about the past. After a while I met a woman, fell in love, we got married, and for a while this house was a happy one.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm back. (Not quite as far in the future. Korena is an artist and Nog is in red TNG uniform and Tony is out of the age makeup.)

title: The Visitor
line: Nog. I didn't realize you were here already. I was trying to finish a painting before the light changed and I guess the time got away from me.

title: The Visitor
line: It's good to see you.

title: The Visitor
line: You too. Did you start the grill?

title: The Visitor
line: What are we having?

title: The Visitor
line: Blackened redfish fresh from the bayou.

title: The Visitor
line: Fish? When these woods are crawling with perfectly good slugs?

title: The Visitor
line: I suppose you're going to ask me to chew your food for you?

title: The Visitor
line: I have to admit I've been more popular with women since I stopped asking them to do that.

title: The Visitor
line: I tried to tell you that twenty years ago.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm a slow learner.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm going to get some champagne.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm glad you're here, Nog.

title: The Visitor
line: I see you've got another pip on your collar. You keep that up you're going to make captain by the time you're forty.

title: The Visitor
line: Last time we talked you mentioned you might be heading to the Bajoran Sector.

title: The Visitor
line: The Klingons agreed to let Starfleet send an expedition through the wormhole. They said it was in the spirit of scientific exchange, but I think they were happy to have us test the waters in the Gamma Quadrant after all these years. Find out how the Dominion would react to ships coming through.

title: The Visitor
line: Did you see the station?

title: The Visitor
line: I'm sorry to say it's looking a little run down these days. But you'll never guess who's still there.

title: The Visitor
line: Not your father?

title: The Visitor
line: No, no. He and my Uncle left years ago. Quark finally got that little moon he was always talking about, and my father, as usual, is making sure it doesn't fall out of orbit. But Morn is still there, running the bar!

title: The Visitor
line: Talking his customers' ears off and drinking himself out of business, I'll bet.

title: The Visitor
line: Well, why don't we get to the point of today's little celebration.

title: The Visitor
line: To my dear friend Jake Sisko, winner of this year's Betar prize for his Collected Stories. May the years continue to be good to you, may your muse continue to inspire you, and may someone make a holoprogram out of one of your stories so you can start raking in the latinum.

title: The Visitor
line: Are you all right? Do you want me to call a doctor?

title: The Visitor
line: No. I'll be fine.

title: The Visitor
line: You should rest.

title: The Visitor
line: No. You came a long way to find out why I had stopped writing and you deserve an answer.

title: The Visitor
line: Later that night, after Nog had left, I stayed up working. My new novel was going well, and when it's going well you don't want to stop.

title: The Visitor
line: Coming to bed?

title: The Visitor
line: I'm not tired.

title: The Visitor
line: Neither am I.

title: The Visitor
line: You know, I wanted to ask you something. How would you feel about designing the cover to my new book?

title: The Visitor
line: Do you mean it?

title: The Visitor
line: What was that?

title: The Visitor
line: Jake?

title: The Visitor
line: Did you get through?

title: The Visitor
line: I talked to someone at Starfleet Science. They're going to get a team here as soon as they can.

title: The Visitor
line: This is Korena, my wife.

title: The Visitor
line: Your wife?

title: The Visitor
line: I never thought I'd have the pleasure of meeting you.

title: The Visitor
line: The pleasure is mine. How long have you two been married?

title: The Visitor
line: Seven years.

title: The Visitor
line: Do I have any grandchildren?

title: The Visitor
line: Not yet.

title: The Visitor
line: We were married in New Orleans, in your father's restaurant.

title: The Visitor
line: He insisted. Just about everyone came. Dax, Kira, O'Brien.

title: The Visitor
line: That must've been something.

title: The Visitor
line: I got to go call Starfleet.

title: The Visitor
line: Whoa. They'll get here as soon as they can. Talk to me. I've missed so much. Let's not waste what little time we have.

title: The Visitor
line: I have a feeling you might want to see these. They're Jake's.

title: The Visitor
line: You did it. I always knew you would.

title: The Visitor
line: Oh, Jake.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm sorry.

title: The Visitor
line: What for?

title: The Visitor
line: For giving up on you.

title: The Visitor
line: No one could be expected to hold out hope for this long.

title: The Visitor
line: I should have just kept trying to find you. I just went on with my life.

title: The Visitor
line: And I'm proud of what you've accomplished.

title: The Visitor
line: None of it matters now that I know you're still out there, lost somewhere.

title: The Visitor
line: Of course it matters. You have a wife, a career. And don't think because I'm not around much that I don't want grandchildren.

title: The Visitor
line: Within a few seconds, he was gone again.

title: The Visitor
line: I don't know what to say.

title: The Visitor
line: You don't need to say anything. Just listen, because there isn't much time and there's so much more for me to tell you. I consulted with Dax and we realized that the accident must have created some sort of subspace link between my father and myself.

title: The Visitor
line: That's why he always appeared somewhere near you even if you were hundreds of light years away from where the accident happened.

title: The Visitor
line: We also realized that there was a pattern to his appearances. They were governed by fluctuations in the wormhole's subspace field. Dax's calculations also showed that the next time he appeared, I'd be an old man. And so I decided to put aside my novel and try to find a way to help him. At the age of thirty seven, I went back to school and started studying subspace mechanics. At first, Korena was very patient. She supported what I was trying to do. But I got so caught up in my work I didn't notice I was losing her. By the time I became a graduate student, we were no longer living together. By the time I had entered my doctoral program, it was over between us. But I pressed on with what I was doing, and one day, years later, it hit me. I figured out a way to recreate the accident. It had been almost fifty years, and the wormhole would soon be undergoing another inversion. There was only one other thing I needed.

title: The Visitor
line: The Defiant. Nog was a Captain by then, and he helped me round up the old crew and get the ship pulled out of mothballs. Worf threw his weight around with the Klingon High Council, and they gave us permission to enter the Bajoran system.

title: The Visitor
line: Take us out of warp.

title: The Visitor
line: I think I remember how to do that.

title: The Visitor
line: I haven't worked a two-dimensional control panel in a long time. How did we manage?

title: The Visitor
line: We always seemed to muddle through somehow.

title: The Visitor
line: Look.

title: The Visitor
line: Maybe after we've got Captain Sisko back, we can all stop by Morn's for a drink for old time's sake.

title: The Visitor
line: I'd designed a subspace flux isolator and we set it up in Engineering.

title: The Visitor
line: Are you ready over there, Dax?

title: The Visitor
line: As ready as I'll ever be, considering the replicators were just about the only things still working when we came aboard.

title: The Visitor
line: It's a lucky thing too. Dax isn't any good to anybody these days without a cup of coffee in her hand.

title: The Visitor
line: It's the only thing that's kept me awake while you prattled on about your latest paper, or your new backhand, or your kid's science projects.

title: The Visitor
line: We're picking up temporal distortions in the subspace field.

title: The Visitor
line: The wormhole's beginning to invert.

title: The Visitor
line: According to our readings, it's going to kick out a gravimetric wave like the one that almost destroyed the Defiant last time.

title: The Visitor
line: Don't worry. I've modulated the shields to channel the wave's energy into this apparatus.

title: The Visitor
line: Once subspace begins to fragment, we'll try to locate the captain.

title: The Visitor
line: Since the accident created a subspace link between him and Jake, there'll be a path of bread crumbs to follow.

title: The Visitor
line: I'd better get back to the bridge. Good luck.

title: The Visitor
line: The wormhole wouldn't undergo another inversion for decades, so this was my only chance.

title: The Visitor
line: Subspace field fragmentation is beginning.

title: The Visitor
line: It's working.

title: The Visitor
line: I think I've got the captain's signature.

title: The Visitor
line: Something's happening. I'm losing him.

title: The Visitor
line: We're losing them both. They're being pulled into subspace.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake. How long has it been?

title: The Visitor
line: Fourteen years. What is this place?

title: The Visitor
line: I don't know

title: The Visitor
line: We could be inside some sort of subspace fragment. Sisko to Dax. Can you read me? I brought the Defiant back to the wormhole. We're trying to rescue you. Dax, if you can hear me, try to lock onto my signal.

title: The Visitor
line: Look at you. You're older than I am.

title: The Visitor
line: Damn it. Why can't they lock on to us?

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, they're doing the best they can. There's nothing we can do from here. It's been so long. I need to know what I've missed. What about those grandchildren we talked about?

title: The Visitor
line: Korena and I, we're no longer together. She left me.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm sorry.

title: The Visitor
line: I shouldn't have let her go, but there was so much I had to do. This has taken years of planning.

title: The Visitor
line: What about your writing?

title: The Visitor
line: Dax, try boosting the carrier amplitude. Maybe you can

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, what's happened to you?

title: The Visitor
line: This is the last chance I'm ever going to have to help you.

title: The Visitor
line: No!

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, it's over. It's not going to work.

title: The Visitor
line: It has to.

title: The Visitor
line: Let go, Jake. If not for yourself, then for me. You still have time to make a better life for yourself. Promise me you'll do that. Promise me!

title: The Visitor
line: I want you to see something. Go over to my desk. Go ahead.

title: The Visitor
line: It's a collection of new stories. I decided to honor my father's request and try to rebuild my life. Writing these stories was the best way I knew to do that. I'd like you to have a copy. Let me get you one.

title: The Visitor
line: Can I have these instead?

title: The Visitor
line: Well, if you'd like, but those have handwritten notes all over them.

title: The Visitor
line: I know. I want to study them so I can see the changes you made.

title: The Visitor
line: Because you want to be a writer someday.

title: The Visitor
line: Can I ask why you haven't published these?

title: The Visitor
line: Well, I was tinkering with the last story just this morning. Besides, if you publish posthumously no body can ask you for rewrites. I was hoping to finish another two stories, but there isn't enough time.

title: The Visitor
line: You keep on saying there's no more time.

title: The Visitor
line: You see, Melanie, after the last attempt to rescue my father failed, I spent months trying to figure out what went wrong. Eventually, I came to understand the nature of what was happening to him. It was as if he was frozen in time at the moment of the accident, and the link between us was like an elastic cord. Every so often the cord would go taut enough to yank him forward into my time. But only for a few minutes. I realized that if my motion through time came to a stop, the cord would go slack and he'd be lost in subspace forever. But if I could cut the cord when the link was at its strongest, while we were together, he'd return to the moment of the accident.

title: The Visitor
line: Your father's coming here, isn't he? Soon.

title: The Visitor
line: Yes.

title: The Visitor
line: You're going to cut the cord, aren't you?

title: The Visitor
line: I want you to promise me something.

title: The Visitor
line: Anything.

title: The Visitor
line: While you're studying my stories, poke your head up every once in a while. Take a look around. See what's going on. It's life, Melanie.

title: The Visitor
line: And you can miss it if you don't open your eyes.

title: The Visitor
line: Thank you. For everything.

title: The Visitor
line: It was a pleasure meeting you, young lady.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake.

title: The Visitor
line: I've been expecting you.

title: The Visitor
line: I'm glad to see you're still in this house. You seemed happy here. And this. I can't tell you how good it makes me feel you got back to writing.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, what is it?

title: The Visitor
line: Read at the dedication.

title: The Visitor
line: To my father, who's coming home. Thank you, but I don't understand.

title: The Visitor
line: It was me. It was me all along. I've been dragging you through time like an anchor and now it's time to cut you loose.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, what are you saying?

title: The Visitor
line: It won't be long now.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake! No!

title: The Visitor
line: When I die, you'll go back to where this all began. Just remember to dodge the energy discharge from the warp core.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, you could still have so many years left.

title: The Visitor
line: No. We have to be together when I die.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake, you didn't have to do this. Not for me.

title: The Visitor
line: For you and for the boy that I was. He needs you more than you know. Don't you see? We're going to get a second chance.

title: The Visitor
line: Jake. My sweet boy.

title: The Visitor
line: You okay?

title: The Visitor
line: How'd you know that was coming?

title: The Visitor
line: I guess we were just lucky this time.

title: The Visitor
line: You okay, Dad?

title: The Visitor
line: I am now, Jake. I am now.

title: Indiscretion
line: Worf to Major Kira.

title: Indiscretion
line: This is Kira.

title: Indiscretion
line: Major, you've got an incoming transmission from a Razka Karn. He claims to be an old friend.

title: Indiscretion
line: Put him through. Razka. It's been a while. How's business?

title: Indiscretion
line: Oh, let's just say I miss the old days on Bajor. Smuggling might not have been the safest line of work, but it was a lot more exciting than selling scrap metal.

title: Indiscretion
line: What's on your mind, Razka?

title: Indiscretion
line: I picked up a lead on the Ravinok.

title: Indiscretion
line: Like the last time?

title: Indiscretion
line: Last time it was just a rumor. This time I have evidence, a fragment of metal. Looks like it's part of the forward sensor array.

title: Indiscretion
line: Can you bring it to Deep Space Nine for analysis?

title: Indiscretion
line: Sorry. I'm afraid I can't leave the Badlands right now. Important business. You understand.

title: Indiscretion
line: Tholians are after you again?

title: Indiscretion
line: Let's just say it'd be better if you came to me.

title: Indiscretion
line: It's been six years. Even if you have found a piece of the Ravinok, it doesn't mean there are any survivors.

title: Indiscretion
line: There's only one way for you to find out. I'll be waiting.

title: Indiscretion
line: And item number seventeen, Trelos Vren was arrested on the Promenade outside of the Klingon restaurant. He's being held on four counts of petty theft.

title: Indiscretion
line: Trelos Vren? Where have I heard that name?

title: Indiscretion
line: We arrested him once for attempting to break into the assay office.

title: Indiscretion
line: And now he's taken up pickpocketing?

title: Indiscretion
line: Without much success. Still, I suppose you should admire him for his persistence. That was a joke.

title: Indiscretion
line: I'm sorry, Odo. I may have a lead on the Ravinok. I know what you're going to say. It's been six years since the Ravinok disappeared. Odds are everyone on board is dead.

title: Indiscretion
line: That all may be true, but that is not what I was going to say. I was going to say good luck.

title: Indiscretion
line: Good luck?

title: Indiscretion
line: You had a friend aboard the Ravinok, correct?

title: Indiscretion
line: Lorit Akrem.

title: Indiscretion
line: Which means it doesn't matter if I think there are any survivors, or even if you think there are any survivors. You are going to go looking for that ship, and all I can say is good luck. And I hope you find them.

title: Indiscretion
line: Come in. Captain. You here to see me off?

title: Indiscretion
line: I'm afraid not. I'd like you to postpone your trip for at least for a day or two.

title: Indiscretion
line: What's wrong?

title: Indiscretion
line: Somehow the Cardassian government got wind of your plan to search for the Ravinok. They've asked permission to send someone with you.

title: Indiscretion
line: And you said yes?

title: Indiscretion
line: I said I'd talk to you about it. The Ravinok was a Cardassian ship.

title: Indiscretion
line: Carrying Bajoran prisoners. I'm not stopping anyone else from looking. I just don't see why they have to come with me.

title: Indiscretion
line: The request came directly from the leader of the new civilian government. Nerys, I know this isn't what you had in mind, but Bajor and Cardassia must to learn to work together and that means cooperating on missions like these.

title: Indiscretion
line: All right. Just tell them I'm not going to wait forever. If their representative isn't here within fifty two hours, I'm going alone.

title: Indiscretion
line: I'll be sure they get the message.

title: Indiscretion
line: So did you and Kasidy have a nice time last night?

title: Indiscretion
line: I just wish she wasn't leaving tomorrow.

title: Indiscretion
line: It sounds like the two of you are getting serious.

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't know about that. I don't think Kasidy is looking to get serious.

title: Indiscretion
line: Ben!

title: Indiscretion
line: Kasidy.

title: Indiscretion
line: We were just talking about you.

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't mean to interrupt. I wanted you to know I won't be leaving tomorrow after all.

title: Indiscretion
line: That's good news. I mean, that's great. How long are you going to be here?

title: Indiscretion
line: That depends on whether I get this new job or not. I've applied for a position with the Bajoran Ministry of Commerce to captain one of their freighters.

title: Indiscretion
line: You're going to work for the Bajorans?

title: Indiscretion
line: If we can hammer out an agreement. It's a terrific opportunity. I get to use my own ship, pick my own crew, and the best part is, I never have to leave this sector.

title: Indiscretion
line: Where're you going to live?

title: Indiscretion
line: On my ship, I suppose.

title: Indiscretion
line: Well, why don't you stay here? I'm sure that Benjamin could arrange for some quarters.

title: Indiscretion
line: That's not a bad idea.

title: Indiscretion
line: Yeah.

title: Indiscretion
line: Well, I have a meeting on Bajor and the shuttle leaves in a few minutes. I'll see you tonight?

title: Indiscretion
line: That answers that. She's serious.

title: Indiscretion
line: Captain, the Cardassian transport Rabol is approaching the station. They're requesting permission to beam their representative directly to Ops.

title: Indiscretion
line: Someone's in a big hurry.

title: Indiscretion
line: Permission granted.

title: Indiscretion
line: Aye, sir.

title: Indiscretion
line: Ah, Major Kira. I'm ready to leave whenever you are.

title: Indiscretion
line: We'll be crossing into the Badlands in approximately six hours.

title: Indiscretion
line: Very good, Major.

title: Indiscretion
line: Dukat, let's get one thing straight. This is my mission. The only reason you're here is because I agreed to let you come along. When I give an order, I expect you to follow it. No questions asked.

title: Indiscretion
line: Believe me, Major, I want nothing more than for this mission to be concluded as quickly and as efficiently as possible. I leave the details in your capable hands.

title: Indiscretion
line: Good, then we shouldn't have any problems. There's one thing I don't understand. Why did the Cardassian government send you?

title: Indiscretion
line: The Ravinok was under my general command. Those were my troops and it is my duty to try to find them. The question is, what are you doing here, Major?

title: Indiscretion
line: I knew someone aboard the Ravinok.

title: Indiscretion
line: One of the prisoners, I assume?

title: Indiscretion
line: Lorit Akrem.

title: Indiscretion
line: I see. So you're on this mission for personal reasons.

title: Indiscretion
line: Is there something wrong with that?

title: Indiscretion
line: Not at all. I've found that when one is trying to do a difficult job, personal reasons can be quite an incentive. So who was he? A family member, a compatriot, a lover?

title: Indiscretion
line: Lorit recruited me into the Shakaar resistance cell.

title: Indiscretion
line: Ah. The infamous Shakaar resistance. We never could eliminate that little group of yours. And it was not from lack of trying, I assure you. I hope you don't take this the wrong way, Major, but I've always admired you. You are the embodiment of the new Bajor. A Bajoran born out of the ashes of the occupation, a Bajoran tempered with Cardassian steel.

title: Indiscretion
line: Captain Sisko's right. You are in love with the sound of your own voice.

title: Indiscretion
line: I know you find this to accept, but I believe that in some ways the Occupation actually helped Bajor.

title: Indiscretion
line: Which part? The massacres or the strip mining?

title: Indiscretion
line: I have no desire to debate the merits of the Occupation with you. I'm even willing to admit that perhaps we were a little harsh in our methods. But the fact is, the Bajoran people are stronger now than they have been in centuries. When we arrived, you were a weak, contemplative race, choking on your isolation. And now you have a new confidence, a whole new sense of purpose, not to mention a key role in the future of this entire quadrant.

title: Indiscretion
line: All of which Bajor achieved in spite of the Cardassians, not because of them.

title: Indiscretion
line: Think what you must, But I believe the time will come when Cardassia and Bajor will grow to be not only allies but also close friends.

title: Indiscretion
line: Cardassia and Bajor, maybe. You and me? I doubt it.

title: Indiscretion
line: All I ask is that you have an open mind.

title: Indiscretion
line: All right, Dukat, that's enough. Now, if you don't mind, I would like to spend the next six hours in silent meditation.

title: Indiscretion
line: Is that a request, or an order?

title: Indiscretion
line: Whatever it takes.

title: Indiscretion
line: Well, in that case, as much as it pains me.

title: Indiscretion
line: We both might survive this trip after all.

title: Indiscretion
line: They didn't even wait for the interview to be over. After twenty minutes, Minister Azin said she'd heard enough, and if I wanted the job, it was mine.

title: Indiscretion
line: So what did you tell them?

title: Indiscretion
line: What do you think I told them? I said yes.

title: Indiscretion
line: Congratulations.

title: Indiscretion
line: That's it?

title: Indiscretion
line: Oh.

title: Indiscretion
line: That's not what I meant. I want to know how you feel about it.

title: Indiscretion
line: I think it's great. We'll see a lot more of each other.

title: Indiscretion
line: You know, I was thinking about what Dax said. Maybe I should get quarters on the station.

title: Indiscretion
line: That's a big step.

title: Indiscretion
line: What does that mean?

title: Indiscretion
line: I just meant it's a big step.

title: Indiscretion
line: A bad big step, or a good big step?

title: Indiscretion
line: A good one.

title: Indiscretion
line: Could you muster a little more enthusiasm?

title: Indiscretion
line: I am enthusiastic. I'm proud of you. This job

title: Indiscretion
line: Forget about the job. I'm talking about us. I tell you I'm thinking about living on the station and all you can say is, it's a big step?

title: Indiscretion
line: Oh, I don't think you took it the way I meant it.

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't think you know what you meant. But I do. You're afraid of commitment.

title: Indiscretion
line: Who said anything about commitment?

title: Indiscretion
line: Obviously not you. You know what? Forget the whole thing. I'm not going to take the job. If you don't want me to stay here, that's fine with me.

title: Indiscretion
line: Phew.

title: Indiscretion
line: How'd you get a hold of this, Razka?

title: Indiscretion
line: I bought it off a Ferengi scrap metal merchant.

title: Indiscretion
line: It appears to be composed of uridium alloy. It's definitely Cardassian.

title: Indiscretion
line: Can you tell if it's from the Ravinok?

title: Indiscretion
line: Why didn't you tell me you were bringing him along?

title: Indiscretion
line: Because when we talked, I didn't know I would be.

title: Indiscretion
line: Too bad. The Maquis would've paid handsomely to get their hands on him.

title: Indiscretion
line: And my government would be very happy to get their hands on you. Razka Karn, if I'm not mistaken. Smuggler, thief, black marketeer. There are at least twelve outstanding warrants for your arrest on Cardassia right now. But I suggest we ignore all that and try to cooperate with one another.

title: Indiscretion
line: The voice of the new Cardassia, so compassionate, so understanding. Almost makes you forget that five years ago he was working Bajorans to death in forced labor camps and shooting anybody who tried to stop him. Almost makes you forget.

title: Indiscretion
line: It's from the Ravinok. No doubt about it.

title: Indiscretion
line: Did the Ferengi tell you where he found it?

title: Indiscretion
line: No, but I was curious so I bribed one of his crewmembers. Turns out his last trip was to the Dozaria system.

title: Indiscretion
line: Dozaria. I believe there is one class M planet in that system.

title: Indiscretion
line: Barely class M. He found that in orbit.

title: Indiscretion
line: Dozaria it is then. Thanks, Razka. I owe you one.

title: Indiscretion
line: Just let me know what you find out. Lorit was my friend too.

title: Indiscretion
line: I just don't understand how the Ravinok could've gotten so far off course. Dozaria is light years from where they should have been.

title: Indiscretion
line: The Central Command always believed that the ship was destroyed in some kind of escape attempt by the Bajoran prisoners.

title: Indiscretion
line: Maybe. Or they could've had a problem with their navigational array or run into some kind of subspace anomaly.

title: Indiscretion
line: Hopefully we'll find the truth.

title: Indiscretion
line: We're entering orbit.

title: Indiscretion
line: I'm reading severe ionic interference in the planet's atmosphere. Sensors will be limited, to say the least.

title: Indiscretion
line: I'm picking up a faint magneton signature. It could be residual radiation from a damaged warp nacelle.

title: Indiscretion
line: Shall we beam down?

title: Indiscretion
line: I wouldn't advise it. All this ionic interference will scatter our molecules halfway around the planet. We're going to have to do this the old fashioned way.

title: Indiscretion
line: It's going to be a difficult landing. I'll take the controls if you like.

title: Indiscretion
line: That'll be the day. Going in.

title: Indiscretion
line: Invigorating, isn't it. A bit sunny, perhaps, but this heat feels wonderful.

title: Indiscretion
line: Only a Cardassian would call this hellhole invigorating.

title: Indiscretion
line: Oh, I forgot. Compared to us, you Bajorans are a bit fragile, physiologically speaking, of course.

title: Indiscretion
line: Don't worry about me.

title: Indiscretion
line: The Ravinok.

title: Indiscretion
line: It's a big step. That's all you said?

title: Indiscretion
line: That's all.

title: Indiscretion
line: You're sure?

title: Indiscretion
line: Positive.

title: Indiscretion
line: What do you think, Julian?

title: Indiscretion
line: It's ambiguous. Definitely open to interpretation. But it could've been worse. He could have said it's a very big step.

title: Indiscretion
line: You didn't say that, did you?

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't think so.

title: Indiscretion
line: Oh, that's good, anyway. So, what does he do now?

title: Indiscretion
line: It's simple. He goes to Kasidy, admits that everything was his fault, and pledges his undying love.

title: Indiscretion
line: That sounds a little extreme to me. What if he just tells her he made a mistake, there had been a misunderstanding, and that he really would like her to live on the station?

title: Indiscretion
line: Could work. Assuming that's what you want.

title: Indiscretion
line: Captain, I would think long and hard before answering.

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't recall asking your opinion, Quark.

title: Indiscretion
line: Well maybe you should. I mean, who knows more about women than me?

title: Indiscretion
line: Everyone.

title: Indiscretion
line: You humans. All you want to do is please your women. You want them to be your friends. But we Ferengi know better. Women are the enemy and we treat them accordingly. The key is to never let them get the upper hand. If she says she doesn't see you enough, threaten to see her even less. If she wants more gifts, take back the ones you've already given her. It's all about control.

title: Indiscretion
line: What if your woman leaves you?

title: Indiscretion
line: That's what holosuites are for.

title: Indiscretion
line: It's a wonder the Ferengi reproduce at all.

title: Indiscretion
line: So, you never answered the question. Do you want her to stay or not?

title: Indiscretion
line: I appreciate all the advice. I'll let you know how it turns out.

title: Indiscretion
line: So, just between you and me, what do you think about Kasidy moving onto the station?

title: Indiscretion
line: It's a big step.

title: Indiscretion
line: A very big step.

title: Indiscretion
line: She didn't just crash. These are phaser hits.

title: Indiscretion
line: Looks like she put up quite a fight.

title: Indiscretion
line: And paid for it.

title: Indiscretion
line: Twelve graves.

title: Indiscretion
line: There were eighteen crewmembers and thirty two prisoners aboard.

title: Indiscretion
line: So where's everybody else?

title: Indiscretion
line: First things first.

title: Indiscretion
line: What are you doing?

title: Indiscretion
line: We need to identify these bodies.

title: Indiscretion
line: I'll help.

title: Indiscretion
line: No. Our funeral rites are very strict. It would dishonor the dead for a non-Cardassian to view the remains.

title: Indiscretion
line: There could be Bajorans buried here too.

title: Indiscretion
line: No doubt. But if memory's correct, Bajorans are much more concerned with the souls of the dead than they are with the physical remains. How did Kai Meressa put it? What remains after death is but a shell, a sign that the pagh has begun its final journey to the Prophets. Please, Major, don't make this any more difficult for me than it already is.

title: Indiscretion
line: I have a list of the missing Bajorans. I should be able to identify them from the family imprints on their earrings. I'll work on the Ravinok. I should be able to get something from the ship's computers.

title: Indiscretion
line: You'll need the command codes.

title: Indiscretion
line: Standard Cardassian military codes from six years ago, right?

title: Indiscretion
line: Yes.

title: Indiscretion
line: I got them from Bajoran intelligence before we left.

title: Indiscretion
line: Very good, Major. Very good.

title: Indiscretion
line: Dukat, I was able to reactivate the Dukat. What was her name? I recognize a Bajoran pledge bracelet when I see one.

title: Indiscretion
line: Her name was Tora Naprem. You see, Major, you're not the only one who had a friend aboard that ship.

title: Indiscretion
line: Friend? Is that all she was? I see. Don't worry, Dukat. You're not the only Cardassian officer who kept a Bajoran mistress.

title: Indiscretion
line: It wasn't like that. Naprem and I loved each other.

title: Indiscretion
line: The head of the Occupation in love with a Bajoran?

title: Indiscretion
line: Ironic, isn't it?

title: Indiscretion
line: Did your wife know?

title: Indiscretion
line: No. And she's never going to find out. Now if you don't mind, Major, I'd rather not talk about this right now. Here are the earrings you wanted.

title: Indiscretion
line: If Lorit's dead, he's not buried here. According to the ship's computers, the Ravinok was attacked by two unidentified warships. The attackers chased the Ravinok here and must have forced her to crash-land.

title: Indiscretion
line: Then the survivors could have been captured and taken away.

title: Indiscretion
line: Or they could still be here somewhere on this planet.

title: Indiscretion
line: We should go up in the runabout and scan for them from orbit.

title: Indiscretion
line: Too much ionic interference. The sensors would never be able to pick up their life signs. There may be another way. In these conditions, tricorder readings will only be about twelve meters, but that should be enough.

title: Indiscretion
line: Enough for what?

title: Indiscretion
line: During the occupation, Bajoran resistance fighters carried subdermal implants of tritonium isotopes. The idea was that if they were captured, they could activate the implant which would leave a trail of isotopes so they could be tracked and rescued. I think I have something. That way.

title: Indiscretion
line: Let's go.

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't know why we have to stop.

title: Indiscretion
line: For one thing, I can't see two meters ahead of us. And anyway we could both use the rest. So stop pacing and sit down.

title: Indiscretion
line: What is it?

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't know. I sat on something. I sat on something!

title: Indiscretion
line: Let me see.

title: Indiscretion
line: Ooo, get it out.

title: Indiscretion
line: Well keep still and let me see what I can do.

title: Indiscretion
line: Get it out!

title: Indiscretion
line: Oh. This is going to hurt.

title: Indiscretion
line: It already hurts. Just take it out.

title: Indiscretion
line: If you say so.

title: Indiscretion
line: OW!

title: Indiscretion
line: Ouch. Run this dermal regenerator over the wound.

title: Indiscretion
line: This isn't funny.

title: Indiscretion
line: It is from this angle.

title: Indiscretion
line: You know what's even funnier? This doesn't work.

title: Indiscretion
line: You have to activate it.

title: Indiscretion
line: Ah. Ah, yes. Oh, much better.

title: Indiscretion
line: You probably should eat one of these.

title: Indiscretion
line: Ah, I haven't had field rations in a very long time. I'm sure they haven't improved a bit.

title: Indiscretion
line: Actually, they've gotten a little worse. Tell me something.

title: Indiscretion
line: What?

title: Indiscretion
line: Who's Tora Ziyal? When I reactivated the Ravinok's computer, I downloaded the manifest. There were two civilians on board in addition to the prisoners and crew. One was your friend, Tora Naprem, and the other was Tora Ziyal, a thirteen year-old girl.

title: Indiscretion
line: I suppose you wouldn't believe me if I told you she was Naprem's sister?

title: Indiscretion
line: Ziyal's a Cardassian name. The way I see it, there's only one explanation. Ziyal was Naprem's daughter, and you

title: Indiscretion
line: I was her father.

title: Indiscretion
line: Now I know why you're in such a hurry to find the survivors. You're hoping that she's still alive and you can rescue her.

title: Indiscretion
line: Not quite. You see, if my daughter is still alive, I'll have no choice but to kill her.

title: Indiscretion
line: You know I'm not going to let you do it. I mean it, Dukat. You are not going to kill that girl.

title: Indiscretion
line: Major, why don't you worry about the other survivors and let me worry about Ziyal. After all, she is my daughter.

title: Indiscretion
line: That's right. She's your daughter. And there is nothing more important to Cardassians than family. At least that's what your people are always saying.

title: Indiscretion
line: I have a wife and seven children. They are my family. They are the ones I must protect.

title: Indiscretion
line: Well, you should have thought of that before you got involved with Naprem.

title: Indiscretion
line: You're right. I should have. But I made a mistake. A mistake I intend to correct.

title: Indiscretion
line: You don't have to take her back to Cardassia with you. Let me take her to Bajor. No one has to know that you're her father.

title: Indiscretion
line: What kind of life would that be for her? Your people have never exactly welcomed half-Cardassian children into your society. That's why I sent her and her mother away in the first place. I knew the Occupation was coming to an end, and that there'd be no place for them on Bajor or Cardassia.

title: Indiscretion
line: So you sent them to a prison camp.

title: Indiscretion
line: They were not on their way to a prison camp. The Ravinok was supposed to rendezvous with a freighter which would take Naprem and Ziyal to Lissepia, where they could live out their lives in some sort of peace.

title: Indiscretion
line: I don't understand. If you cared enough to help Ziyal then, how can you be thinking about killing her now? Why not send her away again?

title: Indiscretion
line: Because my position isn't nearly as stable as it once was. By aligning myself with the new civilian government, I've made many enemies. Enemies that wouldn't hesitate to use Ziyal against me.

title: Indiscretion
line: Listen to you. It's not your wife or your seven children you're protecting, it's you.

title: Indiscretion
line: By protecting myself, I am protecting them.

title: Indiscretion
line: And the only one who suffers is Ziyal. You would kill your own daughter to save your career. I don't understand you. You said you loved Naprem. I saw you crying at her grave.

title: Indiscretion
line: I did love her. And when I bury Ziyal, I'll weep over her grave just as I wept over her mother's. But that will not stop me from doing what I have to do. Do you understand? And when the time comes, I suggest you stay out of my way.

title: Indiscretion
line: Good morning, Jake-o.

title: Indiscretion

line: A Vulcan geological survey team was mining bakrinium on an uncharted planet when they accidentally unearthed some ancient ruins. They brought back several artifacts to study, including the cloth.

It is said its return will bring back a new era of glory for the Klingon Empire. With the Sword, the Emperor will be able to unite my people again.

title: The Sword of Kahless
