line: To be perfectly honest, Doctor, I wish you were both going with me. I could use the company. I doubt that a shape-shifter is will be welcome on Earth at the moment.

title: Homefront
line: No one can hold you responsible for what your people are doing.

title: Homefront
line: Oh really? Well, I'd better get over to the Lakota. We'll be leaving shortly.

title: Homefront
line: Good luck.

title: Homefront
line: I don't believe in luck. But I appreciate the sentiment.

title: Homefront
line: Well, we'd better get out of these uniforms.

title: Homefront
line: The Lakota's gone to warp.

title: Homefront
line: When was the last time the wormhole opened?

title: Homefront
line: Twelve hours ago.

title: Homefront
line: Perhaps it has returned to normal.

title: Homefront
line: I suppose so.

title: Homefront
line: You sound disappointed, Major.

title: Homefront
line: I guess I am. Part of me was hoping that the Prophets were behind it. That they were finally going to show themselves to the Bajoran people.

title: Homefront
line: I prefer Klingon beliefs.

title: Homefront
line: I suppose your gods aren't as cryptic as ours.

title: Homefront
line: Our gods are dead. Ancient Klingon warriors slew them a millennia ago. They were more trouble than they were worth.

title: Homefront
line: I don't think I'll ever understand Klingons.

title: Homefront
line: Don't worry about it, Major. Nobody does. That's the way they like it.

title: Homefront
line: Ben.

title: Homefront
line: Admiral Leyton. Good to see you again, sir.

title: Homefront
line: Captain Sisko. This is my adjutant, Commander Benteen. Benjamin was my executive officer aboard the Okinawa. And a damn fine one too.

title: Homefront
line: I did all right.

title: Homefront
line: Ah, don't be modest. Admiral Leyton has had his share of executive officers and you're the only one he ever speaks fondly of.

title: Homefront
line: Present company excluded.

title: Homefront
line: Admiral Leyton is the one who recommended me for the job on Deep Space Nine.

title: Homefront
line: One of my better ideas. You must be Odo.

title: Homefront
line: That's right.

title: Homefront
line: Forgive me for staring, but you're the first changeling I've ever met.

title: Homefront
line: That you know of.

title: Homefront
line: I sympathize with your problem. Uncovering changeling infiltrators is no easy task.

title: Homefront
line: Well, with the help of the two of you, I trust it'll be a little easier.

title: Homefront
line: What exactly do you want us to do?

title: Homefront
line: We'd like to confer with you and Odo, see if there's anything about the Founders you left out of your official reports.

title: Homefront
line: I'll help any way I can, but I think you'll find my reports were quite thorough.

title: Homefront
line: Admiral, I doubt you brought us all this way just for a debriefing.

title: Homefront
line: Of course not. Ben, Earth is in danger. Maybe the greatest danger it's faced since the last world war. Something has to be done about these shape-shifters. Which is why you're here. You know more about the Dominion than anyone in Starfleet. And so, effective immediately, I'm making you acting head of Starfleet Security here on Earth.

title: Homefront
line: Congratulations, Captain.

title: Homefront
line: This is one beautiful fish. Seems a shame to eat a trout this pretty. Why, you should thank me for the privilege of simply looking at it. Well, go on, take a bite. It won't bite you back. Now, I don't want to see anybody studying the dessert menu. If you order anything but the bread pudding soufflé, you'll be making a mistake you will regret the rest of your lives.

title: Homefront
line: You should listen to him. The man knows his bread pudding.

title: Homefront
line: Benjamin!

title: Homefront
line: Dad.

title: Homefront
line: Jake-o.

title: Homefront
line: Hey.

title: Homefront
line: When are you going to stop growing? If you keep this up, you'll be bumping your head on that alligator before too long.

title: Homefront
line: I remember when you used to tell me that alligator was just in stasis, and you let it out at night to guard the restaurant.

title: Homefront
line: I had to stop doing that. It got to be too much trouble wrestling it back up to the ceiling every morning. Come on. I'll get Nathan to bring you both something to eat and we can catch up. Nathan, some gumbo for these fine young men.

title: Homefront
line: Yes, sah.

title: Homefront
line: So, where's this shape-shifting fellow you were coming with?

title: Homefront
line: With things the way they are, Odo thought it would be better if he stayed at Starfleet Headquarters.

title: Homefront
line: I don't blame him. I haven't seen people so nervous since the Borg scare. Me, personally, I'd like to meet him. Though I have to admit, I'm a little suspicious about anyone who doesn't eat.

title: Homefront
line: Grandpa.

title: Homefront
line: Well, aren't you going to eat anything?

title: Homefront
line: I ate before you got here. Son, don't look at me that way.

title: Homefront
line: You've lost weight.

title: Homefront
line: You think so?

title: Homefront
line: The doctors said you have to keep your weight up.

title: Homefront
line: Don't you start, too. I have a vat of crayfish in the back that needs cleaning and it's got your name on it. Now I'm going to say this one time and one time only. I am fine. I'm happy, I'm healthy, and I'm planning on celebrating at least fifty more birthdays. Satisfied?

title: Homefront
line: Gumbo's as good as I remember.

title: Homefront
line: Starfleet must be taking the shape-shifters pretty seriously to have you come all the way back here.

title: Homefront
line: It is serious, Dad.

title: Homefront
line: Twenty seven people murdered right here on Earth. Never thought I'd see the day. But now that my son's on the case, I feel a lot better.

title: Homefront
line: Jake!

title: Homefront
line: Nog?

title: Homefront
line: Captain Sisko. What do you think?

title: Homefront
line: You look good, Cadet.

title: Homefront
line: You think so?

title: Homefront
line: Nog, I thought I was going to see you tomorrow at the Academy.

title: Homefront
line: You are. I'm just here for dinner. Nathan, the usual.

title: Homefront
line: I didn't know you liked Creole food.

title: Homefront
line: I don't. I like tube grubs, and your father is the only person on this planet who can get me live ones.

title: Homefront
line: I've been thinking of adding them to our menu. Of course I'll have to cook them for my human customers, serve them with a nice remoulade.

title: Homefront
line: Cook them? What good are tube grubs if they don't wriggle on the way down?

title: Homefront
line: So how's everything at the Academy?

title: Homefront
line: Jake, they call it the Academy, but what it really is is school.

title: Homefront
line: I want to hear about it.

title: Homefront
line: It's a lot of work. Lots of classes, lots of studying. I'm doing okay. Now where are those tube grubs?

title: Homefront
line: Good night. You come back soon. Come on, Ben. I've got a nice bottle of cognac I've been saving for a special occasion, and I think this qualifies.

title: Homefront
line: I think you're right.

title: Homefront
line: Ah. There's nothing like a full stomach to make life worth living.

title: Homefront
line: So, you going to tell me what's on your mind or not?

title: Homefront
line: What do you mean?

title: Homefront
line: I mean you didn't stay here until closing just to get one more root beer. Something's up.

title: Homefront
line: My friend the writer. Always looking for a good story.

title: Homefront
line: If you don't want to tell me, fine. Don't tell me.

title: Homefront
line: It's nothing. It's stupid.

title: Homefront
line: All right. Forget about it.

title: Homefront
line: It's just the Academy is different than I thought it would be.

title: Homefront
line: Different how?

title: Homefront
line: Some of the cadets. They're kind of standoffish, especially the upperclassmen.

title: Homefront
line: Because you're a Ferengi?

title: Homefront
line: That's what I thought at first. But then I heard some of the other freshmen complaining about the same thing.

title: Homefront
line: Complaining about what?

title: Homefront
line: Little things. For instance, there's this group called Red Squad made up of all the top students. They're always going off on trips, getting special training. None of them will even talk to me.

title: Homefront
line: You've only been in the Academy for a month. You can't expect to fit in right away. Who knows, one of these days you might even be in Red Squad. I'm sure if you let them get to know you, show them you're a good guy to be around, everything'll work out.

title: Homefront
line: I am a good guy to be around, aren't I?

title: Homefront
line: I always thought so.

title: Homefront
line: Mister President, I'd like to introduce Captain Sisko. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: Captain. I've seen your record. Most exemplary.

title: Homefront
line: Thank you, sir.

title: Homefront
line: Captain Sisko has several suggestions on how to combat Dominion infiltration. I think you'll find them very interesting. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: Hmm. I understand the need for increased security, but blood screenings? Phaser sweeps?

title: Homefront
line: They've proven very effective on Deep Space Nine. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: I'm sure they have. But I hope you'll keep in mind that this is Earth, and not a military installation.

title: Homefront
line: Which means it's a lot more vulnerable. We have to take precautions. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: Precautions may be advisable, but I will not disrupt the lives of the population. Despite what happened at Antwerp, I believe the changeling threat to be somewhat less serious than Starfleet does.

title: Homefront
line: Mister President, I assure you the threat is real. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: For all we know, there was only one changeling on Earth, and he may not even be here anymore.

title: Homefront
line: But if he is here, we have a problem. There's no telling how much damage one changeling could do. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: Forgive me for saying so, Captain, but you sound a little paranoid.

title: Homefront
line: Do I?

title: Homefront
line: Forgive the intrusion, Mister President, but as you can see, Starfleet has every right to be concerned.

title: Homefront
line: Allow me to introduce Odo, my Chief of Security. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: A very effective entrance, Mister Odo.

title: Homefront
line: One that never should have been allowed to take place. Admiral Leyton and Captain Sisko walked in here without being searched, without being blood-tested, and without having their possessions subjected to phaser sweeps.

title: Homefront
line: If Odo was a Dominion infiltrator, he could have killed you.

title: Homefront
line: Or replaced you. The way security is now, a changeling could get anywhere on Earth, replace anyone, even you.

title: Homefront
line: Mister President, all we want is your permission to increase security at Federation and Starfleet installations here on Earth. Blood tests will be limited to high-ranking Federation officials, Starfleet officers and their families. The average citizen won't even notice the difference. I wish these security measures were not necessary, but the safety of Earth and the entire Federation depends on them. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: You present a convincing argument, Captain. It seems I have no choice but to accept your proposals.

title: Homefront
line: Thank you, sir. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: Don't thank me. If I could think of another solution, I would use it. It took centuries for Earth to evolve into the peaceful haven it is today. I would hate to be remembered as the Federation President who destroyed paradise.

title: Homefront
line: We're not looking to destroy paradise, Mister President. We're looking to save it.

title: Homefront
line: Activate the phaser.

title: Homefront
line: That's enough. How do you feel?

title: Homefront
line: That time I definitely experienced discomfort.

title: Homefront
line: What was the setting?

title: Homefront
line: Three point one. If we set the phasers at three point four, we should be able to stun any changeling we hit and force them back into a gelatinous state.

title: Homefront
line: I'd push it to three point five just to be on the safe side. But if you want to do any more tests, you'll have to get another guinea pig. I've been shot quite enough for one day.

title: Homefront
line: Three point five it is. I want these units installed in every room at Starfleet and Federation Headquarters, then start working on the orbital stations.

title: Homefront
line: We'll have them in place by tomorrow night. I want to thank you, Captain.

title: Homefront
line: Thank me? For what?

title: Homefront
line: For convincing the President to implement these security measures. It feels like we're finally on the right track.

title: Homefront
line: Huh. You'd think she would have thanked me as well. I'm the one who got shot thirteen times today.

title: Homefront
line: Captain Sisko. I hope I'm not interrupting anything.

title: Homefront
line: We were just about finished.

title: Homefront
line: Can I speak to you for a minute? In private.

title: Homefront
line: Captain, I just want to say I appreciate everything you've done for me so far, and

title: Homefront
line: Jake says you're having difficulty in school.

title: Homefront
line: He told you that?

title: Homefront
line: He tells me everything.

title: Homefront
line: I don't want you to get the wrong idea.

title: Homefront
line: Nog, you and I both knew that it was going to take a while for you to adjust to the Academy and for the Academy to adjust to you.

title: Homefront
line: I know, but it turned out to be even more difficult than I expected.

title: Homefront
line: You're just going to have to stick with it.

title: Homefront
line: And I intend to. In fact, I think I've come up with something to help me make some new friends.

title: Homefront
line: Good.

title: Homefront
line: But I need your help. I want to join Red Squad.

title: Homefront
line: Red Squad?

title: Homefront
line: What do you think?

title: Homefront
line: I don't know what to think. I've never heard of it.

title: Homefront
line: It's an elite squad of cadets at the Academy. You know, the best of the best. They get special classes, simulated missions, off-campus training sessions, all kinds of things.

title: Homefront
line: A group of elite cadets? They never had anything like that when I was at the Academy.

title: Homefront
line: It's pretty new. It's a way of rewarding excellence among the cadets. I have the grades to qualify, but I need to be sponsored by a high-ranking officer.

title: Homefront
line: And you want me to put your name in for consideration?

title: Homefront
line: All I'm asking for is a chance to prove myself.

title: Homefront
line: I'm kind of busy right now, Nog. But if I get the chance, I'll see what I can do.

title: Homefront
line: Thank you, sir. This means a lot to me.

title: Homefront
line: I can see that. Dismissed, Cadet.

title: Homefront
line: Yes, sir.

title: Homefront
line: Well, look who's here. Come in, stranger.

title: Homefront
line: Sorry. I haven't been around much lately. Things have gotten a little busy.

title: Homefront
line: You want to tell me about it?

title: Homefront
line: I'm afraid I can't.

title: Homefront
line: You'd think that Admiral could spare you for a few hours a day to visit your father. With you in San Francisco and Jake off visiting that school in New Zealand, it's like the two of you aren't even here.

title: Homefront
line: You know, Dad, you could come and visit us at the station once in a while.

title: Homefront
line: Don't start that again. Earth's my home. It's where I belong. Besides, what would happen to the restaurant if I went gallivanting around the galaxy? You think Nathan can handle this place on his own?

title: Homefront
line: Nathan will be running things around here sooner than you think if you don't take better care of yourself. I had a talk with your doctor and he tells me that you haven't been in to see him for eight months.

title: Homefront
line: The man's an idiot. He's lived in New Orleans twenty years and can't tell the difference between Creole food and Cajun food.

title: Homefront
line: Maybe not, but he can tell the difference between a healthy body and one with progressive atherosclerosis. He says that if you don't come in for vascular regeneration therapy, that this restaurant will be looking for a new owner.

title: Homefront
line: Ben, at my age, staying healthy is a full time job, and I am too old to work two jobs. Now, how long until you're due back at Starfleet Headquarters?

title: Homefront
line: I've got about an hour.

title: Homefront
line: Just enough time to take a walk to Audubon Park. You up for a stroll with your old man?

title: Homefront
line: I can't think of anything I'd rather do.

title: Homefront
line: Nathan, don't forget to stir the gumbo.

title: Homefront
line: Odo. That was really something. I've never seen you imitate a lifeform before.

title: Homefront
line: Well, I was just taking a little aerial tour of San Francisco. It's quite nice. Not as ancient as the cities on Bajor but almost as impressive.

title: Homefront
line: It makes me wonder how many other changelings might be flying around up there.

title: Homefront
line: If all they're doing is flying around imitating seagulls, we don't have much to worry about.

title: Homefront
line: I doubt that other changelings are wasting their time imitating birds. They don't all share Odo's lack of skill when it comes to mimicking humans.

title: Homefront
line: That's right, they don't. I'm glad you're keeping that in mind.

title: Homefront
line: Well, if you ask me, that was a pretty convincing seagull.

title: Homefront
line: Thank you. Though I'm not sure the gulls would agree.

title: Homefront
line: Commander, I think we've taken up enough of Mister Odo's time. Keep practicing. You'll have those birds fooled in no time.

title: Homefront
line: Admiral.

title: Homefront
line: Yes.

title: Homefront
line: I know that Starfleet Command has always been a little uneasy about a changeling working in their midst. I just wanted to say how much I appreciate the trust you've shown in me. Thank you.

title: Homefront
line: You're welcome.

title: Homefront
line: Well done, Odo.

title: Homefront
line: Are you all right?

title: Homefront
line: I'm fine.

title: Homefront
line: How did you know he wasn't me?

title: Homefront
line: I'm not sure exactly. It's as if I could feel the changeling's hostility toward me.

title: Homefront
line: You're the only changeling who's ever harmed one of his own people. I'm sure that hasn't made you many friends.

title: Homefront
line: What I'd like to know is, why was he imitating me?

title: Homefront
line: You have access to all our security procedures, all our protocols. That makes you a logical target.

title: Homefront
line: I suppose so.

title: Homefront
line: The bottom line is a changeling infiltrated the grounds of Starfleet Headquarters, imitated the Admiral, and got away scot-free. Our security measures aren't working.

title: Homefront
line: We're doing everything the President will let us do.

title: Homefront
line: Maybe that's not enough.

title: Homefront
line: We could talk to the President again.

title: Homefront
line: I'm afraid that would be a waste of time. Jaresh-Inyo would be a fine president in peacetime, but we have a war on our hands. He doesn't seem to understand that. All he cares about is not upsetting people. But humans are tougher than he thinks. We've created a paradise here and we're willing to fight to protect it.

title: Homefront
line: And you think the President isn't willing to fight?

title: Homefront
line: I think the President is a long way from home. This isn't his world. We can't expect him to care about it the way we do.

title: Homefront
line: Sisko here.

title: Homefront
line: Captain, your son's trying to contact you. He says it's urgent.

title: Homefront
line: Put him through.

title: Homefront
line: Dad, you'd better get down here right away.

title: Homefront
line: What's wrong?

title: Homefront
line: It's Grandpa. He's been arrested.

title: Homefront
line: What's going on here?

title: Homefront
line: Captain, we never meant for things to get out of hand.

title: Homefront
line: What did you think would happen? Storming in here and accusing me and my grandson of being a couple of shape-shifters.

title: Homefront
line: We never accused you of being a shape-shifter, Mister Sisko. We were just carrying out our orders. All family members of Starfleet personnel are required to submit to blood screenings. No exceptions.

title: Homefront
line: That's the most ridiculous thing I ever heard of. Do you believe that?

title: Homefront
line: I should. I signed the orders myself.

title: Homefront
line: Now why would you go and do a stupid thing like that?

title: Homefront
line: Dad, it has to be done.

title: Homefront
line: Grandpa, look, I'll take the test first. Go ahead.

title: Homefront
line: Now me.

title: Homefront
line: Sir, that's not necessary.

title: Homefront
line: Do it anyway.

title: Homefront
line: it's your turn.

title: Homefront
line: Jake, do you think I'm a shape-shifter?

title: Homefront
line: Come on, Grandpa.

title: Homefront
line: Answer the question.

title: Homefront
line: No, I don't think you're a shape-shifter.

title: Homefront
line: At least somebody in my family has some sense.

title: Homefront
line: Dad!

title: Homefront
line: I don't want to hear about it. You take these two vampires and tell them to either sit down and grab a menu or get out of my restaurant.

title: Homefront
line: Jake, get them a menu.

title: Homefront
line: But sir.

title: Homefront
line: I would recommend the shrimp Creole. Look, Dad

title: Homefront
line: I don't want to hear it.

title: Homefront
line: Listen to me. You have got to take the test.

title: Homefront
line: Why should I? If I were an enemy spy looking to replace someone, I think I could come up with better choices than an old chef.

title: Homefront
line: Yeah, you're probably right. But this isn't about you. We've got civilian families living on starships and Starfleet installations all over the Federation. The only way we can secure those facilities is to test everyone there, whether they wear a uniform or not.

title: Homefront
line: I'm not living on a Starfleet installation.

title: Homefront
line: Dad, if we're going to test the family members of one Starfleet officer, we must to test them all.

title: Homefront
line: You may want to test everyone, but that doesn't mean we all have to cooperate. I didn't take an oath to Starfleet. Neither did Jake or your sister or anyone in your family. We have rights, Ben, including the right to be as stubborn or thickheaded as we want.

title: Homefront
line: Damn it, Dad. Can't you cooperate just one time? You don't take your medication, you don't go to the doctor, you won't let Judith help you in the restaurant. Just one time, please do what you're asked.

title: Homefront
line: I wish I could, but what you're asking me to do is wrong. You can't go around making people prove they are who they say they are. That's no way to live and I'm not going to go along with it. Now, if you want to make yourself useful, start some water boiling for the shrimp.

title: Homefront
line: Come on, Dad. Don't be this way. If I have to, I will get a warrant

title: Homefront
line: And what? Hold me down and force me to give you my blood? Because that's the only way you'll get. Damn it. Now look what I've done.

title: Homefront
line: Jake?

title: Homefront
line: Yeah?

title: Homefront
line: I've got a dermal regenerator under the. Benjamin Lafayette Sisko. What the hell has gotten into your head? You actually thought I was one of them, didn't you?

title: Homefront
line: I don't know. I wasn't sure.

title: Homefront
line: This business has got you so twisted around you can't think straight. You're seeing shape-shifters everywhere. Maybe you ought to think about something for a minute. If I was a smart shape-shifter, a really good one, the first thing I would do would be to grab some poor soul off the street, absorb every ounce of his blood, and let it out on cue whenever someone like you tried to test me. Don't you see? There isn't a test that's been created a smart man can't find his way around. You aren't going to catch shape-shifters using some gadget. The only thing you can count on in this life is

title: Homefront
line: Grandpa!

title: Homefront
line: The EMT's said he'd be okay and they were right. It turns out it was just a mild stroke brought on by his atherosclerosis.

title: Homefront
line: How's Jake handling it?

title: Homefront
line: He is very upset. He knows as well as I do that if my father doesn't take better care of himself

title: Homefront
line: I've found that when it comes to doing what's best for you, you humanoids have the distressing habit of doing the exact opposite.

title: Homefront
line: I can't argue with that. But what bothers me is that for a few minutes there, I really believed that my own father was a changeling.

title: Homefront
line: A reasonable assumption, considering the circumstances.

title: Homefront
line: I don't care if it's reasonable or not. But when a son can't trust his own father?

title: Homefront
line: That's why my people came here. To undermine the trust and mutual understanding the Federation is built on.

title: Homefront
line: But what if my father's right? What if all our precautions turn out to be useless?

title: Homefront
line: Maybe they will. But that doesn't mean you should give up. My people are here and you've got to fight them with whatever you've got.

title: Homefront
line: I hope you don't take this the wrong way, Constable, but there are times I wish you'd never found your people.

title: Homefront
line: Believe me, Captain, sometimes I feel the same way.

title: Homefront
line: Grandpa, would you please sit down?

title: Homefront
line: Enjoy your meal. Your food'll be right out.

title: Homefront
line: What's that look supposed to mean?

title: Homefront
line: You sat down.

title: Homefront
line: You're damn right I sat down. I feel terrible.

title: Homefront
line: You should be in bed.

title: Homefront
line: Jake, the only time you should be in bed is if you're sleeping, dying, or making love to a beautiful woman. I'm not tired, I'm not dying, and the truth is I'm too old for beautiful women, so I might as well be here. Your father's the one you should be worried about.

title: Homefront
line: Dad? Why?

title: Homefront
line: I've never seen him so tense. It's like he's carrying the weight of the world on his shoulders.

title: Homefront
line: He is.

title: Homefront
line: I suppose he is at that.

title: Homefront
line: What happened?

title: Homefront
line: I don't know. The whole block's dark.

title: Homefront
line: You all right?

title: Homefront
line: I'm fine. Admiral, what's going on?

title: Homefront
line: From what we can tell, Earth's entire power relay system's been knocked offline. Even Starfleet's emergency backup's been affected.

title: Homefront
line: How could that happen?

title: Homefront
line: I don't know, but if you ask me, there's only one possible explanation.

title: Homefront
line: Sabotage.

title: Homefront
line: The changelings.

title: Homefront
line: Take down the power relays, and you neutralize sensors, transporters, surface-based defense installations.

title: Homefront
line: In other words, Earth is defenseless.

title: Homefront
line: If the Dominion attacks now, we don't stand a chance.

title: Homefront
line: I'm not interested in excuses. It is imperative we get the power relay system functioning again.

title: Homefront
line: Mister President. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: How did you people get here?

title: Homefront
line: We contacted the Lakota and used their transporters. Mister President, as acting head of Earth Security, I must advise you to declare a State of Emergency. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: You're serious. With the exception of the Borg incident, there hasn't been a State of Emergency declared on Earth in a century.

title: Homefront
line: I am aware of that, but I have reason to believe that a Dominion warfleet may be in the Alpha Quadrant headed for Earth. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: Do you have evidence to back this up?

title: Homefront
line: Just before we left Deep Space Nine, the wormhole was exhibiting some unusual behavior, opening and closing for no apparent reason.

title: Homefront
line: We didn't detect any ships coming through at the time, but the Dominion might have been using some kind of cloaking technology. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: I wasn't aware the Dominion had cloaking technology.

title: Homefront
line: The combined Cardassian and Romulan fleet that the Dominion destroyed in the Gamma Quadrant was equipped with cloaking devices. Who knows what my people might have taken from the wreckage? JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: How long until the power relays are fixed?

title: Homefront
line: From what we can tell, the changelings infected the system with some kind of self-replicating computer protocol. It jumped from one power relay to the next, disrupting every system it came in contact with.

title: Homefront
line: The only way to correct the problem is to shut down the entire grid, purge all the operating systems, and restart the relays.

title: Homefront
line: And that could take days.

title: Homefront
line: Which is why it is imperative that you declare a State of Emergency. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: What good will that do when we have no way to defend ourselves?

title: Homefront
line: Mister President, we can use the Lakota's transporters and communications system to mobilize every Starfleet officer on Earth in less than twelve hours. We've been preparing for something like this for a long time. We have stockpiles of phaser rifles, personal forcefields, photon grenades, enough to equip an entire army. I can start getting men on the streets immediately. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: What you're asking me to do is declare martial law.

title: Homefront
line: What I'm asking you to do is let us defend this planet. We don't know what the changelings will do next, but we have to be ready for them. Ben, tell him.

title: Homefront
line: Sir, the thought of filling the streets with armed troops is as disturbing to me as it is to you, but not as disturbing as the thought of a Jem'Hadar army landing on Earth without opposition. The Jem'Hadar are the most brutal and efficient soldiers I've ever encountered. They don't care about the conventions of war or protecting civilians. They will not limit themselves to military targets. They'll be waging the kind of war that Earth hasn't seen since the founding of the Federation.

title: Homefront
line: At the same time, my people will continue to undermine Earth's defenses in any way they can. This power outage is only the beginning. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: I never sought this job. I was content to simply represent my people on the Federation Council. When they asked me to submit my name for election, I almost said no. Today I wish I had.

title: Homefront
line: We appreciate your feelings, Mister President, but we don't have time for regrets. You accepted the job and now it's yours.

title: Homefront
line: Mister President, there are people all over this planet right now huddled in the dark, terrified about what might happen next. They're waiting for a sign, something to reassure them that everything will be all right. But they won't wait long. Fear is a powerful and dangerous thing. And if you don't act, if you don't show them that they're not alone, then fear will surely take over.

title: Homefront
line: Give us the authority we need, Mister President, and we will take care of the rest. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: Earth is in your hands, gentlemen. Do what needs to be done.

title: Homefront
line: Thank you, sir. You've made the right decision. JARESH-

title: Homefront
line: I hope you're right, for all our sakes.

title: Homefront
line: Grandpa! Grandpa, wake up.

title: Homefront
line: I'm not sleeping. I'm checking my eyelids for holes.

title: Homefront
line: You'd better come take a look at this.

title: Paradise Lost
line: It'll be good to have you home again, Benjamin.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Dad, you know that this isn't exactly a vacation. I'll be spending most of my time in San Francisco at Starfleet Headquarters.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Ben, Earth is in danger. Something has to be done about these shape-shifters. You know more about the Dominion than anyone in Starfleet. And so, effective immediately, I'm making you acting head of Starfleet Security here on Earth.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Forgive the intrusion, Mister President, but as you can see, Starfleet has every right to be concerned.

title: Paradise Lost
line: If Odo was a Dominion infiltrator, he could have killed you.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You actually thought I was one of them, didn't you?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I don't know. I wasn't sure.

title: Paradise Lost
line: This business has got you so twisted around you can't think straight.

title: Paradise Lost
line: A changeling infiltrated the grounds of Starfleet Headquarters, imitated the Admiral, and got away scot-free. Our security measures aren't working.

title: Paradise Lost
line: We're doing everything the President will let us do.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Maybe that's not enough.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Earth's entire power relay system's been knocked offline.

title: Paradise Lost
line: In other words, Earth is defenseless. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: What you're asking me to do is declare martial law.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What I'm asking you to do is let us defend this planet.

line: You'd better come take a look at this.

line: Come on. And now, the conclusion.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I don't like this. The more I read Starfleet's reports on the sabotage of the power relays, the more unanswered questions I have. How were the changelings able to infiltrate the Division of Planetary operations? Where did they get the codes for the Division's computer control network? And how did they even manage to disable every power relay on Earth at the same time?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Captain, have you ever heard of a group called Red Squad?

title: Paradise Lost
line: They're an elite team of Starfleet cadets. According to Nog, every student at the Academy wants to be a part of it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: That explains it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Explains what?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Well, according to this transporter log, a group called Red Squad was beamed back to Starfleet Academy twenty six minutes after the State of Emergency was declared.

title: Paradise Lost
line: That's strange. During the blackout, Starfleet mobilized hundreds of units. Why would they demobilize Red Squad?

title: Paradise Lost
line: That's why I brought it up. But if they're cadets I suppose Starfleet wanted to get them out of harm's way.

title: Paradise Lost
line: If that's true, how do you explain this? (Sisko calls up a file on his wall monitor. It reads as follows - From Commander, Starfleet to OIC Training Squadron 47, stardate 49334.53. Trans code 4747-23 routing Paris/satcom 5/Luna 6017/San Francisco. Message begins. Effective immediately. All members of CTS-47 designation Red Squad are hereby assigned to field duty patrolling Sol sector, Terra 1. Mission specific orders will be transmitted once all squadron personnel are on station. Message ends.)

title: Paradise Lost
line: Three hours later Starfleet Command issued an order assigning the entire Corps of Cadets to field duty.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Which means they weren't bringing Red Squad home for their protection.

title: Paradise Lost
line: So the question is, why would they demobilize Red Squad only to mobilize them again three hours later?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Lights.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Are you sure re-opening the restaurant is a good idea?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Jake, it's been four days since the power outage. Have you seen any Dominion invasion fleet?

title: Paradise Lost
line: No.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Neither have I. Besides, at my age, I don't have time to waste sitting at home being bored.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You know, there's hardly anyone on the streets. You're not going to have any customers.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Oh, I've got plenty of customers. Just look outside.

title: Paradise Lost
line: All I see are security officers.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And I bet not one of them has had a good meal in four days. Now you do your grandfather a favor and start chopping up the okra.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Captain Sisko, is there something I can do for you?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I need to talk to you about Red Squad.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Go on.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Are you aware that there's a transporter record of Red Squad being returned to the Academy not long after the power outage?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Are you saying that's in the official records?

title: Paradise Lost
line: That's right.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Is this a secure line?

title: Paradise Lost
line: It is at my end.

title: Paradise Lost
line: One moment.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Sorry, Captain, but I think you'll agree that this is a time for caution.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Absolutely.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Does Admiral Leyton know about this report?

title: Paradise Lost
line: He hasn't mentioned it to me.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Listen to me, Captain. I want that record erased before anyone else can see it. Is that understood?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'll take care of it immediately.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Good. That report could cause us a lot of trouble. I'm glad you spotted it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: So am I. I'd hate to see the members of Red Squad get into any trouble.

title: Paradise Lost
line: They're fine young men and women. When Leyton talked to me about using them I thought it was a mistake, but I must to admit they performed their mission admirably. I appreciate your call, Captain. I'm in your debt.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Well, that certainly raised more questions than it answered.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What did I tell you? As human as I ever was.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You seem pretty jovial today.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Is there a problem with that?

title: Paradise Lost
line: It's just, well, you didn't seem too happy about being tested a few days ago.

title: Paradise Lost
line: That was before the changelings sabotaged the power grid.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I know, but you have to admit you were pretty adamant about it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I don't understand you. When I didn't want to be tested, you made it an issue. Now that I'm cooperating, you're still not satisfied.

title: Paradise Lost
line: It's not you, Dad.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Then what is it?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'm not sure. Maybe I'm just being paranoid.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Captain, Jake said you wanted to see me.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Yes, I do.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You two talk. I'll go chill some tube grubs.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What can I do for you, sir?

title: Paradise Lost
line: It's about Red Squad.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Red Squad? Did you get me in?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Not just yet.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Too bad. Those guys are the best. They're the only people I know who aren't afraid of the Dominion.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Why is that?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I don't know. They're not scared of anything, I guess.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You seem to know them pretty well.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Jake told I should try to get to know them better, show them I'm a good guy. And so far it seems to be working. The truth is, I think they only like me because I know you.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Is that so?

title: Paradise Lost
line: You're kind of their hero. The man at the front line in the war with the Dominion.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'd like to meet some of these cadets. You think you could introduce me to one of them?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'm sorry. I can't do that, sir. The names of Red Squad members are supposed to be secret.

title: Paradise Lost
line: But you know who they are.

title: Paradise Lost
line: It's not easy keeping secrets from a Ferengi. But I feel funny about telling anyone else. Besides, if they found out I told you who they were, I'd never get in.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Cadet, you are obviously under the mistaken impression that I'm asking a favor. I want a name, and I want it now. And that is an order. Understood, Mister Nog?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Yes, sir.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Cadet Shepard reporting as ordered, Captain.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Riley Aldrin Shepard, Starfleet Service number C nine five three oh four six nine nine four two seven. A third year student at Starfleet Academy with a specialty in tactical operations.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Yes, sir.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Cadet, I have been reviewing a record of Red Squad activities on the night of the twenty third. The night of the power outage.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Record, sir? We were told that there was not going to be any written record.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Are you contradicting me, Cadet?

title: Paradise Lost
line: No, sir.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Good. Now who told you there wasn't to be a written record?

title: Paradise Lost
line: The briefing officer, sir.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I want that officer's name.

title: Paradise Lost
line: She didn't give us her name, sir, but she did say there would be no record of our actions and that our role would have to go unrecognized, at least for now.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Maybe if you'd done your job better, it would have. But you fouled it up, didn't you? You cadets did some sloppy work. Some damn sloppy work.

title: Paradise Lost
line: With all due respect, sir, that's not true, sir. The mission went perfectly. If anything, it was easier than the simulations.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Now son, if you think by lying to me you're going to save your own hide, you'd better forget it. Mistakes were made, and I will find out who's responsible.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'm not lying to you, sir. I was there. I was at Planetary Operations the whole time. If anything had gone wrong, I would have known about it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Is that so? All right, Cadet. Let's go over this step by step, from the time of your mission deployment until your return to base at nineteen hundred forty seven hours PST on the twenty third.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Yes, sir. We assembled on the Eastern Quad at seventeen hundred hours on the evening of the twenty third.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I assume by we you mean Red Squad?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Yes, sir. After assembly we were beamed aboard the Lakota. Once aboard we received our equipment and the necessary codes, and were transported directly to the Division of Planetary Operations in Lisbon.

title: Paradise Lost
line: At what time?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Oh four hundred hours exactly, local time of course.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Go on, Cadet.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Our contact inside the DPO gave us access to their computer control network. From there we used the access codes we were given, bypassed the security lockouts, and downloaded the disordering protocols into the network.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And from there the protocols spread to every power relay on the planet.

title: Paradise Lost
line: It was a pretty impressive sight, sir, watching those relays wink out one after another.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Sorry I missed it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: After that, all we had to do was sabotage the restart sequencers and get out. Like I said, sir, it was all by the numbers.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And are you sure that this cadet is telling the truth?

title: Paradise Lost
line: He admitted to committing acts of treason against the Federation. If he was going to lie, I think he would have made up a better story.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I take it that you gave him a blood screening.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I tested him myself. He's human.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Well then, let's say he is telling the truth, that his superior officers ordered him to sabotage the power relays. That still doesn't rule out Dominion involvement. For all we know, his superiors have been replaced by changelings.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I thought about that. But if it were changelings, what have they accomplished? There's been no invasion and power's been restored.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And Starfleet has fortified Earth. I see your point, Captain. So let's say you're right. Starfleet officers have sabotaged the power grid. What are you going to do about it?

title: Paradise Lost
line: That is the bottom line, isn't it? What am I going to do? These aren't evil people, Odo. These are people I've worked with. They're my friends, people I respect. How can I turn against them?

title: Paradise Lost
line: It seems to me, if they have committed treason against the Federation, the Federation that you swore to protect, you won't be turning against them. They will have turned against you.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Captain, I've been in politics for seventy years. I'm no stranger to overstatement and exaggeration. But the idea that Starfleet would plot to overthrow the Federation government is the single most astonishing accusation I have ever heard.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Sir, if you'll hear us out. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: As I intend to. But you'll forgive me if I remain somewhat skeptical. Now, you should start at the beginning.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Several months ago, I learned from one of my people that changelings had infiltrated the Federation. Not long after I gave this information to Starfleet, reports indicate that Admiral Leyton led a contingent of high ranking officers to meet with you and recommend implementation of sweeping security measures meant to protect Earth. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: And I rejected their suggestions as extreme.

title: Paradise Lost
line: It's no secret that Leyton disagreed with you, and despite your calls for calm, his concern about the Dominion threat continued to grow.

title: Paradise Lost
line: When the Antwerp Conference was bombed, Leyton became convinced that the changelings posed a greater threat to Earth than you were prepared to admit. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: And so Admiral Leyton approached me again, this time with you two at his side. And I agreed to his proposals.

title: Paradise Lost
line: To some of his proposals.

title: Paradise Lost
line: We believe that Admiral Leyton and his supporters weren't satisfied with the limited security procedures you authorized. They were convinced that extraordinary measures were necessary to counter the changeling threat.

title: Paradise Lost
line: More than that, they were determined to prove to you and to everyone else how vulnerable Earth was to a Dominion takeover. So they sabotaged the global power grid. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: Starfleet officers committing sabotage?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I know exactly how you feel, but it's the truth. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: I find that difficult to believe. Admiral Leyton may be somewhat grating and inflexible at times, but for a man of his accomplishments, a man of his distinguished record to commit treason?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'm sure the Admiral doesn't see it as treason. He would probably defend it as a desperate act of patriotism. He and his supporters think that their actions are both necessary and justified.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Not to mention effective. Think about it. The power grid fails, and the next thing you know Starfleet security officers are on the streets of every city, armed with phaser rifles, blood testing citizens at random. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: Your story has a certain logic to it, gentlemen, but what it lacks is proof.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You want proof? Order Admiral Leyton to withdraw his troops from the streets. See what he does. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: You think he would refuse a direct order from his Commander-in-Chief?

title: Paradise Lost
line: If he orders his troops to stand down, then I'm wrong and I'll offer my resignation. But I don't think that's going to happen. With those troops in place, Admiral Leyton controls Earth. And he's not going to give up that control until he's convinced that he has ended the Dominion threat. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: He may not have to give up anything. If what you say is true, if the power outage was part of Leyton's plan, then it's worked perfectly. Right now the public overwhelmingly supports the increased security. If I tried to remove those troops over Leyton's objections, I'll have a planetwide riot on my hands.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What if we bring you the proof? Hard evidence linking Leyton to the sabotage of the power grid?

title: Paradise Lost
line: With that, you could force Leyton to stand down, make him withdraw the troops. JARESH-

title: Paradise Lost
line: If what you say is true, I'll have his resignation. Bring me the evidence, I promise I'll use it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Sorry I'm late.

line: Where's Cadet Shepherd?

title: Paradise Lost
line: That's a good question. I couldn't find him anywhere.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What do you mean you couldn't find him?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I mean he's gone. And as far as I can tell so is every other member of Red Squad. The rumor is they've all been sent on some kind of training exercise.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'm afraid Cadet Shepherd won't be returning to Earth anytime soon.

line: Admiral Leyton, it's

line: Return to your quarters, Cadet.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Ben, I think you and I have to talk, in private.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'll be in the next room if you need me.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Mind if I get a cup of coffee?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Help yourself.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I haven't been getting a lot of sleep lately. Too much to do.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Maybe you need a vacation.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Mmm. Somehow replicated coffee never tastes this good. I'm afraid I owe you an apology, Ben.

title: Paradise Lost
line: The way I see it, you owe a lot of people an apology.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I wish I could have told you the truth from the beginning, but somehow I suspected we wouldn't see eye to eye on this thing.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Then why did you bring me here?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Because I needed someone who knew how to fight shape-shifters, and that's you. And I suppose on some level I hoped that when you saw what we were accomplishing, you'd join us. You've always had a strong sense of duty.

title: Paradise Lost
line: My duty is to protect the Federation.

title: Paradise Lost
line: That's what we're trying to do.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What you're trying to do is to seize control of Earth and place it under military rule.

title: Paradise Lost
line: If that's what it takes to stop the Dominion.

title: Paradise Lost
line: So you're willing to destroy paradise in order to save it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Remember when we were on the Okinawa fighting the Tzenkethi? That time when I wanted to take the ship into an asteroid belt to chase down those three raiders.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And I said it was an unnecessary risk.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You spoke your mind. Which is exactly what a good executive officer is supposed to do. But I overruled you. After the staff meeting you followed me into my ready room and tried to argue your point again.

title: Paradise Lost
line: That's right, I did.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And remember what I told you?

title: Paradise Lost
line: That a good officer must respect the chain of command. There comes a time when you must to accept the orders of a superior officer, and carry out those orders whether you agree with them or not.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I also told you when you became a CO, you'd feel the same way.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And you were right. About going after the Tzenkethi, and about me.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Without the chain of command, Starfleet would cease to function and we wouldn't stand a chance against our enemies. I'm still your commanding officer, and now more than ever I need you to respect my authority.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And I cannot do that! Not this time.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Then as of now, I'm relieving you of your post as temporary head of Earth Security and sending you back to Deep Space Nine. Go home, Ben. You don't belong here.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Beautiful evening, isn't it?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Chief, how'd you get here?

title: Paradise Lost
line: You don't look so good. You've got a lot on your mind, I bet. How is your father?

title: Paradise Lost
line: There's no way the Defiant could get here so soon.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I didn't say I came on the Defiant. Tell me the truth. Do you really believe that phaser rifles will do any good against shape-shifters?

title: Paradise Lost
line: You're not O'Brien.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Luckily, no. The thought of being locked in the one shape all the time. It's unnatural. Don't bother calling for help. It'll only cut short our conversation, and I do enjoy your company.

title: Paradise Lost
line: If you have something to say to me, say it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You solids. You are so impatient. I thought we could sit here for a while, maybe go to a bar, have a pint, throw some darts.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I don't think so.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Let me ask you a question. How many changelings do you think are here on Earth right at this moment?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I'm not going to play any guessing games with you.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Ah. What if I were to tell you that there are only four on this entire planet. Not counting Constable Odo of course. Think of it. Just four of us, and look at the havoc we've wrought.

title: Paradise Lost
line: How do I know you're telling me the truth?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Four is more than enough. We're smarter than solids. We're better than you. And most importantly, we do not fear you the way you fear us. In the end, it's your fear that will destroy you.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Are you finished?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Finished? We've barely begun. I'll be seeing you.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I recognize that look.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What look?

title: Paradise Lost
line: The one you're wearing. The one that says, something's bothering me and I don't know what to do about it.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Oh, that look.

title: Paradise Lost
line: You want to tell me about it?

title: Paradise Lost
line: I wish I could.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Oh, I see. It's a Neffie Beumont kind of thing.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Neffie Beumont? What a crush I had on her.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Not that you'd admit it. You just sat around for weeks, brooding and pining away, trying to sort it all out, until your old man finally sat you down one day and gave you some advice.

title: Paradise Lost
line: There comes a time in every man's life when he must stop thinking and start doing.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And the next day, you finally went over to young Neffie's house and asked her out.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And she turned me down.

title: Paradise Lost
line: But at least you weren't brooding anymore. And when Zoey Phillips moved into the neighborhood a few weeks later, you asked her out before her parents were done beaming in the furniture.

title: Paradise Lost
line: And dated her for three years. I guess what you're telling me is that I must stop brooding and make a decision.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Exactly.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Thank you, Dad.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Don't mention it. Make sure you turn out the lights on your way out. I wonder what ever happened to Zoey Phillips?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Zoey Phillips.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Captain, why are you transmitting on a Bajoran frequency?

title: Paradise Lost
line: We have things we need to discuss that I don't want anyone else to hear. What's your status?

title: Paradise Lost
line: Everything here is fine. There's been no sign of Dominion activity.

title: Paradise Lost
line: What about the wormhole?

title: Paradise Lost
line: It's acting normally again. It stopped opening and closing at random not long after you left. If any Dominion ships did sneak through, they're not giving us any trouble.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Listen closely. There's something I need for you to do.

title: Paradise Lost
line: It's all yours. I suggest you hurry. I doubt it'll take them very long to discover that we're here.

title: Paradise Lost
line: I never knew it was so easy to break into classified Starfleet files.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Everything I know I learned from Quark.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Looks like Leyton's been a busy man. He's personally reassigned over four hundred officers in the past three weeks.

title: Paradise Lost
line: Do you recognize any of these names?

title: Paradise Lost
line: A lot of them. Daneeka, McWatt, Snowden, Orr, Moodus. All of them were officers on the Okinawa when I was Leyton's XO. As far as I can tell, every officer on this list served under Leyton at one time or another.

title: Paradise Lost
