title: Inquisition
line: No wonder I feel so tired. I suppose you find your subjects more malleable when they have been deprived of sleep.

title: Inquisition
line: Not a new technique, I admit, but an effective one nonetheless.

title: Inquisition
line: So, why don't you tell me who you are? Who you work for?

title: Inquisition
line: I would think it's obvious. The same people you work for. The Federation. Starfleet.

title: Inquisition
line: You don't expect me to believe you're with Internal Affairs, do you?

title: Inquisition
line: No, of course not. Internal Affairs is a competent department, but limited.

title: Inquisition
line: So which department are you with?

title: Inquisition
line: Let's just say I belong to another branch of Starfleet Intelligence. Our official designation is Section thirty one.

title: Inquisition
line: Never heard of it.

title: Inquisition
line: We keep a low profile. Works out better that way for all concerned.

title: Inquisition
line: And what does Section thirty one do, apart from kidnapping Starfleet officers?

title: Inquisition
line: We search out and identify potential dangers to the Federation.

title: Inquisition
line: And once identified?

title: Inquisition
line: We deal with them.

title: Inquisition
line: How?

title: Inquisition
line: Quietly.

title: Inquisition
line: So if I had been a Dominion agent, what would have happened to me?

title: Inquisition
line: We wouldn't be standing here having this conversation.

title: Inquisition
line: And Starfleet sanctions what you're doing?

title: Inquisition
line: We don't submit reports or ask for approval for specific operations, if that's what you mean. We're an autonomous department.

title: Inquisition
line: Authorized by whom?

title: Inquisition
line: Section thirty one was part of the original Starfleet charter.

title: Inquisition
line: But that was two hundred years ago. Are you telling me you've been working on your own ever since? Without specific orders? Accountable to nobody but yourselves?

title: Inquisition
line: You make it sound so ominous.

title: Inquisition
line: Isn't it? Because if what you say to me is true, you function as judge, jury and executioner, and I think that's too much power for anyone.

title: Inquisition
line: I admit it takes exceptional people to do what we do. People who can sublimate their own ambitions to the best interests of the Federation. People like you.

title: Inquisition
line: Me?

title: Inquisition
line: You have all the qualifications to be a very useful member of Section thirty one.

title: Inquisition
line: A few minutes ago, you were calling me a traitor and now you want to recruit me?

title: Inquisition
line: Well, you're intelligent, you're resourceful, you've always been fascinated by covert operations. Why else would you spend so much time in Quark's holosuites playing spy?

title: Inquisition
line: You're serious.

title: Inquisition
line: We're on the same team. We believe in the same principles that every other Federation citizen holds dear.

title: Inquisition
line: Yet you violate those principles as a matter of course.

title: Inquisition
line: In order to protect them.

title: Inquisition
line: No, I'm sorry, but the ends don't always justify the means.

title: Inquisition
line: Really. How many lives do you suppose you've saved in your medical career?

title: Inquisition
line: What has that got to do with anything?

title: Inquisition
line: Hundreds? Thousands? Do you suppose that those people give a damn that you lied to get into Starfleet Medical? I doubt it. We deal with threats to the Federation that jeopardize its very survival. If you knew how many lives we've saved, I think you'd agree that the ends do justify the means. I'm not afraid of bending the rules every once in a while if the situation warrants it, and I don't think you are either.

title: Inquisition
line: You've got the wrong man, Sloan.

title: Inquisition
line: I don't think so. In time, you'll come to agree with me.

title: Inquisition
line: Don't hold your breath.

title: Inquisition
line: All I ask is that when you get back to Deep Space Nine, you consider what I've said.

title: Inquisition
line: What if I decide to expose you?

title: Inquisition
line: Let's just say I'm not going to lose any sleep over it.

title: Inquisition
line: I'll say one thing for this fellow Sloan, he's clever. He timed the Doctor's abduction to coincide with his trip to the medical conference. That way, he wasn't missed.

title: Inquisition
line: Yes, he's clever.

title: Inquisition
line: We went over Julian's quarters but we couldn't find any residual transporter signatures. So either they got him off the station some other way, or they have transporter technology that we can't detect.

title: Inquisition
line: Captain, is there any word from Starfleet about Sloan or Section thirty one?

title: Inquisition
line: There's no record of a Deputy Director Sloan anywhere in Starfleet. And as for Section thirty one, that's a little more complicated. Starfleet Command doesn't acknowledge its existence, but they don't deny it either. They simply said they'd look into it and get back to me.

title: Inquisition
line: When?

title: Inquisition
line: They didn't say.

title: Inquisition
line: That sounds like a cover up to me.

title: Inquisition
line: I can't believe the Federation condones this kind of activity.

title: Inquisition
line: Personally, I find it hard to believe they wouldn't. Every other great power has a unit like Section thirty one. The Romulans have the Tal Shiar, the Cardassians had the Obsidian Order.

title: Inquisition
line: But what does that say about us? When push comes to shove, are we willing to sacrifice our principles in order to survive?

title: Inquisition
line: I wish I had an answer for you, Doctor.

title: Inquisition
line: Maybe we should do some checking, try to track down this Sloan ourselves.

title: Inquisition
line: That won't be easy. If he's right and Section thirty one has existed since the birth of the Federation, they've learned to cover their tracks very well.

title: Inquisition
line: We don't have to find them. They'll come to us. You said that Sloan tried to recruit you.

title: Inquisition
line: I turned him down.

title: Inquisition
line: He doesn't strike me as a man who takes no for an answer. And next time he asks you to join his little group, you will say yes.

title: Inquisition
line: Well, congratulations, Doctor. Looks like you're going to get to play a spy after all. Only this time, for real.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Captain's personal log, stardate five one seven, er, five one seven four? Computer, what day is it?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Stardate 51721.3.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: It's only been two weeks. I need to talk about this. I have to justify what's happened, what I've done, at least to myself. I can't talk to anyone else. Not even to Dax. Maybe if I just lay it all out in my log, it'll finally make sense. I can see where it all went wrong. Where I went wrong. I suppose it started two weeks ago,

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: While I was posting the weekly casualty list in the wardroom. Every Friday morning for the past three months, I've posted the official list of Starfleet personnel killed, wounded or missing in the war.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: It's become something of a grim ritual around here. Not a week goes by that someone doesn't find the name of a loved one, a friend or an acquaintance on that damned list.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I've grown to hate Fridays.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Who is it, Dax?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Leslie Wong.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: The skipper of the Cairo?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: She was an instructor at the Academy when I was a sophomore.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Do you know what happened to the Cairo?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Just that she disappeared on patrol in the Romulan neutral zone. I'll look into it.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Don't bother. I'm sure it's the same old story. The Jem'Hadar crossed the Romulan border and caught them by surprise. It's only about the hundredth time it's happened.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I can't believe the Romulans allow them to violate their territory so brazenly. Why do they get away with it?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: The Romulans have a treaty of non-aggression and friendship with the Dominion, so they're willing to turn a blind eye to almost anything in the name of friendship.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: What we need is to bring the Romulans into the war on our side. With the combined forces of the Federation, the Klingons and the Romulans we could finally go on the offensive.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: That's the last thing the Romulans want. Think about it. They're in the perfect position. They get to sit back and watch as their biggest rivals slug it out in a long, bloody war. No one's threatening their interests. Why should they risk their necks? There's simply no reason for them to get involved in our war. No reason at all.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: That was the moment I made the decision. It was like I had stepped through a door and locked it behind me. I was going to bring the Romulans into the war.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: It's in their own best interest to join the war, that's the key. That's the reason the Romulans will finally take action. Not to do us any favors, but to protect themselves from the Dominion.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Okay. Let's say I'm the Romulan Proconsul. From where I'm sitting, the Dominion isn't a threat to me. I have a non-aggression pact with them. They're my allies.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You're not going to put your faith in some piece of paper, are you?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Not at all. I've been watching them very closely since the beginning of the war, and so far, they've kept their part of the bargain.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: They're violating your territory almost every day. What kind of an ally is that?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: So they're crossing my backyard to give the Federation a bloody nose. I can't say that makes me very sad.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You can't be naive enough to think that the Dominion is going to stop with the Federation. When they're finished with us, they're be coming after you.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: That's speculation.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: The Founders see it as their sacred duty to bring order to the galaxy. Their order. Do you think they'll sit idly by while you keep your chaotic empire right next to their perfect order? No. If you watch us go under, then what you're really doing is signing your own death warrant.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: But before I plunge my people into a conflict that will kill millions of loyal Romulan citizens, I need something more concrete than the self-serving argument of a Starfleet officer. I need proof of Dominion duplicity. Not more words, proof.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Very good, old man. You would have made a decent Romulan.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I prefer the spots to the pointed ears.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Okay, you've convinced me. They're going to need evidence. But if there is evidence of a Dominion plan to attack Romulus, it's probably buried deep in the bowels of their headquarters on Cardassia Prime.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Not exactly the most accessible place in the galaxy.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Not for us, maybe. But there is someone on this station who specializes in gaining access to places where he is not welcome.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I must say I'm flattered, Captain. I had no idea you held such a lofty opinion of me. Your faith in my ability to retrieve classified information from my former homeland is most gratifying.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Mister Garak, let's dispense with the usual repartee and concentrate on the issue at hand. Can you do it or not?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: No one wants to see the Dominion destroyed more than I do, but to go to Cardassia Prime, penetrate one of the most heavily guarded facilities in the quadrant, steal top secret war plans and then return them safely to you is not just another job. It's more like a suicide mission. And that is well outside my field of expertise.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I didn't say you had to go there yourself. I have to believe that a man like you still has a few contacts at home. A colleague from the Obsidian Order, an old friend, a reliable informant. Someone who might owe you a favor.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Perhaps.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Then I'd say it's time to call in a favor.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: It would mean calling in all my favors, Captain. To do what you're asking would use up every resource I have left on Cardassia. And it may be a very messy, very bloody business. Are you prepared for that?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I posted my fourteenth casualty list this morning. I'm already involved in a very messy, very bloody business. And the only way I can see to end it is to bring the Romulans into the war. I am prepared to do whatever it takes to accomplish that goal, but I can't do it alone. I need help. Now, are you in or out?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'm in.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: My father used to say that the road to hell is paved with good intentions.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I laid the first stone right there. I'd committed myself. I'd pay any price, go to any lengths, because my cause was righteous. My intentions were good. In the beginning, that seemed like enough.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: If there's one thing I've learned over the years, it's that bad news invariably comes in the middle of the night.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Kira to Captain Sisko.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Go ahead, Major.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: We just received a priority one communication from Starfleet Command. The Dominion has invaded Betazed.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: According to initial reports, the invasion force must have come from somewhere in the Calandra Sector.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Did Starfleet Intelligence know anything about the buildup?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: No. They believed Calandra was too far from the Dominion supply lines to be a threat.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: There's plenty of blame to go around. The Tenth Fleet was supposed to be protecting Betazed and its outlying colonies, but it was caught out of position on a training exercise. What's worse, Betazed's own defense systems are obsolete and undermanned. The planet was theirs in less than ten hours.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: With Betazed in the hands of the Jem'Hadar, the Dominion is in a position to threaten Vulcan, Andor, Tellar, Alpha Centauri.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: If we ever needed a new ally, it's right now.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Mister Garak, it's been three days. Have you made any progress?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Well I suppose that depends on how you look at it.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: This is how I look at it is. Betazed has just fallen to the Dominion and we need to get this operation underway.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I share your desire for swift action, Captain. In fact, after our last conversation, I made a few discreet inquiries among my former associates still living on Cardassia. As I anticipated, they shared my loathing for the current government and were willing to take on an assignment aimed at its destruction.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: That sounds like progress to me.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Doesn't it? Unfortunately, they're all dead now.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: What?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Yes. All killed within one day of speaking with me. I suppose that's a testament to the effectiveness of Dominion security. One should admire such efficiency.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'm sorry.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I hope you're not giving up that easily. After all, the stakes are much higher than a few dead operatives. The fate of the entire quadrant hangs in the balance. Or at least that's the case you made to me.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Do you have another plan?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: As a matter of fact, I do. But I suspect you won't like it.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Try me.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: If you want to guarantee that we obtain evidence of a Dominion plan to attack the Romulans, I suggest that we manufacture that evidence ourselves.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Maybe I should have put a stop to it right there. Maybe I should have said, thank you very much for your input, Mister Garak. I will take your suggestion under advisement, and gone back to my office and forgotten about the whole thing. But I didn't. Because in my heart, I knew what he was saying made sense.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: His name is Vreenak. He's been a key member of the Romulan Senate for the past fourteen years. He's Secretary of the War Plans Council, Vice Chairman of the Tal Shiar, and one of the most trusted advisors to Proconsul Neral.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: He's also the man that negotiated the non-aggression pact with the Dominion.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Since you're familiar with him, I'll skip the rest of his biography. What's important is that he continues to be one of the most ardently pro-Dominion voices in the Senate. If we can convince him that the Dominion is a threat, the rest of the Senate will follow.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: All right, how?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Ten days from now, Senator Vreenak will be making a trip to Soukara for a diplomatic meeting with Weyoun. I am certain that he can be persuaded to make a secret detour to DS Nine if he were invited by one Captain Benjamin Sisko.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: How do you know he'll be visiting Soukara?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: There are some things I'd rather not discuss. May I continue?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Please.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: When Senator Vreenak arrives, you will show him a holographic recording of a secret meeting held at the highest level of the Dominion in which the planned invasion of Romulus is being discussed. You will tell the Senator that this information was obtained through various covert means at great cost to the Federation. At least ten good men lost their lives bringing it across the line, that sort of thing. He will immediately suspect it's a forgery, but you will assure him that such a thing would be impossible. You see, Senator, this is an official Cardassian transcript. It was recorded on a one time optolythic data rod used for official record keeping. These rods are manufactured only as needed on Cardassia Prime. Information can only be transcribed on them once, and then cannot be altered.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: He'll want to examine it.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Of course. And he will discover to his amazement that it's completely genuine. At least, so it will appear.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: But in reality?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You will have handed him a genuine optolythic data rod, but it will contain one of the most perfect forgeries ever fashioned. I'm still working on obtaining the data rod, but I have located the man who will create the holorecording.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You realize I can't authorize a thing like this on my own. I'll have to clear it with Starfleet Command.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Of course. But I suspect that with the fall of Betazed, they'll be ready to do whatever it takes to bring the Romulans into the war.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'll let you know.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: One last thing, Captain. The man we need to forge this holoprogram is currently sitting in a Klingon prison awaiting execution. To save time and incidentally his life, I thought that perhaps you could contact Chancellor Gowron today and arrange a pardon.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: What's his name?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Grathon Tolar.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I cannot tell you how grateful I am, Captain. The Klingons were going to execute me tomorrow. Of course, they say that every day. It's one of the little games they like to play.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You do understand the terms of your parole?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Oh, yes. I have to promise to stay away from the Klingon Empire. That'll be tough. And I have to create some kind of a special holoprogram for you. I can hardy wait. I've never worked for Starfleet before.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Let's be very clear about this. You're not working for Starfleet. This entire matter is off the record. As far as you're concerned, you're working for me.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Oh. A personal matter. Something special for your eyes only. Something with, perhaps, five or six Orion slave girls and

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Mister Tolar, I suggest you go wait in your quarters. Mister Garak will provide you with all the information you need.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Garak is here?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: That's right.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Oh. Oh. Well, that's different. I'll wait in my quarters.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Why I didn't listen to the voice in the back of my mind telling me not to believe a word he said, I'll never know.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: But it didn't take long for me to come face to face with the fact that I'd made a mistake.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Odo to the Captain.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Go ahead, Constable.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'm sorry to disturb you, but do you know a man named Grathon Tolar?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Yes. Why do you ask?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Because he just tried to kill Quark.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Sit still, Quark. You'll be fine.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: All right, keep an eye on him.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: What happened?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: As I understand it, Mister Tolar over there came in about two hours ago and ordered a bottle of Whelan Bitters. Fifteen minutes later, he ordered a second bottle, then a third. Halfway through his fourth bottle he decided to dance with M'Pella. She was otherwise engaged running the dabo wheel and declined his invitation. He decided to force the issue. A brief struggle ensued and Quark, in an uncharacteristic display of chivalry, attempted to intervene, so Tolar stabbed him. Normally, he'd be sitting in a holding cell, but he claims he's a friend of yours.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: He's no friend of mine, but he is working for me. It's an extremely sensitive matter concerning Federation security. I can't have any record of him being on the station.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I see. I am certainly aware of the need for special security measures during wartime, but as a matter of law, if Quark chooses to press charges against Tolar, I have no choice but to make an arrest.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: May I speak to Quark.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: How is he?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: How do I look? I'm a man who just had a brush with death.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: He'll be fine. His ribs deflected the knife from his major organs. The bleeding was superficial.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Superficial? Do you know how much this shirt cost?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Will you excuse us for a moment, Doctor?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'll check on you tomorrow.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Do you intend to press charges?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You bet I do.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: What will it take, er, to, er, convince you otherwise?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Are you offering me a bribe? I knew it. Captain, I've always liked you. I suspected that somewhere deep down in your heart of hearts there was a tiny bit of Ferengi just waiting to get out.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: What's your price?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Well, let's start with replacing my clothes and M'Pella's clothes.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: All right.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'm not finished. I think I should be compensated for the loss of business I suffered today, which I calculate as no less than five bars of gold pressed latinum.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Done.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'm also having a problem with station security. They're holding some cargo containers which I've been waiting for because of some missing import license or something.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'll handle it. Anything else?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: No. I think we can call it a bribe. And thank you, Captain. Thank you for restoring my faith in the ninety eighth Rule of Acquisition. Every man has his price.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: That was my first moment of real doubt, when I started to wonder if this whole thing was a mistake. So then I went back to my office and there was a new casualty list waiting for me. People are dying out there every day. Entire worlds are struggling for their freedom and here I am still worrying about the finer points of morality. No, I had to keep my eye on the ball. Win the war, stop the bloodshed. Those were the priorities!

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: So I pushed on. And every time another doubt appeared before me, I just found another way to shove it aside.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Mind if I join you?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Be my guest.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Ops.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Hold. The less I'm seen parading through Ops, the better.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I couldn't agree more.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You seem angry.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Who's watching Tolar?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I've locked him in his quarters. I've also left him with the distinct impression that if he attempts to force the door open, it may explode.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I hope that's just an impression.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: It's best not to dwell on such minutiae. In any case, we have far more important matters to discuss. I've located a gentleman willing to sell us a genuine optolythic data rod.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: How do you know it's genuine?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I trust the source, but rest assured I will confirm the rod's authenticity before I make payment. Which brings me to you.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: How much does he want?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I'm afraid he's not interested in latinum. The gentleman in question has requested to be compensated with two hundred liters of biomimetic gel.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: What?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I don't know why, exactly. One would assume it has something to do with genetic experimentation.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Offer him something else.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Believe me, I wouldn't be relaying this request if I thought he'd take anything else.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Biomimetic gel is strictly controlled by the Federation and not for sale at any price. Find someone else who's willing sell us a rod.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I wasn't exaggerating when I told you about the near impossibility of obtaining a genuine Cardassian data rod. It's something of a minor miracle that I was able to locate this one source, I'm virtually certain I won't find another. I'm afraid we either give him what he wants or forget the whole enterprise.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Then let's forget about it. Ops. Hold. Two hundred liters is out of the question. There's not that much gel in the entire sector.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I believe the quantity is open to negotiation.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Ops.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Captain, biomimetic gel is an extremely dangerous compound, as you know. I can't release it without at least some idea of where it's going. In the wrong hands, it could be used to make biogenic weapons, or for illegal replication experiments, or to develop organic explosives

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Perhaps I didn't make myself clear, Doctor. This is not a request, it's an order. You will package eighty five liters of biomimetic gel for interstellar transport and deliver them to cargo bay three. Is that understood?

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Yes. I'd like this order in writing, please, sir.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: I thought you might.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: You should know that I shall note this in my log and file an official protest with Starfleet Medical.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: That is your right. But I want the gel by the end of the day. Dismissed.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: The Founders have decided to implement stage two ahead of schedule.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: The invasion of Romulus? It's too soon. We're engaged in heavy fighting all along the border with the Federation. The Klingons are preparing to go on the offensive and

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Fortunately, the Founders have better vision than you do. They can see the opportunities before us even when you cannot. Consider. The Romulans don't expect an attack from Cardassia. The bulk of the Romulan fleet is still deployed along the Neutral Zone with the Federation. The Founders estimate that we could be on Romulus itself in less than three weeks.

title: In The Pale Moonlight
line: Three weeks? I heard the same kind of estimates before we attacked the Federation.
