title: Chimera
line: The truth is, I prefer the so-called primitive lifeforms. They exist as they were meant to, by following their instincts. No words get in the way, no lies, no deceptions.

title: Chimera
line: We're not the ones who can disguise ourselves as anything we want.

title: Chimera
line: Meaning?

title: Chimera
line: Meaning shape-shifters are not to be trusted.

title: Chimera
line: I trust Odo.

title: Chimera
line: Of course you trust Odo. Look at him. You've convinced him that he is as limited as you are.

title: Chimera
line: Laas.

title: Chimera
line: You've seen through our evil plan.

title: Chimera
line: Foiled again.

title: Chimera
line: It's not funny.

title: Chimera
line: No, I'm very worried for him.

title: Chimera
line: Odo can take care of himself.

title: Chimera
line: Thank you, Colonel. Well, this has been interesting. If you'll excuse us, Colonel, Counselor, Doctor, Chief. Laas.

title: Chimera
line: Nice to see you again.

title: Chimera
line: This way.

title: Chimera
line: Was it really necessary to insult my friends?

title: Chimera
line: I was merely speaking my mind.

title: Chimera
line: You could call it that.

title: Chimera
line: Humanoids are such tragic creatures. They've lost the ability to take joy from simply existing, and yet they haven't evolved to the next level where consciousness exists independent of form.

title: Chimera
line: You're certainly not afraid to make grand generalizations.

title: Chimera
line: I've been many things in my time, Odo. I speak from experience. Enough talk. Link with me.

title: Chimera
line: Here?

title: Chimera
line: Why not?

title: Chimera
line: I don't think that's a good idea.

title: Chimera
line: Are you embarrassed?

title: Chimera
line: No.

title: Chimera
line: You don't want to do anything to remind them that you're not truly a humanoid.

title: Chimera
line: I don't go out of my way to point it out, no.

title: Chimera
line: Why not? Are you afraid they will reject you?

title: Chimera
line: I don't like to confront people with something that might make them uncomfortable.

title: Chimera
line: So you deny your true nature in order to fit in.

title: Chimera
line: You're reading too much into it.

title: Chimera
line: Before I came here, when was the last time you assumed another form? You can't even remember. You've been pretending to be a humanoid for so long, it doesn't even occur to you that you can be anything else.

title: Chimera
line: That's not true. I've been involved with other things lately.

title: Chimera
line: Like what? Courting Kira? She can't even Link with you.

title: Chimera
line: Leave her out of this.

title: Chimera
line: It won't last.

title: Chimera
line: The fact that your relationship failed doesn't mean that mine will.

title: Chimera
line: True. And if you're very lucky, you can watch her grow old and die.

title: Chimera
line: I think you should stay out of my affairs.

title: Chimera
line: I don't want to see you make the same mistakes I made. You're wasting your time trying to be a humanoid. You're limiting yourself. Let's leave here, Odo. Let's find the others. A hundred were sent away and they're out there somewhere. If we can find even a few of them, we can form a new Link. Think of it, Odo. We can exist the way we were meant to. As changelings.

title: Chimera
line: I can't believe he actually thought you'd just drop everything and leave with him.

title: Chimera
line: He just can't understand why I want to stay here.

title: Chimera
line: How did he take it when you said no? You did say no, didn't you?

title: Chimera
line: I told him I'd think about it. I didn't want to dismiss it out of hand. He would have taken offense. Why do you look at me like that?

title: Chimera
line: It just bothers me that he thinks you're not happy here. It makes me think he knows something that I don't.

title: Chimera
line: What makes you say that?

title: Chimera
line: He Linked with you. Something about that gave him the impression that you might want to leave here.

title: Chimera
line: It's just wishful thinking on his part. The thought of the two of us going off together looking for the others, exploring the galaxy as changelings, it's very alluring. To him.

title: Chimera
line: Sounds like it's alluring to you, too.

title: Chimera
line: I'm happy here.

title: Chimera
line: I'm sorry I can't Link with you.

title: Chimera
line: It doesn't matter, Nerys. I love you.

title: Chimera
line: Computer, activate fire suppression sys Laas? I need to talk to you.

title: Chimera
line: You didn't realize it was me. Did you even know we could exist as fire? I didn't think so. No matter. Once we're away from here, I'll teach you to become things you've never even dreamed of.

title: Chimera
line: I'm not leaving. I'm staying here.

title: Chimera
line: Why? So you can keep pretending to be one of them?

title: Chimera
line: I'm sorry if you're disappointed.

title: Chimera
line: I'll survive. And when I find some of the others, I'll send for you. You'll change your mind. You'll join us.

title: Chimera
line: It could take a long time for you find another changeling.

title: Chimera
line: Is that supposed to discourage me?

title: Chimera
line: All I'm saying is you don't have to leave right away. I wouldn't mind the company of another changeling. I'm sure you wouldn't mind either.

title: Chimera
line: All right, Odo, I won't abandon you to these monoforms. As a favor to you, I'll stay a while.

title: Chimera
line: You might as well. If you can't get along with me, what makes you think you can get along with any other changeling?

title: Chimera
line: Just remember, I have no interest in monoforms, even if they are your friends.

title: Chimera
line: After what happened at Quark's, I don't think you have to worry about an overcrowded social schedule.

title: Chimera
line: Good.

title: Chimera
line: Great. The environmental system's out again.

title: Chimera
line: There goes our holosuite reservation.

title: Chimera
line: I'd better go see what the problem is.

title: Chimera
line: Don't bother, Chief. There's nothing wrong with the environmental system.

title: Chimera
line: Where's this fog coming from?

title: Chimera
line: It's not fog, it's Laas.

title: Chimera
line: Laas?

title: Chimera
line: What's he doing?

title: Chimera
line: Being fog, what's it look like?

title: Chimera
line: Can't he be fog somewhere else?

title: Chimera
line: Or at night, when no one's around?

title: Chimera
line: He's not hurting anyone.

title: Chimera
line: Still. It's creepy.

title: Chimera
line: Careful, Miles. He might hear you.

title: Chimera
line: Good.

title: Chimera
line: Laas. Laas.

title: Chimera
line: Congratulations. You managed to disrupt the entire Promenade.

title: Chimera
line: I was just relaxing.

title: Chimera
line: If you want to relax, do it in private.

title: Chimera
line: Did I embarrass you?

title: Chimera
line: Ka'vek! What is this Founder doing here?

title: Chimera
line: He's not a Founder. Now move along.

title: Chimera
line: Don't change form in my presence again.

title: Chimera
line: I change form where I please. Look at him. Look at the hate in his eyes.

title: Chimera
line: Laas.

title: Chimera
line: Your hands are stained with the blood of Klingon warriors.

title: Chimera
line: But then, the stench would still be on them.

title: Chimera
line: P'tak!

title: Chimera
line: Mine's bigger.

title: Chimera
line: Ke'chaw!

title: Chimera
line: No!

title: Chimera
line: Doctor Bashir wasn't able to save the Klingon's life. General Martok has asked that Laas be detained until the Magistrate can determine jurisdiction.

title: Chimera
line: Jurisdiction?

title: Chimera
line: The Klingons want to extradite him.

title: Chimera
line: That's ridiculous. He killed that Klingon in self-defense.

title: Chimera
line: That is in dispute.

title: Chimera
line: He was about to draw his disruptor.

title: Chimera
line: According to the other Klingon, he was reaching for his dagger.

title: Chimera
line: Are you saying that's not true?

title: Chimera
line: It all happened too fast. But their intentions were obvious. One of them put a knife in his chest.

title: Chimera
line: The Klingons are arguing that since Laas knew he couldn't be harmed by a knife, that he wasn't justified in responding with deadly force.

title: Chimera
line: Since when do Klingons resort to legal quibbling? They get involved in fights all the time. They never file charges. It isn't honorable.

title: Chimera
line: In this case, the Klingons are exercising their rights under the law.

title: Chimera
line: Sir, they are only doing this because they distrust changelings.

title: Chimera
line: He should not have provoked them.

title: Chimera
line: Provoked them? They attacked Laas.

title: Chimera
line: They claim that he surrounded them menacingly.

title: Chimera
line: They felt menaced by fog?

title: Chimera
line: They weren't the only ones. There are twelve other people who filed complaints.

title: Chimera
line: Is it a crime to shape-shift on the Promenade?

title: Chimera
line: It's not a crime, but obviously it's not a good idea.

title: Chimera
line: You're going to allow the Klingons extradite him knowing they won't give him a fair trial.

title: Chimera
line: That's not my decision. It's up to the Magistrate.

title: Chimera
line: But you'd just as soon be rid of him. You never wanted him on the station in the first place. I practically had to beg you to let him out of that holding cell.

title: Chimera
line: That's quite enough, Constable. Now, Martok has expressed concerns about our security arrangements.

title: Chimera
line: Meaning?

title: Chimera
line: He's not sure it's appropriate that you should be in charge of the prisoner.

title: Chimera
line: May I ask why?

title: Chimera
line: Because you were a witness to the alleged crime.

title: Chimera
line: That's a relief. For a moment I thought you were going to say it's because I'm a changeling.

title: Chimera
line: Odo. I heard about your friend. Rumor has it the Klingons want to put him on trial.

title: Chimera
line: They're the ones who should be put on trial. If they'd attacked anyone other than a changeling, they would be.

title: Chimera
line: You're probably right. That fog episode certainly didn't help matters.

title: Chimera
line: Laas was only doing what comes naturally to us.

title: Chimera
line: You never pulled a stunt like that. You're smart enough to know that people don't want to be reminded that you're different. Who wants to see somebody turn into goo? I hope you don't do that around Kira.

title: Chimera
line: Why shouldn't I?

title: Chimera
line: If she's anything like me, she'd rather you didn't. Don't you get it, Odo? We humanoids are a product of millions of years of evolution. Our ancestors learned the hard way that what you don't know might kill you. They wouldn't have survived if they hadn't have jumped back when they encountered a snake coiled in the muck. And now millions of years later, that instinct is still there. It's genetic. Our tolerance to other lifeforms doesn't extend beyond the two arm, two leg variety. I hate to break this to you, but when you're in your natural state, you're more than our poor old genes can handle.

title: Chimera
line: So what are you saying, Quark? That the Klingons couldn't help what they did because of their genes?

title: Chimera
line: I'm not trying to excuse what they did. I'm only telling you why it happened. Watch your step, Odo. We're at war with your people. This is no time for a changeling pride demonstration on the Promenade.

title: Chimera
line: Constable.

title: Chimera
line: I'd like to have a few minutes alone with the prisoner.

title: Chimera
line: Sorry, sir. I have my orders.

title: Chimera
line: I don't know what to say.

title: Chimera
line: You could say you were wrong. You could say the people here are no different than any other humanoids.

title: Chimera
line: Hopefully this will all get straightened out at your hearing.

title: Chimera
line: I am sure it will be fair and impartial.

title: Chimera
line: Just tell them exactly what happened.

title: Chimera
line: My word against a humanoid's? Whom do you think this Magistrate is going to believe?

title: Chimera
line: I shouldn't have convinced you to stay. If I had just let you go, none of this would have happened.

title: Chimera
line: My only consolation is that this may finally make you understand that you don't belong here. You saw the hatred in that Klingon's eyes. Perhaps now you'll recognize it when you see it hiding in the faces of your so-called friends. They tolerate you, Odo, because you emulate them. What higher flattery is there? I, who can be anything, choose to be like you. But even when you make yourself in their image, they know you are not truly one of them. They know that what you appear to be does not reflect what you really are. It's only a mask. What lies underneath is alien to them, and so they fear it. And that fear can turn to hate in the blink of an eye.

title: Chimera
line: They're going to extradite him.

title: Chimera
line: You don't know that.

title: Chimera
line: Yes, I do. And no one is going to do anything to stop it.

title: Chimera
line: There's not much anyone can do.

title: Chimera
line: If he weren't a changeling, the Captain would find a way to intervene.

title: Chimera
line: Odo, that's unfair.

title: Chimera
line: Is it?

title: Chimera
line: You're starting to sound like Laas.

title: Chimera
line: Maybe that's because I'm starting to see things more clearly now.

title: Chimera
line: What is that supposed to mean?

title: Chimera
line: Look at me, Nerys. What do you see?

title: Chimera
line: I see you.

title: Chimera
line: No. No, this is just a form I've borrowed. I could just as easily be someone else or something else.

title: Chimera
line: I know that. But this is what you have always chosen to be. A man. A good and honest man. A man I fell in love with. Are you trying to tell me that he never really existed?

title: Chimera
line: I don't know. I care about you more than anyone I've ever known. These last few months have been the happiest of my life. But even so, part of me wishes that Laas and I were out there right now searching for the others, existing as changelings. Because that's what I am. Not a humanoid. I'm a changeling.

title: Chimera
line: Well then maybe you're right. Maybe you do belong out there.

title: Chimera
line: Can I help you, Colonel?

title: Chimera
line: I need to talk to the prisoner. Alone.

title: Chimera
line: Aye, sir.

title: Chimera
line: Go to the third planet in the Koralis system. You'll find an orbital tether running down to an abandoned mining complex. I'll tell Odo to meet you there.

title: Chimera
line: Is this some kind of a trick?

title: Chimera
line: Do you want to get out of here or not?

title: Chimera
line: That vent will lead you through some conduits to an airlock.

title: Chimera
line: Why?

title: Chimera
line: I love him.

title: Chimera
line: Escaped? How did he get through the containment field?

title: Chimera
line: I can't explain it. All I can tell you is what I saw. He turned himself into some kind of plasma energy and forced his way through. Before I could stop him, he had disappeared into the air vent.

title: Chimera
line: According to the operations log, one of the airlocks was activated shortly after that.

title: Chimera
line: If he left the station, why didn't our sensors detect him?

title: Chimera
line: A Corvallen freighter was leaving at about the same time. He must have shadowed it to keep from being spotted.

title: Chimera
line: He could be anywhere by now.

title: Chimera
line: General Martok is not going to be happy about this

title: Chimera
line: By fleeing, the changeling has demonstrated his guilt.

title: Chimera
line: Either that, or his lack of faith in our justice system.

title: Chimera
line: He must be apprehended and brought to trial.

title: Chimera
line: Mister Worf, have all available runabouts begin a sector wide search.

title: Chimera
line: Aye, sir.

title: Chimera
line: Good luck

title: Chimera
line: Constable, I know it's a long shot, but I'm sure you can agree we should do everything we can to find him.

title: Chimera
line: Of course.

title: Chimera
line: Dismissed.

title: Chimera
line: Level Nine.

title: Chimera
line: You didn't hide it very well. That you're glad he escaped.

title: Chimera
line: I should have known he'd be able to escape. What's a forcefield to a changeling with his abilities?

title: Chimera
line: You said you wished you were out there with him. Well, it's not too late.

title: Chimera
line: I don't understand.

title: Chimera
line: He's waiting for you at an abandoned mine on Koralis Three.

title: Chimera
line: You helped him escape.

title: Chimera
line: I don't want you to stay here out of some sense of obligation. Good luck. I hope you find what you're looking for.

title: Chimera
line: Laas?

title: Chimera
line: I knew you would come. This is a new beginning for us, Odo. A new beginning for our people. You and I are about to embark on the adventure of our lives. What's wrong?

title: Chimera
line: I'm not going with you.

title: Chimera
line: Why are you here?

title: Chimera
line: I've came to say goodbye.

title: Chimera
line: Don't be a fool. What are you holding on to? Kira? Even she knows that this is what's best for you. Why else would she have helped me to escape?

title: Chimera
line: You really don't know, do you? You don't have any idea what it means to love someone enough to let them go.

title: Chimera
line: She let you go so that you could find out where you belong.

title: Chimera
line: I know where I belong. Laas, humanoids are not the petty, limited creatures you perceive them to be. What Nerys did should prove that even to you.

title: Chimera
line: Love conquers all, is that it?

title: Chimera
line: I'm sorry you can't understand. You've done many things, been many things, but you've never known love.

title: Chimera
line: Compared to the Link, it is a pale shadow, a feeble attempt to compensate for the isolation that monoforms feel because they are trapped within themselves.

title: Chimera
line: Maybe the fact that it's not easy is what makes it worthwhile.

title: Chimera
line: Odo, the Founders are dying. This could be your last chance to exist the way you were meant to. Don't throw it away.

title: Chimera
line: You'd better go. They're looking for you. Good luck.

title: Chimera
line: And to you, Odo. You'll need it more than I.

title: Chimera
line: Watch over him. Help him find his way.

title: Chimera
line: Yes.

title: Chimera
line: I didn't think I'd see you again.

title: Chimera
line: I couldn't go.

title: Chimera
line: If I ever made you feel that you can't be yourself with me, I'm sorry. I want to know you the way you really are.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: All right, next item. Item seven. warbird repair and maintenance. Senator?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Repairs on our ships have continually been delayed in favor of Klingon and Federation vessels. The Dividices and the Genorex have been waiting almost three weeks while more than a dozen Klingon ships have been given first priority.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I make up the repair schedule according to my assessment of which ships have the greatest need.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Odd that the Klingons seem to always have the greatest need.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: They are usually more damaged because Klingon warships are relentless in pressing home their attack.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Reckless would be another way of putting it.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: The fight must be taken to the enemy. We cannot win this war if

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: All right. We're not here to debate combat tactics. Chief, how soon can you have those warbirds into a docking bay?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well, I suppose I could bring them in tomorrow. That would mean delaying repairs to the Hornet and the Rotarran. Somebody's going to have to explain to General Martok why his flagship was bumped.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Worf, you just volunteered for that assignment.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: This brings up the question of shore leave. At the moment, we have the crews from two Klingon ships on the station. I'd rather not have that many Klingons and Romulans on the Promenade at the same time.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: We'll forgo shore leave until the Klingons depart. Our soldiers are professionals. They're here to fight, not to get drunk in Quark's.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: All right, that's it for today then. Same time next week? Oh sorry, Senator, you'll be attending that conference on Romulus, won't you?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Yes. But SubCommander Velal will be here in my place.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Fine. Have a safe trip.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Thank you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Ah, yes, Romulus. How well I remember it. You'll find the predominant color to be gray. The buildings, the clothes, the people. Did you know that the Romulan heart itself is gray? It's true. And altogether appropriate for such an unimaginative race.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I take it you didn't enjoy your brief stint on Romulus. You were posing as a gardener, weren't you?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It was one of the few instances where my cover was more enjoyable than the actual assignment.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What was the assignment, anyway?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm afraid I can't talk about that. Back to the subject at hand. What will your role be at this conference?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well, I'll be giving a talk on Dominion biogenic weapons, chairing a seminar on Ketracel white, and attending a meeting on a proposal to transfer twenty five Federation hospital ships over to Romulan control.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: How dull.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sorry to disappoint you. Admiral Ross and his staff will be discussing the exciting military issues.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I see. I trust that Starfleet Intelligence will be sending someone along to make good use of this opportunity.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What do you mean?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Isn't it obvious? This is a golden opportunity to gather intelligence on Romulan intentions and military capabilities.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: They're our allies, Garak. And with any luck, this could be the beginning of a entirely new friendship between our peoples.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: The eternal optimist.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Guilty as charged.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: How sad. I must tell you I'm disappointed hearing you mouthing the usual platitudes of peace and friendship regarding an implacable foe like the Romulans. But, I live in hope that one day you'll come to see this universe for what it truly is, rather than what you'd wish it to be.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well, I shall endeavor to become more cynical with each passing day, look gift horses squarely in the mouth and find clouds in every silver lining.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: If only you meant it.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Lights.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sloan.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Hello, Doctor. It's good to see you. I hope you're well rested. Section Thirty one has an assignment for you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You're taking quite a risk. I could have a security team here in thirty seconds.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I suspect you'd be unable to communicate with anyone outside this room.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I could scream for help.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Possible, but uncharacteristic. Screaming for help, that's too undignified for you. But don't let me stop you. I enjoy being wrong.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What do you want?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I told you. You have an assignment.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I don't work for you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You passed the test. You were accepted into the organization.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I didn't ask to be accepted.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You were, nevertheless. And now it's time to go to work.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm sure you're dying to know what your mission is, but you won't give me the satisfaction of admitting it. So, I'll just tell you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Lucky me.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Section Thirty one is extremely interested in this conference of yours. However, the Tal'Shiar will be handling the security arrangements, so we have virtually no chance of using any technical assets to gather intelligence. As a result, we'll be forced to rely on organic assets, like you. Your mission is to gather data on the Romulan leadership. In essence, we want you to take the pulse of their government. No pun intended.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You want me to spy on an ally.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: To evaluate an ally. And a temporary ally at that. I say that because when the war is over, the following will happen in short order. The Dominion will be forced back to the Gamma Quadrant, the Cardassian Empire will be occupied, the Klingon Empire will spend the next ten years recovering from the war and won't pose a serious threat to anyone. That leaves two powers to vie for control of the quadrant, the Federation and the Romulans.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: This war isn't over and you're already planning for the next.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well put. I hope your report is equally succinct.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: How many times do I have to tell you, Sloan? I don't work for you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You will. It's in your nature. You are a man who loves secrets. Medical, personal, fictional. I am a man of secrets. You want to know what I know, and the only way to do that is to accept the assignment.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Whoa! Easy, Julian! What's going on?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Odo's checked all the security logs. There's no indication of how Sloan got aboard or where he went.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Can't say I'm surprised. From what we've seen of them, Section Thirty one is very meticulous in covering their tracks. I had a conversation with Admiral Ross this afternoon. He and I both agree that the Romulan conference is too important to cancel.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What about me?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Starfleet Command has promised to send the expert on Dominion biogenic weapons and Ketracel white to the conference. Since that's you, you go. And we want you to carry out your assignment. Make a few discreet observations on the Romulan leadership and then wait for Sloan to contact you again.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Somehow, I don't think giving Sloan any information is a good idea.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: That was my instinct as well, but after talking to Ross I think we might have an opportunity here we can turn to our advantage. Officially, Starfleet Command has said that they are appalled at the very notion that an organization like Section Thirty one might exist, and that they plan to get to the bottom of this entire business.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: And unofficially?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: They have quietly pushed the investigation aside, which means either they don't take Section Thirty one seriously or someone at Starfleet Command is protecting them. Either way, we now have a chance to get someone inside and I think I want to take it.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: So you want me to play along, pretend that I've decided to work for Sloan after all?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Exactly. When he contacts you to find out what you learned at the conference, make it seem like you've reluctantly come around to his way of thinking. Let him believe that he has seduced you into helping him.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: That shouldn't be too difficult. Sloan thinks I'm already so tempted that I can barely can see straight. Well, listen, I'd better packed. The Bellerophon leaves in three hours.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: One more thing, Doctor. Remember this isn't a game. Section Thirty one is very dangerous. If Sloan suspects that you are really working for us.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I understand.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Good hunting.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: A glass of Romulan ale, Doctor?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Thank you, Senator.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: The trading embargo has been officially lifted, if you were wondering.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It hadn't crossed my mind, actually.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: To one of the many benefits of the Alliance.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Need a medical team, sir?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: No, thank you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Don't tell me this is your first glass of Romulan ale.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well, it was illegal.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: That never stopped most of your colleagues.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I know. I was probably one of the few officers in the fleet who didn't indulge occasionally.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Would you like something else?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: No, no, I'll manage.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: That's the spirit, sir. Never say die.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What an odd expression. What does it mean?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It's a line from an old Earth poem. Forgive me for interrupting. I couldn't help overhearing and etymology is one of my hobbies. The phrase 'never say die' is originally from a nineteenth century poem based on Shakespeare's 'Merchant of Venice.' Now, it's since passed into the vernacular as an exhortation never to give up, no matter the cost.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Interesting.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Wendell Greer, Assistant Director, UFP Department of Cartography.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It's a pleasure. Admiral William Ross. Senator Cretak.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Admiral. Senator.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: And Doctor Julian Bashir.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Ah. The physician from Deep Space Nine. I was hoping to meet you. I have so many questions about the Bajoran sector, the navigational anomalies, the transport patterns. Could you spare a moment? Unless I'm interrupting?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Not at all.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Try to play your cards a little closer to your vest, Doctor. You're lucky they didn't see that look of shock on your face.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: If you've managed to attach yourself to this delegation, why do you need me?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: All in due time. Now you have a lot of work do before we arrive at Romulus. There's a PADD in your quarters. Read it. I'll join you at twenty two hundred.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well, Mister Greer certainly has his ducks in a row. According to the Department of Cartography, he's been a low level bureaucrat for almost fifteen years.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: That doesn't surprise me he has a solid cover story, sir. But I think it's too dangerous to allow him to participate in the conference or even set foot on Romulus. We don't know what he's up to.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: On the other hand, if we move against him now, we lose any hope of penetrating Section Thirty one. His access at this conference will be limited to a few low level briefings and seminars. It shouldn't be hard keeping tabs on him. If Sloan's here it suggests more important than a simple intelligence gathering mission. He's up to something and it's imperative that we know what that something is. We go forward.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Next.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Neral. Formerly Proconsul and now Praetor of the Romulan Star Empire. Neral's ascension to the top post was confirmed by the Continuing Committee a little over a year ago. His immediate family was killed in a Klingon raid approximately twenty five years ago. His interests include sociology and archeology. His favorite food is Delvan pudding and his pet set'leth's name is Pensho.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Very good. Total recall is a useful attribute for an operative. (Next, the familiar sneering features of John Fleck.)

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Koval. Chairman of the Tal'Shiar. Section Thirty one believes that he was involved in the death of Vice Admiral Fujisaki last year, but there's no proof.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: The proof is buried somewhere in Koval's personal database, which puts it out of our reach for now. But believe me, Doctor, the Deputy Chief of Starfleet Intelligence doesn't just die of food poisoning. I have to give him credit though. It was a textbook operation. No sign of foul play, and certainly no sign of Romulan involvement. It was very tidy. Koval's political status?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Ambiguous. He hasn't been elevated to the Continuing Committee, which is usually a given for the head of the Tal'Shiar. His nomination's probably being held up because of his opposition to the Federation Alliance, which is supported by the majority on the Committee.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Which, in turn, opens the door for your friend, Senator Cretak. She's an advocate of the alliance and she's been lobbying for this open seat. There is another rumor about Koval which is not contained in his file. We've heard he's ill. Something called Tuvan Syndrome.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm familiar with it. It's a neurological disease which affects mainly Romulans, Vulcans and Rigelians. It's degenerative and incurable at present.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: If Koval is ill, he'll try to hide it. It's a weakness, and one that could hamper his chances of being appointed to the Committee.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Is that what I'm here for? A diagnosis? What's the matter Sloan, doesn't Section Thirty one have its own doctors?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Our physicians weren't genetically enhanced. They need equipment to make a diagnosis. Equipment that the Romulans won't permit at this conference.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm incapable of making a diagnosis by simply looking at a man.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Your genetically enhanced friends determined that Gul Damar killed a woman just by watching him give a political speech. I'm sure you can do better than that.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You're going to make a move against Koval, aren't you? You're going to find a way to use his illness to keep him off the Committee. I suppose it would be naive of me to point out that interfering in the internal affairs of a sovereign power is explicitly forbidden by the Federation charter.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Without confirming or denying your speculation, I will say that if Koval comes to power, it'll be a disaster for the Federation. He'll argue for the Romulans to abrogate the alliance and negotiate a separate peace with the Dominion. And I don't think I need to tell you what that would do to the course of the war.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You can't justify that by manipulating a

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Let's make a deal, doctor. I'll spare you the ends justify the means speech and you spare me the we must do what's right speech. You and I are not going to see eye to eye on this subject, so I suggest we stop discussing it. Our mission is reconnaissance. You're not going to be called upon to do anything other than that. Now why don't you get some rest. We'll be in orbit of Romulus by oh six hundred and you will need to have your wits about you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Here you are sir.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Doctor Julian Bashir?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Yes.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I understand you were the officer who first identified the biogenic weapon known as the Quickening.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: That's right. On Boranis Three, in the Gamma Quadrant. I don't believe we've been introduced.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Koval.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Ah. It's a pleasure to meet you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Why?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well, you've got me there. It's just a simple form of expression, I suppose.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: And like most human expressions, completely devoid of meaning. Can the Dominion's Quickening virus be replicated?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: We've had a little difficulty in recreating the exact RNA sequence of the virus, which why we've been unable to develop a vaccine. However, there are alternate methods of making vaccines which

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm not interested in the vaccine, I'm interested in the virus. Do you know how to introduce the Quickening into a population?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Basically.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Good. I look forward to hearing your lecture.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You're going to make a very fine operative, Doctor.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I beg your pardon?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: The Chairman of the Tal'Shiar rarely speaks with anyone in public, much less someone wearing that uniform. Starfleet Intelligence should recruit you immediately.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What makes you think I'm not working for them already?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Somehow, it wouldn't surprise me if half the people in this room turned out to be operatives.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You are joking?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It may be impolitic to say this, but there are those who believe the alliance is merely a momentary truce.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Are you one of them?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I could ask you the same thing.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well in my case it's a firm no. But you've answered my question with a question.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I try not to predict the future.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What about Chairman Koval?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You tell me. You just spoke with him. That's more than I've done in six months.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I take it you two don't get along?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: We have different views.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Which are?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: State secrets.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Naturally.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: This is an adult female inhabitant of Boranis Three. The markings on the face are typical of a humanoid who's been infected by the disease, but who has not yet entered the terminal stage.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: In this next photograph, you can tell by the necrotic nature of the lesions the patient has indeed entered the terminal stage of the disease. This is also marked by an increase in leukocyte production.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Thank you, Doctor.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Excellent.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Thank you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Very enlightening. You almost made it comprehensible.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Next time I'll do the lecture with hand puppets just for you.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Thank you very much.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm glad to see you still have your sense of humor. I trust you noticed who was sitting in the front row.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Yes. He came to see me this morning between sessions. He wanted to know more about the Quickening. Specifically, if I knew how to replicate the virus and how to introduce it into a population.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What did you think of his health?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Didn't you hear what I just said?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I heard you. Koval wants to get his hands on the Quickening. That's not news to me that the head of the Tal'Shiar is interested in biogenic weapons. Pull your head out of the sand, and take a look around, Doctor. These are not nice people we're dealing with here. Now answer my question.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: His eyelids were slightly displaced. He had a noticeable weakness in the facial muscles, possibly the result of compromised neuromuscular function. And his respiration was somewhat irregular.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Bottom line?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: He may have Tuvan Syndrome, but if he does, it's in the very early stages.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: How long does he have?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: If his case fits the profile, he will start experiencing a loss of motor skills in ten to fifteen years, with a life expectancy in the twenty to twenty five year range.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Are there any instances in which the disease accelerates without warning?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It happens, but in less than five percent of the cases.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Is there anything that could trigger the acceleration?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You know, I don't know what you're asking me.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Never mind. Thank you, Doctor. You've been very helpful.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: This is unbelievable. Let's put aside for the moment that he's contemplating the murder of a high ranking official. What in the hell makes him think that the next head of the Tal'Shiar would be any better than Koval?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sloan's more concerned with who gets the empty seat on the Continuing Committee. He's hoping that Cretak gets that.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I sort of agree with him there. Cretak, for all her abrasiveness, is at least a patriot.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What makes her any different from Koval?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: If you saw the reports from Starfleet Intelligence that I see, you would never ask that question. Koval would like nothing better than to see the Romulan banner waving over Earth. Believe me, Doctor. Chairman Koval is not someone we want at the Praetor's right hand. I'll have Sloan confined to his quarters immediately, but that may not solve our problem.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sir?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Has it occurred to you that you and Sloan may not be the only ones here working for Section Thirty one? For all we know, he has a confederate somewhere in the delegation.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sloan did say that our mission would be strictly reconnaissance and that we wouldn't be called upon to do anything else. That could suggest another operative. Someone whose mission isn't limited to reconnaissance.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: If that's true, it could be anyone. Even a member of the Bellerophon crew.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Or a Romulan.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sir, I believe Sloan has an accomplice here, on Romulus.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What makes you say that?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Two things. First, Sloan has too much information on the inner workings of their government, too many insights into their political process. Second, Sloan's plan is to kill Koval while making it appear to be an accelerated case of Tuvan Syndrome. Now the only way to do that would be to expose Koval to a short burst of nadion radiation. The simplest plan would be to maneuver him near a phaser relay and surreptitiously irradiate him. Now since I doubt very much that Sloan is going to have a chance to do that, it stands to reason someone else is going to have to.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: A Romulan.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Exactly. Sir, Sloan may have already got things underway. We have to warn them.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: And how am I supposed to explain Section Thirty one to the Romulans? All hell would break loose if they hear that there's a rogue Federation agency is running around plotting assassinations. It could bring the Alliance down. Besides, all we have is speculation at this point.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Admiral

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: The answer is no. After I have Sloan arrested, I'll break radio silence and inform Starfleet Command of the situation. Your orders are to sit tight and do nothing until you hear from me.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Aye, sir.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I don't know. Jepella said she went in to deliver a report and found him slumped over his desk.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Do they have any idea what happened?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Doctor Frame said it looked like an aneurysm, but they're still running tests.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: An aneurysm. I saw the Admiral this morning. He looked fine.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: They say that's the way it happens.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Which admiral are you talking about?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Admiral Ross, sir. He collapsed at his desk.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Where is he?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sickbay.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Hey.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I can't trust anyone aboard the Bellerophon and I can't contact DS Nine. For security reasons there's been a communications blackout. Senator, I have no one else to turn to. I need your help.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: To do what?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I have reason to believe that Sloan has an accomplice within the Romulan government. Someone who's going to help him carry out this assassination.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Koval has been saying that there's a traitor in the Senate, someone working for Starfleet Intelligence

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Section Thirty one isn't part of Starfleet Intelligence.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: They are Federation citizens working to advance your interests. That makes them your responsibility.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You're absolutely right. That's why I'm doing everything I can to stop them. I'm trying to convince Sloan that Koval doesn't have Tuvan Syndrome. But he may have already asked his accomplice to proceed. So if we want to be sure to stop this assassination we have to find Sloan's Romulan accomplice.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: And you expect me to find this traitor?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sloan said something about Koval having a personal database. It stands to reason that it contains a list of potential suspects. Is there any possible way you can get me a copy of this database so that I can run an analysis of

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You are asking me to hand over secret documents!

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm asking you to put aside three centuries of mistrust between our peoples and help me stop a murder. Senator, if we can't reach out and bridge the gulf that is between us, if we can't trust each other, a man will die and we will be partially responsible. I need your help. Please.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You wanted to see me, Doctor?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Yes. I'm not convinced that Koval is suffering from Tuvan Syndrome. His symptoms could be the result of any number of different health problems.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You didn't say that before.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'm not an expert on Romulan physiology. Most of my knowledge of Tuvan Syndrome comes from studies done on Vulcan patients.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I thought Vulcans and Romulans were virtually identical.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Yes, but there are some important genetic differences. And the more I study the available data on Romulan physiology, the less sure I am that my diagnosis was correct.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: How could you find out for sure?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: The best way would be to do an examination, but I hardly think he'll agree to that.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What if you obtained a sample of his skin cells? Could you run an analysis?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Probably. But how do you propose

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: We'll treat your palm with a microcellular adhesive. The next time you shake his hand, you'll get your sample.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: All right.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Mister Chairman? What a pleasure to see you again.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I'd be happy to resume our discussion on the Quickening before this conference is adjourned.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I believe you answered all my questions, Doctor.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Well then, I'm glad to have been able to help.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Doctor. I would like to have a word with you on another matter, in private.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Of course. I believe the lecture hall is empty.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: We have other more comfortable facilities available. If you please.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sit down. I can assure you that you will be sitting in that chair one way or the other, Doctor.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Now we'll have our private talk.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What shall we talk about?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Why you're really on Romulus, who you're working for and, of course, who's helping you. Don't worry. I won't waste your time with pointless questions.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: This can be painful or not. That's up to you, Doctor. Either way, I will know what you know.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It appears that your brain's neurocellular structure is not susceptible to our scanning techniques, evidently a result of the genetic enhancements made to your parietal cortex.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Sorry.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I do have other methods at my disposal, but it would save everyone a great deal of trouble if you would simply tell me what I want to know.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: You haven't asked me any questions yet.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I think you know what I'm interested in. Who are you working for? Why are you here? Bring him.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Doctor Julian Bashir, you are appearing before the Continuing Committee of the Romulan People. Any statements will be made part of the official record. Senator Cretak is charged with attempting to access a Tal'Shiar database without proper authorisation. The Senator has told the Committee a remarkable story. Since you're a key figure in her story, we are most eager to hear your version of the events.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: What I am about to say may be shocking. It may even damage the relations between our two peoples, but it's the truth. A few days ago, I became aware of a plot to assassinate Chairman Koval. It was conceived of by a man known to me only as Sloan. He works for an organization called Section Thirty one. They see themselves as protecting the interests of the Federation, although they have absolutely no official standing. Once I realized what Sloan was attempting to do, I contacted Senator Cretak in order to enlist her aid in stopping him.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Why her?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I had no one else to turn to. I was unable to contact Deep Space Nine and I couldn't trust anyone aboard the Bellerophon.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: But you felt that you could trust a Romulan Senator?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Yes. For all our differences, I do respect her.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Continue.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: For reasons that are extremely complicated, I came to believe that there's a traitor in your government working for Section Thirty one. I asked the Senator to obtain the database so that we could expose this person and prevent the assassination.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Senator Cretak, why didn't you come to me with this information?

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: I was afraid that if word of this plot got out, it would destroy the Alliance. I decided to keep my own counsel. I regret that decision.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: As well you should, Kimara.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: It's an interesting story. But it's not the whole story. if I may be permitted to bring in another witness? Bring in prisoner five two seven.

title: Inter Arma Enim Silent Leges
line: Praetor, this is the man known as Sloan. Unlike the Doctor, his mind is quite susceptible to our data retrieval methods. Under questioning, he has confirmed much of what the Doctor and the Senator have told you, with one important exception. There is no Section Thirty one. Sloan, in fact, works for Starfleet Intelligence. Far from being the master of a rogue agency, he is simply one of many operatives in the employ of the Federation. He's had a long career, most of which is still unknown to us. However, there is one interesting element that we do know. He was the protégé of the late Vice Admiral Fujisaki. Sloan did not take the death of his mentor well. He came to believe he was murdered by the Tal'Shiar. In his eyes, the assassination of a Starfleet admiral was stepping over the line. Isn't that the phrase? After Fujisaki's death, he was confronted with a dilemma. How could he seek vengeance without violating the Federation laws? His answer was to invent Section Thirty one, a rogue organization that answered to no one. If they killed the head of the Tal'Shiar, Starfleet Intelligence would be held blameless. As the Committee knows, I have been diagnosed with Tuvan Syndrome. Sloan became aware of my condition and hoped to make my death look like a sudden acceleration of the disease. To do that, he needed a doctor. Sloan arranged to recruit Doctor Bashir into Section Thirty one. After that, Sloan bided his time, and waited for an opportunity to present itself. He found one when he learned of this conference. He then arranged for Bashir to be invited. Everything was going perfectly, but then he made a fatal mistake. He decided to come to Romulus himself. He was unaware that his identity had become known to us. Once we recognized him in the delegation, we knew immediately that an intelligence operation was underway. What I don't understand is why? Why did you come here and take the risk of being discovered?

line: It is the finding of this Committee that Senator Cretak has conspired to commit treason against the State. Sentence to be determined at a later date. Doctor Bashir will be returned to the Bellerophon. Mister Sloan is remanded to the custody of the Tal'Shiar for further interrogation.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Oh, you'll have to do something about him long before that, Commander.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Thanks for all your help.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: You seemed to have things well under control.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Did I?

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Despite his statement to the contrary, Rusot will not wait until the end of the war to make his move. I suggest you don't wait either. Kill him before he kills you.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Challenge Gowron? In the middle of a war? It's treasonous.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Gowron is leading us all to ruin. It is your duty to challenge him to protect the Empire.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: You would have me protect the Empire by breaking my oath, by spilling the blood of a Klingon brother while an enemy stands at our door? Where is the honor in that?

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: He is sacrificing our troops for his own petty reasons. Where is the honor in that?

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: The troops are his to command. It is not our place to question him unless he acts with cowardice and there is no proof of that.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: You are not listening.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: I've heard every word that you have said. You want me to become Chancellor. Me. Tell me Worf, how do you think the members of the High Council will react when they're asked to follow a common man from the Ketha Lowlands? A man without a drop of noble blood in his veins?

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Kahless himself was not high-born.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Kahless was divine.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Your name is revered throughout the Empire. If you seize the leadership, every warrior from here to Kronos would swear an oath to you. And with that kind of support, the High Council will have no choice but to accept you as Chancellor.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: You begin to sound like a Romulan.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: You know I am right.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: I am a loyal soldier of the Empire. I would rather die than dishonor my uniform by raising a hand to my Chancellor in a time of war. I would bring shame to everything that I've fought to protect, everything that I believe in.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: General.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: My decision is made. We will not speak of this again.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: You're staring again.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Sorry. I'm just worried about you.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Well don't. It may be a long time before the first symptoms manifest themselves, and by then I'm sure Doctor Bashir will have found the cure.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Right. Could you take the helm? I'm going to get a raktajino.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: What's wrong?

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: One of our listening posts picked up a message. The Dominion has succeeded in locating Damar's family.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: They're dead. They weren't a part of this rebellion. The Dominion knew that, the Founder knew that. Weyoun knew that. To kill her and my son. The casual brutality of it. A waste of life. What kind of state tolerates the murder of innocent women and children? What kind of people give those orders?

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Yeah, Damar, what kind of people give those orders?

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Oh, that was stupid.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Not at all. Damar has a certain romanticism about the past. He could use a dose of cold water.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: I could have picked a better time.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: If he's the man to lead a new Cardassia, if he's the man we hope him to be, then the pain of this news made him more receptive to what you said, not less.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: We're approaching the rendezvous point.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: The shuttle is here.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Right on time. Just as I promised.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Damar to shuttle. Lower your shields and we'll beam aboard.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Acknowledged.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Let's go.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: And in truth, I understand his position. It is the duty of every soldier to support their leaders in time of war. Asking Martok to stand against Gowron was a foolish error.

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Try to convince Gowron to discontinue these attacks. You have said very little.

line: You are still a member of the House of Martok.

line: This is the first that I've heard of it.

line: The General and I talked about it weeks ago. He likes you. And he considers you an honorable woman, a worthy successor to Jadzia, and so do I.

line: Don't get me wrong, I'm very touched that you still consider me to be a member of the House of Martok, but I tend to look at the Empire with a little more skepticism than Curzon or Jadzia did. We're talking about a warrior culture that prides itself on maintaining centuries old traditions of honor and integrity, but in reality it's willing to accept corruption at the highest levels.

line: You are overstating your case.

line: Am I? Who was the last leader of the High Council that you respected? Has there even been one? And how many times have you had to cover up the crimes of Klingon leaders because you were told it was for the good of the Empire? I know this sounds harsh, but the truth is, you have been willing to accept a government that you know is corrupt. Gowron's just the latest example. Worf, you are the most honorable and decent man I've ever met, and if you're willing to tolerate men like Gowron, then what hope is there for the Empire?

title: Tacking Into The Wind

title: Tacking Into The Wind
line: Hail, Martok! Leader of the Empire! Leader of destiny.

line: You're still a Cardassian, Garak. You're not going to kill one of your own people for a Bajoran woman.

title: Tacking Into The Wind

line: You want her dead too, Damar. I know you do. But you're the leader of the rebellion and don't want to kill someone wearing a Starfleet uniform. Let me do it for you.

line: Damar, shoot him. We can kill them both and keep the Breen weapon for ourselves. I believe in you, Damar. I know you're the right man to restore the Empire we loyally served. The Empire we loved. Together we can lead our people to greatness again. Just aim and fire.
